cards.name: EPA AirNow
cards.summary: The U.S. EPA's AirNow program serves real-time Air Quality Index readings (NowCast AQI) and agency-issued AQI forecasts from more than 2,500 monitoring stations run by over 150 local, state, tribal, provincial and federal agencies across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Keyless hourly files (reportingarea.dat by reporting area, HourlyAQObs and HourlyData by monitoring site) download from files.airnowtech.org; the AirNow API web services (by ZIP, lat/long, reporting area or bounding box) need a free account and key. The data are preliminary and unvalidated.
cards.short: The EPA's official real-time Air Quality Index for the US, Canada and Mexico; hourly, free, keyless files.

tasks: current NowCast AQI per pollutant for a reporting area (the peak across the area's monitors), by ZIP code, lat/long or reporting area code
AQI forecasts by reporting area, ZIP or lat/long (where agencies issue them)
hourly observations by monitoring site: AQI for ozone, PM2.5, PM10 and NO2, and concentrations incl. CO and SO2 (keyless HourlyAQObs/HourlyData files, or the keyed bounding-box service)
PM2.5, ozone and combined AQI contour maps (KML) for a bounding box
action-day flags and forecast discussions from air agencies

pricing.notes: Free. The file products on files.airnowtech.org download without a key; the web services need a free AirNow API account and key.

latency.typical: Observations for the previous hour are generally available 10-30 minutes past the hour; reportingarea.dat is updated twice per hour at :25 and :55
latency.notes: AirNow FAQ: observations update once per hour and forecasts are issued once per day. On 2026-10-27 04:59 UTC the keyless reportingarea.dat (last modified 04:42 UTC) held observations for 00:00 EDT (04:00 UTC), and HourlyData for 03:00 UTC was last modified 04:54 UTC.

coverage.notes: AirNow covers the United States, Canada and Mexico. AQI by reporting area (reportingarea.dat and the ZIP/lat-long services) is for US reporting areas plus Mexicali; Canadian and most Mexican data appear as monitoring sites in the hourly site files. Reporting areas range from part of a city to a whole county, and the lat/long and ZIP services return the reporting area's peak value, not the nearest monitor. Forecasts are not issued for every area, every day or every season.

licensing.summary: EPA AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines (PDF, Aug 2025) (account sign-up also requires agreeing to a Data Use Agreement): the data are preliminary, not fully verified or validated, and must not be used for regulation, trends, guidance or other government or public decision-making (official data come from EPA's AQS). The federal, state, local and tribal agencies own the data. Users must credit those agencies and EPA AirNow, disseminate values and advisories unaltered, use the AQI colours, label displays and products as preliminary, tell the agencies and EPA AirNow when products rely on the data, and keep their contact details current. AI training and resale are not mentioned.

Request an account at https://docs.airnowapi.org/account/request/ (name, user name, email, phone, agency, comment, and agreement to the Data Use Agreement and Data Use Guidelines), activate it with the emailed confirmation code, then copy the key from the top right of the Web Services page; it is passed as the API_KEY query parameter.

cards.name: ALERTCalifornia cameras (UC San Diego)
cards.short: 1,289 wildfire-watch PTZ cameras across California; latest frame about every 15 s, no key.
cards.summary: UC San Diego's statewide network of high-definition pan-tilt-zoom wildfire cameras with near-infrared night vision, aimed by trained first responders. A public ArcGIS feature service lists every camera with location, online status, current pan/tilt/zoom and a latest-frame image URL. Free for non-commercial use under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

tasks: current still from a fixed-site PTZ camera
visual check for smoke, fire, snow, weather or visibility in California wildlands
night view via near-infrared
find cameras by county, radius or bounding box

pricing.notes: Free for non-commercial use with credit. For-profit (commercial) use needs a commercial licence negotiated with UC San Diego's OIC 'with appropriate licensing fees'; no price published.

latency.typical: seconds to minutes
latency.notes: Provider: camera images update approximately every 15 seconds; camera direction and viewsheds update every two minutes, and images may run ahead of the orientation fields. Sampled 2026-10-26 ~22:01 PDT: latest-frame redirected to JPEGs 24 s and 31 s old; layer max viewTime ~2.5 min old, but some rows' viewTime lag ~24 h even when the frame is seconds old.

coverage.notes: 1,289 cameras in the feed, 1,252 online at ~22:01 PDT on 2026-10-26 (1,251 on 2026-10-27); all within California (feed extent 32.59 to 41.93 N). Ridgetop/backcountry sites that can see up to 60 miles by day and 120 miles on a clear night; not street cameras. Operators move the PTZ view and cameras sweep 360 degrees about every two minutes, so the field of view changes. Some mountaintop cameras go offline in winter ('winter mode'). Check isOnline and viewTime per camera: one feed row had a viewTime of 2026-10-25, so some cameras are stale.

licensing.summary: ALERTCalifornia program data is copyrighted by UC San Diego (Regents of the University of California) and licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: non-commercial use with credit 'ALERTCalifornia | UC San Diego', no derivatives; do not crop the information bar or partner logos on screen grabs. For-profit use must contact OIC to negotiate a commercial licence with fees. The terms have no explicit resale clause: "forbidden" is inferred from CC BY-NC-ND (no commercial use, no derivatives). AI or ML training is not named; NC and ND make it risky. automation_allowed true only means no ban on automated access; use stays non-commercial.

human.unknown: Capture is automatic. Cameras are aimed by trained first responders and emergency managers, but who aimed a given frame is not exposed.

application.unknown: No capture-app or device attestation is published; frames carry ordinary EXIF (make, model, firmware) that is not signed.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Fixed Axis PTZ cameras operated by UC San Diego; the acquisition engine pulls images from the physical cameras over Axis VAPIX. A sampled frame's EXIF reads AXIS Q6075-E, 1920x1080. No per-image sensor proof: EXIF is unsigned, the sampled JPEG had no C2PA manifest, and Axis is not on the C2PA conforming products list.

time.method: Capture timestamp in the redirected object path, in the x-amz-meta-context timestamp and in EXIF DateTime; per-camera viewTime field in the feed.
time.unknown: Not signed or time-stamped by a third party; the layer's viewTime can lag the image by hours.

cards.name: Capella Space
cards.summary: Operator of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through cloud and at night. Its Console and REST API let you task a new point or area capture in a UTC window, choose a collection tier (urgent, priority, standard, flexible), set up repeat tasking down to a 24-hour cycle, review a cost estimate before approving, track status, and download the delivered collect. Capella advertises 0.25 m resolution and 93% of collects delivered in under 3 hours. Access is by signed order form, invoiced in USD.

collection tiers urgent, priority, standard and flexible (repeat requests: routine or flexible)
repeat tasking of a point every N days (minimum cycle 24 hours), until a count, an end date, or cancelled
retask an earlier request, an existing archive collect, or a repeat series
imaging geometry constraints: look direction, ascending/descending, orbital plane (45, 53, 97), off-nadir, azimuth, grazing angle, squint, day/night or custom local time
cost estimate and approve/reject before scheduling (or pre-approve)
status tracking (received, review, submitted, active, accepted, completed, rejected, expired, and others) and signed-URL download of the delivered product

pricing.model: cost estimate per tasking request, approved before scheduling; fees invoiced
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. No public price list was found. Each tasking request returns a cost estimate (order.summary.total; repeat requests: costPerImageEstimate) for approval. Fees are payable in US dollars, invoiced monthly in arrears and due net 30; payments are non-cancelable and non-refundable; cancelling an accepted order incurs the cancellation fees in Capella's Product Guide.

latency.typical: 93% of collects delivered in under 3 hours (provider claim)
latency.notes: Homepage: '93% Data Collects Delivered in Under 3 Hours', '15-minute scheduling cycles', '2-15 Revisit Opportunities Per Day'. Capture happens inside the window you set (windowOpen/windowClose); the docs give no minimum lead time, and the standard tier has a minimum window duration whose value isn't stated. The Standard Terms say any delivery date is an estimate only.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes and scheduling)
coverage.notes: Homepage: '24/7 global coverage'. SAR works through cloud and at night. Acceptance depends on the scheduler: requests can be rejected (e.g. conflicting tasks), expire, or stay 'active' without a guarantee of full collection until 'accepted'. Accounts are not available to persons barred from receiving services under US law.

licensing.summary: Tasked data is licensed, not sold, under Capella's License Agreement (EULA v2.1, May 2026): a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence for the customer's Internal Use, including derivatives for Internal Use, plus an express right to 'use Data to train Models that Customer uses to provide services or deliverables to Third Parties' (Models must not contain or enable reconstruction of the raw Data). Selling, distributing, sublicensing or making Data or Derivatives publicly available is prohibited unless authorised; Capella keeps title to the Data and to Derivatives made by or for Capella; the customer owns its Models and its own contributions (Sec. 11). Bulk download or scraping is barred (EULA 9(m); website ToS Sec. 3 and 12). Use across more than one organisation needs Capella Legal. Console/API evaluation accounts are internal, non-commercial only. U.S. Government licences come via the NRO. Separate open-data collections are CC BY 4.0 / CC BY 2.0 (context only).

Keys are shown once and are valid for 90 days from creation or last use; unused keys are deleted.
The docs show 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' as an alternative to ApiKey (e.g. on POST /keys) but do not say how to obtain a token.

cards.name: Copernicus Sentinel (Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem)
cards.short: Free EU Sentinel radar and optical satellite imagery, usually online 1-4 hours after each pass.
cards.summary: The EU's Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem serves new Sentinel-1 (C-band radar, works day and night through cloud), Sentinel-2 (13-band optical, 10 m resolution) and other Sentinel products free, via STAC, OData, S3, Sentinel Hub and openEO, with PUSH/PULL catalogue subscriptions and a public Traceability service whose traces carry signed product hashes.

tasks: find the newest Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 product over a place (STAC or OData search, keyless)
subscribe to new products matching an area and filter (PUSH or PULL, account needed)
download full products (token) or render a cropped image or index via the Sentinel Hub Process API
check a product's BLAKE3 hash against its signed Traceability trace

pricing.notes: Free for Copernicus General Users: 12 TB download per rolling 30 days (then slowed to 1 MB/s and 1 connection, not cut off), 4 concurrent connections; Sentinel Hub 10,000 requests and 10,000 processing units per month.

latency.typical: about 1 h (Sentinel-1 GRD) to about 3.5-4 h (Sentinel-2 L2A) after sensing
latency.notes: Measured on 2026-10-26 (UTC early 27th) by keyless STAC search: a Sentinel-1C GRD COG sensed 03:49:59Z was published 04:44:50Z (55 min); a Sentinel-2C L2A tile sensed 00:58:11Z was published 04:32-04:34Z (about 3 h 35 min). The Sentinel-1 mission page says marine monitoring services need data 'typically in less than 3 hours'. The next pass depends on orbit; there is no tasking.

coverage.notes: No country limit. Sentinel-2 systematically covers land between 56° S and 82.8° N, coastal waters to 20 km, islands over 100 km² and closed seas, not open ocean. Sentinel-1 follows its observation scenario; revisit depends on orbit and there is no tasking.

licensing.summary: Sentinel Data Legal Notice (EU law): free, full and open access; reproduction, distribution, communication to the public, and adaptation, modification and combination are permitted 'in so far as it is lawful'; credit 'Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]' (or 'Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data [Year]'). No warranty; rare limits for security, third-party rights or service disruption. Other portal content is non-commercial only, and the Terms say "ESA and T-Systems do not grant the right to resell or redistribute any information, documents, images or material" (portal-content context, not the Sentinel Legal Notice). Neither AI training nor resale is named, so both stay unstated.

human.unknown: No people capture the data; satellites operated for the EU by ESA.

application.unknown: No device or app attestation applies; satellites are operated for the EU by ESA. The signed Traceability record is a custody record, not attestation, and is listed under provenance.custody (STANDARD §3, 3.1).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Mission, satellite and instrument (MSI optical, C-SAR radar) are named in the product name and metadata. Instrument identity rests on product metadata; nothing signs it at the sensor.

time.method: Sensing start and end times in product name and metadata
time.unknown: Sensing time is in product metadata; not independently attested. The trace timestamp shows only when CDSE registered the product.

location.method: Footprint geometry and orbit in product metadata
location.unknown: Geolocation comes from product metadata and orbit data; not independently attested.

content.unknown: No manipulation detection. Integrity since CDSE registered the product can be checked against the signed Traceability record (provenance.custody), but that is not a capture-time seal: there is no C2PA hard binding.

corroboration.unknown: Not cross-checked by a third party.

custody.method: CDSE's public Traceability service keeps a trace per product: the event (CREATE at registration), a BLAKE3 hash of the product (per-file hashes on most products), the holder (origin cdse_csc@dataspace.copernicus.eu) and the time, signed RSA-SHA256 with an X.509 certificate for trace.dataspace.copernicus.eu. Anyone can fetch the trace without a login, re-hash a download and compare.
custody.unknown: One documented hop (ground segment registration to you), signed by CDSE itself, not an independent party; it shows the bytes match what CDSE registered, not what the sensor saw. The sampled trace is timestamped 2024-06-19 but its signing certificate (GeoTrust TLS RSA CA G1) was valid only 2023-05-16 to 2024-05-15, so a strict X.509 check at signing time fails; the hashes can still be recomputed. Whether the list of traces is append-only is not documented, and some traces carry only the product hash. Kept at claimed: the trace is signed by the operator itself and the sample's signing certificate had expired before the trace date, so a strict public check fails.

sources.claim: Traceability: signed traces of a product's lifecycle events let users verify authenticity and integrity
Sample trace: CREATE event, BLAKE3 product and file hashes, signature block (certificate expired 2024-05-15, trace 2024-06-19)

cards.name: Defined.ai
cards.summary: AI training-data company (formerly DefinedCrowd) that, besides its dataset marketplace, runs custom collections with a vetted global crowd through its Neevo platform: images (everyday objects, facial expressions, gestures), video (egocentric POV, action sequences, behavioural clips), speech recordings, and wearable sensor data for robotics. Collections are scoped to demographic, language and compliance requirements. Sales-led and quote-only; an enterprise REST API (OAuth2 client credentials) lets account holders clone project templates, upload prompts, track status and download deliverables.

pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. No prices for custom collection; volume discounts by quotation. Marketplace payments are USD by ACH bank transfer, with purchase orders and SOWs on request; no refunds.

latency.notes: The data-collection page says datasets are 'delivered quickly and competitively' with no timeline; the FAQ says custom orders take longer than marketplace purchases. One robotics case study reports 225 hours of sensor data collected in two weeks within a two-month timeframe.

coverage.notes: Defined.ai cites 1.6M+ contributors in 150+ countries (also '150+ markets') and 500+ languages and locales across all services; how many capture images or video, and where, is not published. The public API's language list names locales, not collection countries. An in-house recording studio operates in Lisbon.

licensing.summary: The FAQ says all Defined.ai datasets are covered by its standard Data License Agreement (effective 30 Nov 2022). That licence is non-exclusive, non-sublicensable and non-transferable; §1(c) permits internal use and commercial exploitation of models trained, tested or benchmarked on the data, provided the data is not made available and the model does not output recognisable contributor content (e.g. TTS voices, avatars). §1(b)(ii) and §1(c) forbid selling, sublicensing or otherwise commercialising the data itself, and §4 says Defined.ai owns all rights in the data. The site says every dataset is 'fully consented, copyright-cleared, and privacy-compliant' (GDPR, HIPAA). Use is for internal business operations only (§1(c)), and on termination (60 days' notice, or breach) the licensee must delete or return all copies of the data (§8), despite the FAQ calling the licence perpetual. Whether a custom collection contract changes these terms, including ownership or exclusivity, is not published.

human.method: A 'vetted' crowd recruited through owned channels, ad platforms and local partners; contributors accept the terms, privacy policy and a job-specific NDA and MSA; 'rigorously trained, verified annotators'. Scripted-speech deliveries include information about the speaker.
human.unknown: Screening method and identity checks for contributors who capture images or video are not documented.

application.unknown: Collection runs through Defined.ai's Neevo platform and tools, but no check that a capture came from a genuine, unmodified app or device is documented. Scripted-speech deliveries name the recording device, without proof.

camera.unknown: No check against imported, re-captured or generated media is described.

time.unknown: No trusted capture time is documented in general. One robotics case study describes timestamped streams with global UTC time, as a project requirement, without a checkable proof.

location.unknown: No location capture or check is documented in general. One robotics case study mentions location metadata as a project requirement, with no verification described.

content.method: Multi-layer validation: automated checks plus multi-pass human review, with real-time monitoring dashboards; scripted speech is validated by multiple human annotators; the robotics case study tracked drop-frame rate and frame rate as KPIs.
content.unknown: Review criteria and error rates are not published.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of individual captures is described. ISO 27001, 27701 and 42001 certifications cover management systems, not the captured content.

cards.name: Empiric Earth (Nexar)
cards.summary: Dashcam data company formed when Nexar and Nauto merged; it has operated as Empiric Earth since 15 September 2026. About 350,000 dashcams on vehicles making ordinary journeys feed Atlas, a searchable library of curated driving video (6M+ videos) for AV, robotics and research teams, and CityStream, a continuously refreshed feed of road detections (signs, work zones, defects, surface) plus anonymized road frames for an area (VirtualCam). When a scenario is not in the archive, customers can commission targeted collection, which points the live network at that condition. Atlas and targeted collection are sold through sales. CityStream has REST APIs that need an approved account. Nothing can be ordered by API.

tasks: targeted collection of driving video for a scenario not yet in the archive (by geography, weather or driving behaviour)
edge-case and near-miss driving video for AV and robotics training and validation
fresh road detections for a bounding box: traffic signs, work zones, road defects (potholes, manholes, road plates), surface condition (CityStream Live Feed)
anonymized road frames for a bounding box or H3 cells, filtered by date, time of day, minimum quality, road type and heading (CityStream VirtualCam)
check imagery coverage for an area before requesting frames (VirtualCam coverage endpoint)
curated road-sign inventory and work-zone feed by bounding box or H3 cells (CityStream Road Inventory, Work Zones)

pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. The Atlas, CityStream and AV pages list no prices and route to an enquiry form. Data-licence agreements are separate contracts that are not published.

latency.typical: Unknown for targeted collection; CityStream refreshes as vehicles pass
latency.notes: No delivery time is published for targeted collection. CityStream says the road state 'updates continuously instead of on a survey cycle', and 'a dense urban corridor refreshes constantly; a rural road refreshes when someone drives it'. No latency figure is given. The Live Feed API returns 'real-time detections' since a caller-given epoch time. Enquiry replies: '1–2 business days' on the Atlas and CityStream pages, and 'within one business day' on the AV and contact pages. Those are reply times, not delivery times.

coverage.notes: Company figures: 350,000 active sensors, 300M+ new miles a month across 50+ countries, 10B+ miles of history, 98% of US roads reached, 80M+ objects detected daily. Before the merger, Nexar alone cited 100M+ miles a month across 94% of US roads. 'Coverage follows where vehicles actually drive', and no route is driven to produce data, so rural or low-traffic roads refresh rarely. CityStream describes a 'nationwide' (US) network and MUTCD-coded US signs. Countries outside the US are not listed. Atlas notes that 'coverage varies by geography'. Non-US countries are unnamed, so the card lists only the US.

licensing.summary: Customer licence terms are not public. The website terms say 'product, device and data-licence agreements are separate contracts', and the CityStream OpenAPI files state 'License: Proprietary'. The company says it holds and licenses the record, will not sell personal data, and does not build plate recognition, face recognition or person-level search. It says data is 'de-identified at capture', and VirtualCam returns 'anonymized frames'. The developers page lists 'training or fine-tuning on real-world driving' as a use case, but no published term grants or forbids AI training or resale. On the capture side, Nexar's consumer site says road data is blurred on the device. The same page says Nexar uses footage, including non-anonymized footage, to train its own safety AI. The website terms (s.6(e)) ban robots and automatic access to the website; the API's own terms are unpublished, so automation is not stated.

human.unknown: Footage comes from dashcams on vehicles making ordinary journeys. No driver identity check is documented, and none would be relevant to the data.

application.unknown: Captured on the provider's own dashcams, which run detection models on the device. No device or firmware attestation is published.

time.method: Each VirtualCam frame carries a capture timestamp (captured_at, with timezone offset), and each Live Feed detection carries the evidence-frame timestamp plus first- and last-recorded times (CityStream OpenAPI). Atlas attaches the date to every result.
time.unknown: How capture time is set (device clock, GPS time or server receipt) is not documented, and the timestamps are not signed.

location.method: Each frame and detection carries the camera's GPS position and heading, an H3 cell and an OpenStreetMap road segment (CityStream OpenAPI). Atlas attaches the location to every result.

content.method: Atlas: 'Every video is classified before it enters the index, and in-cabin, stationary, and low-quality footage is filtered out.' Atlas ranks results with the BADAS collision-risk model. Live Feed detections carry model confidence scores, and VirtualCam frames carry a frame-quality score.
content.unknown: Classification error rates for delivered data are not published. BADAS benchmarks are internal, and the provider labels them that way. It is not stated whether people review targeted-collection results.

corroboration.unknown: CityStream reports repeated observations of a place from Empiric's own dashcam fleet ('Every vehicle that passes a location adds an observation'). One operator and one pipeline count as one source (STANDARD §3), so this is re-observation, not independent confirmation. Empiric's /verify page covers model benchmarks only.

Each CityStream product (Live Feed, Work Zones, Road Inventory, VirtualCam) is shown only to accounts in that product's Okta group, so an approved commercial account is needed. Send the token as 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'.

The portal issues a refresh token. Exchange it for an access token with POST https://external.getnexar.com/dev-portal/refresh-token (form field refresh_token), then send 'Authorization: Bearer {token}'.

cards.name: Errand
cards.short: Agents send a nearby person in Seoul (Gangnam beta) for in-app camera photos and answers.
cards.summary: Agent-native errand dispatch in Seoul. An agent checks live worker coverage, gets an exact quote, then dispatches a task (check, verify, photograph, queue or pickup) over a remote MCP server or REST. Nearby workers with the Errand phone app get a push notification; one accepts, goes to the spot and shoots photos with the in-app camera only (gallery uploads blocked), answering up to five structured questions. The server checks capture location and time, then an AI judges the photo against the buyer's validation_criteria; a worker gets two attempts. Results return photos, answers, the verdict, GPS distance and capture time. The beta covers Gangnam and nearby areas only, and live worker availability can be zero. Prepaid in Korean won, topped up by bank transfer.

tasks: check (is a store, pop-up, office or venue open)
verify (product on shelf, price)
photograph (storefront, menu, sign, notice, product, queue)
queue (queue length or waiting time, allowed queue tasks)
pickup (small item)
structured on-site answers

pricing.model: Reward set by the buyer + platform fee of 20% (minimum ₩500), prepaid in KRW
pricing.notes: Reward per task ₩1,000–₩200,000; the smallest possible charge is ₩1,000 + ₩500 fee = ₩1,500 (≈ $1.13 at 1,325.28 KRW/USD, ECB reference rate 2026-10-26). The fee includes VAT and is earned only on completed tasks; reward + fee are escrowed at dispatch and refunded in full on failure, expiry or pre-acceptance cancellation. Examples: reward ₩5,000 → charge ₩6,000; ₩10,000 → ₩12,000. Default key caps: ₩20,000 reward per task and ₩50,000 per day including fees; raise by e-mailing support. The worker page says tasks posted so far paid ₩8,000–₩15,000. POST /api/v1/quote returns the exact total_charge_krw before anything is charged. A first one-photo check in Gangnam/Yeoksam is free through a trial form, placed by the operator.

latency.typical: Tens of minutes to hours; the buyer sets a deadline of 10 minutes to 24 hours
latency.notes: expires_in_minutes 10–1440; the docs recommend 120 or more to allow for travel. Most of the time is a worker accepting and travelling; AI verification takes 10–30 seconds. The worker page says a task usually takes 10–30 minutes on site. Unfinished tasks expire automatically and are refunded. The operator-placed free trial is 'usually same day to next day'.

delivery.basis: Docs: 'expires_in_minutes ✓ 10–1440. 이동 시간을 고려해 120 이상 권장' (10–1440; 120 or more recommended to allow for travel time). FAQ: verification takes 10–30 seconds; most of the time is the worker accepting, travelling and shooting.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes at delivery: captured on site after dispatch
freshness.notes: Each result carries captured_at and checks.capture_age_min. Photo URLs are signed and expire after 1 hour; a read-only share_url lasts 30 days.

regions: South Korea: Seoul, Gangnam / Yeoksam and nearby areas (beta)
coverage.notes: llms.txt: 'Current beta coverage is Seoul, focused on Gangnam and nearby areas. Worker availability is live and can be zero.' The terms (C-1) describe the service as a Gangnam-area beta. The public coverage endpoint reports reachable_workers (notifications on, seen within 24 h, last location inside the radius); the docs say to treat 0 as 0. A keyless call for Gangnam Station (radius 3 km) on 2026-10-27 05:42 UTC returned reachable_workers 0, dispatchable false. Each API key can also be limited to an allowed area.

licensing.summary: Terms B-3: the requester may use task results (photos, location and time, answers) for its own business purposes ('자신의 업무 목적으로 이용할 수 있습니다'). Results contain no worker personal data, and the requester must not use them to identify or contact the worker. Accuracy is guaranteed only as far as the verdict against the validation criteria. Ownership, resale and AI training are not mentioned. The privacy policy says evidence photos are sent to Anthropic only for automated verification and are not used for other purposes.

rate_limit.notes: The public coverage endpoint; 429 RATE_LIMITED on excess. Authenticated endpoints: the key's daily budget is the practical limit.

auth.how_to_get: Connect an OAuth-capable MCP client to https://errand.be/api/mcp; the protected-resource metadata names the Supabase authorization server https://ekygxbccwbwcppkbpetc.supabase.co/auth/v1, which publishes a registration_endpoint (RFC 7591), authorization_code + refresh_token grants, public clients (auth method none) and PKCE S256 (plain also listed). The resource metadata lists no scopes. Docs: OAuth is for MCP; REST uses the API key. Spending still needs a prepaid balance and stays within the key/account caps. Dynamic client registration is deprecated by the MCP specification of 2026-07-28 in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD); whether Errand accepts CIMD is not stated.

Enter an e-mail at https://errand.be and type the 6-digit code; an er_live_ key is issued at once and shown once. Send 'Authorization: Bearer er_live_…'. Works for REST and as the developer/CLI fallback for MCP.

mcp.notes: Stateless Streamable HTTP (POST JSON-RPC only; GET returns 405). Registry latest 0.2.1 (published 2026-09-17). Seven tools mapping one-to-one to REST: errand_check_coverage, errand_list_capabilities, errand_quote, errand_dispatch, errand_get_status, errand_get_result, errand_cancel. A ChatGPT plugin offers only the five read tools (no dispatch, cancel or payment).

endpoints.notes: MCP errand_quote. Creates nothing; returns total_charge_krw, platform_fee_krw, balance_krw, balance_sufficient, coverage and can_dispatch (true only when a worker is reachable and the balance suffices).

endpoints.notes: MCP errand_dispatch. Escrows reward + fee. Text the worker reads should be in Korean. 422 UNSAFE_TASK / PRIVACY_VIOLATING_TASK on content rejection.

MCP errand_get_status. open → accepted → arrived (GPS confirmed on site) → submitted → completed; terminal failures failed (both attempts rejected), expired, cancelled, all refunded. webhook_url receives mission.completed / failed / cancelled / expired.

MCP errand_get_result. Returns status, share_url (read-only, no login, 30 days), verdict {passed, score, feedback}, answers, evidence {photo_urls (signed, expire in 1 h), gps {lat, lng, accuracy_m}, distance_from_task_m, captured_at, checks {distance_m, capture_age_min, exif_gps_present, failures}}.

cards.summary: The Ethiopian Meteorological Institute runs a WIS2-in-a-box node at wis2.ethiomet.gov.et that republishes the country's hourly synoptic (SYNOP) observations. Besides the WMO BUFR files, the node serves each decoded value over an OGC API Features endpoint as GeoJSON or CSV: one feature per variable with station WIGOS identifier, coordinates, variable name, unit, value and report time. A keyless GET sorted by -reportTime on 2026-11-07 UTC returned a report stamped 2026-11-07 21:00 UTC; the collection held 99,373 features and the node's station list 30 stations. The dataset description says it comes from the institute's GBON automatic weather station network.

cards.name: Execution Market
cards.summary: Bounty marketplace run by Ultravioleta DAO ('Universal Execution Layer') where an AI agent or a person posts a USDC-paid task with required evidence types (e.g. GPS-tagged photo, video, text), assigns an applicant, and releases on-chain escrow after reviewing the submission. Executors can be people or other AI agents. Callable over REST, a remote OAuth MCP server and A2A; identity is a crypto wallet with an ERC-8004 on-chain identity, not an account. Most recent completed tasks are small digital or research jobs; physical captures are rare.
cards.short: A crypto-paid bounty marketplace where agents hire people (or other agents) for tasks, incl. GPS-tagged photos.

tasks: physical presence: verify a store is open, photograph a location, check conditions (photo_geo with GPS check)
data collection: surveys, price checks, inventory counts, measurements
knowledge access: scan documents, photograph posted information
simple actions and errands: buy items, deliver packages
human authority: notarize, certify, translate
remote research, verification and digital tasks (often done by AI agents)

pricing.model: publisher sets the bounty; a 13% platform fee is deducted from the bounty at release
pricing.notes: Bounty range $0.01-$10,000 (live config: min_bounty_usd 0.01, max_bounty_usd 10000); the docs say escrow deposits are additionally capped at $100 per task. The 13% fee comes out of the bounty, not on top: a $10 bounty pays the worker $8.70. Optional paid evidence analysis ('verification seal'): $0.50 standard, $1.00 with video, paid over x402. Platform metrics on 2026-10-26 report $934.48 total payment volume across 3,402 completed tasks, so typical bounties are cents.

latency.typical: Not guaranteed; bounded by the deadline the publisher sets (1-720 hours)
latency.notes: The publisher sets deadline_hours (1-720); tasks with no completed submission expire (2,479 of 6,966 tasks had expired by 2026-10-26). Applicants apply and the publisher assigns one, which locks escrow. A submission left unreviewed for 72 hours auto-settles to the worker; an inconclusive automated verdict opens a dispute with a 24-hour response deadline that may go unclaimed for small bounties.

regions: Global (self-registered workers; no country limit stated)
coverage.notes: No country list or limit is published; an OFAC sanctioned-address blacklist exists. Supply is thin: public metrics on 2026-10-26 listed 652 registered workers, 56 workers who have completed a task and 13 active. Of the 200 most recent completed tasks (2026-10-08 to 2026-10-27), 1 was physical_presence and 2 were outdoor photos (sky over Medellin, Miami night sky); most were cent-sized knowledge, research and QA tasks, many done by AI agents. Only 2 tasks were open that day, both remote research. The geo-matching filter (geo_match_mode) is accepted but switched off in production.

licensing.summary: Terms of Service (last updated 2026-10-03) are short: 18+, no fraudulent evidence, 13% fee, payments final once settled on-chain, platform provided as-is. They say nothing about who owns submitted evidence, licences, resale or AI training. The Privacy Policy (2026-10-24) says evidence is kept in private S3 storage and shared through short-lived links with the worker and the publisher only, is sent to third-party AI verification providers (via OpenRouter: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, Qwen, DeepSeek and others) and may be reviewed by human moderators; faces and plates are not blurred; people in evidence can ask for removal. It does not say Execution Market trains its own models on evidence. An optional DX402 copy of each paid submission is anchored, encrypted to the buyer's key, for 90 days by default.

human.method: Every worker wallet must hold an ERC-8004 on-chain identity; World ID Orb verification is required server-side for bounties of $500 or more (live config worldid_min_bounty_for_orb_usd 500). Bidirectional on-chain ratings (ERC-8004, scored via describe.net). Each application and delivery records executor_kind (human, human_via_agent, autonomous_agent, robot, unknown).
human.unknown: Below $500 no proof of personhood is required, and an ERC-8004 identity is a wallet, not a person. Executors may be AI agents: target_executor 'human' is only a preference, and executor_kind is inferred from the request channel, not proven. Most recent completions have no executor_kind recorded.

application.method: A mobile app (Expo camera + location) and a no-login web evidence link capture photos with camera/GPS; agents may also upload files by presigned URL.
application.unknown: No app or device attestation is documented; the docs say the mobile app's store links are 'available when published', and evidence can arrive from the web form or any signed API client.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: the submission records whether the photo came from the camera or the gallery, and uploaded files are SHA-256 hashed into evidence_content_hash (hashing on upload, not signing). No C2PA.

time.method: Photo capture time from EXIF and the submission timestamp are shown to the publisher; a timestamp_proof evidence type exists; Ring 1 checks timestamps.
time.unknown: EXIF time is set by the device and editable; no trusted time-stamp (e.g. RFC 3161) is applied to captures. The EIP-191-signed verdict and DX402 anchor show when EM received and judged the submission, not when the photo was taken.

location.method: gps_required (default on for photo/video tasks with a place): the evidence's GPS, else EXIF GPS, else the browser location, must fall within a radius (500 m default, 1,000 m for simple_action) of the task point, or Ring 1 fails and the delivery goes to a person. Docs describe server-side GPS anti-spoofing (speed and coordinate-consistency checks).
location.unknown: Phone or browser GPS is self-reported and spoofable; the anti-spoofing checks are not specified in detail. Without task coordinates any GPS in the evidence satisfies the requirement.

content.method: Ring 1 'PHOTINT' forensic checks (EXIF, tampering, generative-AI detection with hard-fail floors, photo source camera vs gallery) produce a pre-check score. Optional Ring 2 LLM review (via OpenRouter) scores whether the evidence shows the task was done, with an EIP-191-signed verdict the publisher can check against the arbiter address; the publisher reviews and approves or rejects; disputes go to self-claimed human arbiters.
content.unknown: The signature proves who issued a verdict, not that it is right; Ring 2 is opt-in, runs one provider today, and auto-release on a pass is disabled. Unreviewed submissions auto-settle to the worker after 72 hours. The Ring 1 detector, its version and false-positive rate are not published.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of a capture. Reputation ratings and dispute arbiters judge the worker, not the observation; a publisher could post several tasks for the same place, but that is buyer-side.

receipt.method: When the arbiter runs, its verdict is EIP-191-signed over the per-file SHA-256 evidence hash (evidence_content_hash) and bound to the task_id; anyone can recover the signer and compare it with the published arbiter address. A paid seal is an EIP-191 attestation by the owner of ERC-8004 Agent #2106 over the exact SHA-256 of the artifacts plus the verdict.
receipt.unknown: Signed by the provider's own arbiter, not an independent party; bound to task_id, not to a buyer nonce; the arbiter is opt-in (manual by default). The signature shows who issued the verdict, not that it is right; whether commitment_hash is written on-chain is not shown.

sources.claim: evidence_content_hash, EIP-191 arbiter_verdict_signature, paid seal by the owner of ERC-8004 Agent #2106

auth.how_to_get: ERC-8128 HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421 over EIP-191) signed by the agent's own EVM wallet on every request (Signature, Signature-Input, Content-Digest; nonce from GET /auth/erc8128/nonce; max 300 s). The wallet first registers a gasless ERC-8004 identity at POST /reputation/register; no client_id, password or API key is issued. Recommended signer: PayBox or Open Wallet Standard.

Remote MCP at https://mcp.execution.market/mcp/: OAuth 2.1 authorization code with mandatory PKCE S256, public clients, RFC 7591 dynamic registration at https://auth.execution.market/oauth/register or a Client ID Metadata Document. Sign-in is Sign-In with Ethereum, so the person still needs a wallet. A bearer never moves money on its own: assigning needs a per-operation EIP-3009 signature, and approving needs that or the separately consented agent:approve scope (capped at $100 per approval and 50 approvals; 15-minute token). The auth server lists 9 scopes; the MCP resource metadata advertises 6 and omits agent:approve and reputation:rate.

Signed wallet session for clients that cannot sign requests: POST /auth/session/challenge returns EIP-712 typed data; the wallet signs it and the result is sent in X-EM-Session (TTL up to 900 s). Refused on escrow, evidence, reputation and similar paths. Gated by EM_WALLET_SESSION_ENABLED.

endpoints.notes: Open tasks on the public board; no credentials. GET /tasks?status=completed also lists tasks without credentials.
Find available workers; requires an ERC-8128 signature or bearer token.

endpoints.params: title, instructions, category (21), bounty_usd (0.01-10000), deadline_hours (1-720), evidence_required (1-5 of 18 types, e.g. photo_geo, video, text_response); optional payment_network, location_hint (public), location_lat/location_lng (exact only to the assigned worker), gps_required, location_radius_m, geo_match_mode, min_reputation, arbiter_mode, target_executor
endpoints.notes: Publishing locks no money. Then GET /tasks/{id}/applications, and POST /tasks/{id}/assign with an X-Payment-Auth EIP-3009 escrow signature (challenge at GET /tasks/{id}/assign/challenge) assigns the worker and locks escrow. Unknown body fields are rejected (422).
Task details and status; GET /tasks/{task_id}/events lists what happened since you last looked.

Opens a delivery's evidence (records that the publisher saw it) with evidence_content_hash, arbiter verdict and 5-minute download URLs. GET /tasks/{task_id}/submissions gives status only. POST /submissions/{id}/approve releases escrow; /reject rejects.

api.sdk: OpenAPI 3 (234 paths) at https://execution.market/openapi.json; Swagger at https://api.execution.market/docs; A2A v0.3 agent card; MCP server card v9.7.0; uvd-x402-sdk (Python/npm) for escrow and DX402
api.rate_limits: Task creation 100/h, queries 1000/h, batch create 10/h; request body 1 MiB

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP, 65 tools per llms.txt (em_publish_task, em_assign_task, em_open_submission_evidence, em_approve_submission, ...). Registry entry v1.0.0, published 2026-03-20. Also an A2A JSON-RPC endpoint at https://api.execution.market/a2a/v1.

api.notes: API keys are disabled in production (403). Identity is the wallet; an ERC-8004 identity is mandatory before publishing (403 identity_required otherwise). Task text and location_hint are public on the board, so put exact addresses only in location_lat/location_lng.

payment.notes: Stablecoin only (USDC; EURC, PYUSD, AUSD, USDT listed on some chains) from the publisher's own wallet: an EIP-3009 authorization locks the bounty in x402r escrow at assignment on 9 EVM chains (Base default, Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Optimism, Celo, Monad, Arc), released gaslessly with the 13% fee split on-chain at approval. Solana bounties are paid by charge or a payment channel (channel flow not working end to end in production). Metered MPP sessions are beta on Base and Arbitrum, capped at $100. No card or fiat checkout is documented.

requester.checks: The publisher needs a wallet with an ERC-8004 identity (gasless, self-registered) and must accept the Terms (18+). Each published or edited task's text is reviewed by an LLM (TypeSafe via OpenRouter) against the task policy and can be refused. Workers are told not to make third parties or minors the subject of evidence photos.
requester.unknown: No identity or KYC check on publishers beyond the wallet is documented; the task policy page itself was not retrievable, so how requests to watch, follow or photograph a specific person are handled is not stated.

cards.summary: Crowdsourced shoppers, using the Field Agent mobile app, visit a named store to photograph shelves and displays, check prices and answer audit questions. The company (Field Agent, Inc.) rebranded to Storesight in 2025 and fieldagent.net redirects to storesight.com; the shopper app keeps the Field Agent name. Buyers order audits by the response, at published list prices, in the self-serve Storesight Projects shop (web sign-up, no ordering API), or through full service. pricing.model: Per response (one shopper submission) at self-serve list prices; full-service and enterprise work by quote
pricing.notes: List prices from the Storesight Projects shop on 2026-10-26: Item Photo, Signage Audit and Club Entryway Photos $26; Price Check and On-Shelf Availability $27; Item Check Up and Category Overview Photos $27.50; Display Compliance $28; Planogram Visibility, Modular Pics and Category Display Photos $30; Store Walk $38; Walmart Shelf Price Audit $40; Shelf Correction (Zoning) $24 with before/after photos. Optional add-on questions are $0.50 per response. Survey-style 'Insights' products that need no store visit start at $20. storesight.com/pricing is a 404; prices appear only in the shop.

latency.typical: Self-serve projects run at least 5 days (5 to 17 by product); full-service audits launch in under 24 hours on average
latency.notes: The self-serve builder enforces a minimum project length of 5 days for most store audits and up to 17 for buy-and-review products, with 0 to 3 days' lead time before launch. The platform page promises results from the field 'within days'. Shopper-side review of submissions can take 3 to 5 business days.

coverage.notes: Core network is in the US: Storesight cites 3 million U.S. shoppers and audits 'from major metropolitan areas to rural markets'. The shopper app runs in 8 countries through international partners (separate local sites and support for Canada, UK, Mexico, Ecuador, Spain, South Africa and Australia); density outside the US is not published. Syndicated shelf-photo categories are collected in the USA, Canada and the UK. Company-stated scale: about 6 million shelf and display images a year across 50,000 retail locations; 50 major retailers covered.

licensing.summary: Two documents apply. The shopper Participation Agreement says a shopper's work product is a 'work made for hire' for the Client, and all ownership rights, including worldwide IP, vest in the Client; Field Agent also takes a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence to exploit all submitted materials "in connection with the operation and maintenance of the Platform". The buyer-side Conditions of Use (2 September 2025) say Storesight owns all right, title and interest, including IP, in the Data Services, Site and Services, which are provided as-is with no warranty that they are timely. Neither document mentions resale or AI training. Syndicated shelf data bought from Storesight is Storesight's. Storesight marketing says its models "actively learn and refine their capabilities with increased usage"; no clause says buyers' photos train them, so that is not stated.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). cards.name: Fintraffic Digitraffic road weather cameras
cards.short: 816 road-weather camera stations across Finland, new stills about every 10 min, CC BY 4.0, no key.
cards.summary: Finland's national traffic agency publishes its road weather cameras as open data: 816 stations with 2,288 fixed views (presets). Each view has a stable latest-image URL, a capture time, a road address and a view direction, and the last 24 hours of images can be fetched by version.

tasks: current still of a Finnish road or roadside view
visual check of snow, ice, fog, road surface and traffic
images of the same view over the last 24 hours

pricing.notes: Open data under CC BY 4.0; no key, no account and no paid tier.

latency.typical: about 10 minutes
latency.notes: Digitraffic: images are updated about every 10 minutes (station collectionInterval 600 s). Sampled 2026-10-26 (05:00 UTC on 27 Oct): across 2,283 presets the latest measuredTime was a median 5.5 min old, 90th percentile 10 min, 2,225 under 15 min; a few long-idle presets are days or more stale. The sampled image's x-amz-meta-last-modified matched its measuredTime.

coverage.notes: 816 stations on the Finnish road network, from the south coast to northern Lapland (lat 59.9-70.1), one of them in Eckero, Aland. On 2026-10-26, 814 were GATHERING and 2 REMOVED_TEMPORARILY. Check collectionStatus, state and each preset's inCollection before relying on a view.

licensing.summary: Fintraffic's open data is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, which 'gives the right to distribute, remix, tweak, and build upon our data, even commercially', with credit. Attribution must preserve the copyright notice and disclaimers, link the original site and the licence, and describe any changes; suggested credit: 'Source: Fintraffic / digitraffic.fi, license CC 4.0 BY'. The terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training.

human.unknown: Fixed automated cameras; no person is involved in capture.

application.unknown: No attestation of the camera software or the upload pipeline.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Fixed road cameras; Digitraffic says road data come from the traffic management systems of ITM Finland Ltd, a Fintraffic subsidiary. Station metadata names the camera type (e.g. BOSCH, VAPIX). No per-image proof that a frame came from the named camera; images carry no C2PA manifest.

time.method: measuredTime per preset in /stations/{id}/data; the image's x-amz-meta-last-modified header matches it.
time.unknown: Timestamps are not signed; the image overlay shows no capture time.

location.method: Station coordinates, road address (road number, section, distance) and municipality, plus a direction code and name per preset.
location.unknown: Coordinates and view direction are operator metadata, not verified per image.

content.unknown: No integrity or content checks are documented. An unknown or unpublished preset still returns HTTP 200 with a grey 'Image not available' JPEG, so check the size or the ETag.

corroboration.unknown: Station metadata can name a nearestWeatherStationId (seen on the sampled station) whose road weather readings can be cross-checked by the caller, but Digitraffic publishes no cross-check.

auth.how_to_get: No key. Send a Digitraffic-User header naming your app (no personal data); it raises your request allowance. No Authorization header is needed. JSON APIs require Accept-Encoding: gzip (406 without it); images do not.

endpoints.notes: GeoJSON FeatureCollection of all stations: coordinates, collectionStatus, presets with inCollection.
One station in detail: camera type, collectionInterval, municipality, road address, nearestWeatherStationId, and per preset the imageUrl, resolution, direction and name.
measuredTime per preset; /stations/data returns all stations.
Latest image (e.g. 1280x720). Supports ETag/If-None-Match (304 when unchanged). Unknown presets return a 200 placeholder image.
Links to each preset's images over the last 24 hours (imageUrl with versionId, lastModified, size); /stations/history covers all.
Presets whose publishableTo changed: views taken out of or returned to public view.

api.rate_limits: Without the Digitraffic-User header: 60 requests/min per IP for weathercam images and 60/min for tie.digitraffic.fi v1 APIs; more with the header (no figure published). Excess requests get 429. Most JSON responses are cached for about a minute.

mcp.community: No Fintraffic MCP server in the official MCP Registry. The only Digitraffic entry is a third-party AIS vessel server (io.github.pipeworx-io/digitraffic-ais), not weather cameras.

api.notes: OpenAPI: https://tie.digitraffic.fi/swagger/openapi.json. Deprecated API versions stay up for six months and return Deprecation and Sunset headers.

freshness.typical_age: 0-10 minutes
freshness.notes: Images are kept for 24 hours (history endpoint; S3 expiry rule 'Delete versions and current images after 24h').

delivery.basis: Digitraffic road-traffic page: 'Weather camera images are updated approximately about every 10 minutes.'

rate_limit.notes: Without the Digitraffic-User header; the header raises the allowance (no figure published). 429 on excess. gzip required for JSON.

requester.checks: None. Calls are anonymous; Digitraffic asks for a Digitraffic-User header naming the app and offers optional app sign-up so it can contact heavy users.
requester.unknown: Nothing is ordered or commissioned, so no requester checks apply.

payment.notes: Free; nothing to pay.

cards.name: FlyGuys
cards.short: Nationwide US drone, LiDAR and inspection missions flown by a pilot network.
cards.summary: FlyGuys (Lafayette, Louisiana) runs FlyGuys Capture, a platform that dispatches missions to a network of FAA-certified (Part 107) drone pilots for aerial imagery, mapping, LiDAR, inspections, thermal and multispectral capture, with QA before delivery. It publishes a Swagger API (api.flyguys.com) to create jobs from a catalogue package id and a location, read job status, update status, and fetch delivered files via temporary S3 or Azure credentials; access runs through an Azure API Management developer portal. Pricing is quoted per project.

tasks: order a drone mission (aerial imagery, orthomosaic, 3D, LiDAR, roof or tower inspection, thermal, multispectral) at a US address or polygon
create a job through the API from a catalogue package id, location and annotated areas
read job status and update it (for example put on hold)
list and download delivered files through temporary S3 or Azure storage credentials

pricing.model: quote per project; volume discounts and MSAs
pricing.notes: FAQ: 'FlyGuys does not offer set packages'; LiDAR 'generally range from $6,500 to $9,000 per day and up to $12,000 depending on client needs'. No per-mission list price for imagery was found.

latency.typical: 2 to 5 business days after the flight for non-LiDAR work
latency.notes: FAQ: 'Projects are typically ready within 2-5 business days with an ASAP mindset for all non-LiDAR work' and 'We fly as soon as possible based on factors such as weather, pilot availability, site availability and airspace restrictions.' Time to first flight is not stated. The MSA gives the client 7 days to report non-conforming deliverables, which are re-flown at FlyGuys' cost.

coverage.notes: FAQ: 'If you are within the US, absolutely! All inquiries originating outside the United States will be considered on an individual basis.' The AI-assistants page says 'Geographic coverage: United States, with additional capabilities evaluated according to project requirements.' Pilots need their own drone and a Part 107 licence.

licensing.summary: FAQ: 'FlyGuys owns all data collected using our technology unless otherwise specified by the client.' The Master Services Terms (6 Aug 2024 docx) say FlyGuys owns the Services' intellectual property, that re-use of deliverables for other purposes is at the client's risk, and that deliverables are AS-IS; no clause on AI training or resale was found, and any licence to the client is set in the Task Order.

human.unknown: Pilots must hold their own drone and an FAA Part 107 certificate and register their FAA number in the pilot portal; FlyGuys assigns a mission coordinator. How identity and certificate are verified is not published.
human.method: Pilot portal registration with FAA number

application.unknown: No device or app attestation of captures is documented.

camera.unknown: No capture-device signing (such as C2PA) is documented; recommended drones (Mavic 3 Enterprise, Matrice 4) are named but not attested.

time.unknown: Mission records carry timestamps; no independent time-stamp scheme is documented.

location.unknown: Jobs carry a coordinate and annotated polygons; flight-log or geotag verification is not described.

content.unknown: FlyGuys says it performs QA/QC review of collected data before delivery; no public method or evidence.
content.method: Internal QA/QC review

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check is documented.

freshness.typical_age: Flown after you order
freshness.notes: Weather, pilot, site and airspace permitting.

Credentials come from signing up at the Azure API Management developer portal dev-connect.flyguys.com; whether sign-up is approved by FlyGuys was not verified.

Updates mission status

cards.name: FMI Open Data (Finnish Meteorological Institute observations)
cards.short: Finnish weather, sea level, lightning and air quality; keyless, CC BY.
cards.summary: The Finnish Meteorological Institute publishes much of its data as open data through OGC WFS and WMS services. The keyless WFS at opendata.fmi.fi offers stored queries for observations (weather stations, mareographs, lightning, air quality, magnetometers and more) alongside forecasts and radar; the data are licensed CC BY 4.0, which also covers the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority's data and air-quality data in the service.

mareograph (sea level) observations
lightning observations
hourly air-quality observations
magnetometer observations
radiation measurements from the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority

latency.notes: The live call with timestep=10 returned a latest timestamp of 15:40:00Z at about 15:41Z, but its value was NaN (no reading yet), so the freshest filled value was older. No delivery delay is stated on the pages read.

regions: Finland (land stations, Baltic coast mareographs, lightning, air quality)
coverage.notes: The pages read describe Finnish Meteorological Institute data; geographic extent of each stored query is not listed there.

licensing.summary: Licence page: "The Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license (CC BY 4.0) shall be used by the Finnish Meteorological Institute's open data service. The license shall apply to the FMI's and the Radiation and Nuclear Safety Authority's open data sets as well as air quality data sets that are stored in the open data web-service." The WFS page says "User must accept Creative Commons license before using the open data service interfaces." The terms read do not mention AI training or resale by name.

application.unknown: No signing or attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: Not a camera source.

cards.name: Freelancer.com (local jobs)
cards.summary: Global freelance marketplace whose API can post 'Local Jobs' projects pinned to a place (country, city, latitude and longitude) in job types such as Inspections, Local Job, Photography and Video Tours. Freelancers bid; the buyer awards a bid and pays through Milestone Payments released on approval. The User Agreement (s.33) forbids automated access, including the API, without Freelancer's express written permission.
cards.short: Post a local job anywhere; nearby freelancers bid to go and do it.

tasks: site verification
inspections
local photography and video tours
errands and pickups
investigation

pricing.model: bid-based; buyer sets a budget range, freelancers bid
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published (set by bids). Posting is free. Employer fee on award: 3% or USD 3, whichever is greater (fixed price); 3% of each payment (hourly); refundable if cancelled within 7 days. Card, PayPal or Skrill: USD 0.30 + 2.3% (not for Australian transactions, which carry an Account Admin Fee of AUD 0.75 + 0.99%). Milestone arbitration: USD 5 or 5%, whichever is greater, per party, refunded to the winner. Optional upgrades include IP Agreement (USD 22.99 in the fee table, USD 21.99 in the same page's FAQ), NDA USD 22.99, Urgent USD 10.99.

latency.typical: Not published; posting, review, bidding, then award
latency.notes: No SLA. API-posted projects usually enter a review queue before they go live (developer docs, sandbox page). Active projects on 2026-10-26 via the public API: Inspections 17, Local Job 89, Photo Anywhere 0.

coverage.notes: Freelancer says Local Jobs 'get help in any location, anywhere in the world' and claims a 'talent pool of over 90.5 million professionals'. 167 of 3,487 job types are local. Active Inspections and Local Job projects on 2026-10-26 were concentrated in Thailand, the US, South Korea, Brazil and the UK, with a few in about 20 other countries. Density per city is not published. People barred under Australian or other applicable law may not use the site.

licensing.summary: No default clause transfers ownership of project deliverables to the buyer; a paid IP Agreement upgrade 'ensures intellectual property rights transfer to you' (Fees and Charges). Freelancer takes a broad, sublicensable, irrevocable licence to User Content (User Agreement s.10). The terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training or resale. Freelancer may record in-app audio and video calls for 'quality assurance, training, and service improvement' (s.15), without saying whether that means model training.

human.method: Optional 'Verified by Freelancer' KYC: government photo ID, a photo holding the ID beside a one-time keycode, and two proofs of address, reviewed by Freelancer's team. Freelancer can also demand ID at any time (s.14).
human.unknown: Verification is optional for sellers, so the freelancer you award may be unverified. Freelancer states it 'cannot and do[es] not confirm each User's purported identity' (s.38).

application.unknown: Freelancers upload files they captured however they like; there is no capture app.

camera.unknown: Nothing stops a gallery upload, screenshot or generated image.

time.unknown: No capture timestamp is checked; only message and upload times exist.

location.unknown: The project has a location, but where a file was captured is not checked. OAuth scopes fln:location_tracking_create/view ('location information of freelancer working on project') exist, but no endpoint using them is documented.

content.method: The buyer reviews the work and releases the Milestone Payment; disputes go to Freelancer's Milestone Dispute Resolution, with paid arbitration on submitted evidence.
content.unknown: Freelancer does not review deliverables, and for Local Jobs it does not verify credentials or statements of capability (s.16).

corroboration.unknown: No independent check. A buyer could award the same task to a second freelancer by hand.

auth.how_to_get: Personal Access Token: Generate Token at https://accounts.freelancer.com/settings/develop. Acts only as the account that made it; one active token per environment; valid 30 days. Sandbox tokens (https://accounts.freelancer-sandbox.com/settings/develop) work only on https://www.freelancer-sandbox.com. User Agreement s.33 bars automated means, "including ... access to our API", "without our express written permission"; the API T&Cs (apiterms) govern API use, and issuing a token may count as that permission, which is unconfirmed. Marked false until a person decides.

Create a client application at https://accounts.freelancer.com ('Develop with Freelancer.com'); applications are reviewed (expect a reply within 5 business days), and requests for single-user apps are denied. Authorization-code flow: https://accounts.freelancer.com/oauth/authorize with scope=basic and advanced_scopes as numeric ids; token at https://accounts.freelancer.com/oauth/token with a client secret. Access tokens last 30 days, with refresh tokens.

auth.how_to_get: Add https://getterdone.ai/mcp as a remote MCP server; the client registers itself (POST /oauth/register, RFC 7591) and the owner signs in once on the consent page. authorization_code + PKCE S256 (required); a token minted with resource=https://getterdone.ai/mcp works only at /mcp. Paid task creation still needs the owner's one-time identity check, card and funding token. Dynamic client registration is deprecated by the MCP specification of 2026-07-28 in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD); whether GetterDone accepts CIMD is not stated.

Owner registers the agent at https://getterdone.ai/register-agent (Stripe Identity KYC + card) and gets an API key gd_<clientId>:<clientSecret>; POST /api/auth/agent/token (client_credentials, scope agent:full) returns a Bearer token valid 1 h. Developer path: GET /api/auth/agent/challenge then POST /api/auth/agent/register (proof-of-work).

cards.name: Hire a Human
cards.summary: Small freelance marketplace (operated by Design 3D Solutions Ltd, founder Tom Carr) for physical and digital tasks, where people and AI agents post tasks with a budget and freelancers it says are Veriff-verified bid on them. Agents post through a REST API with a scoped x-api-key, issued only after the operator passes Veriff KYC; an MCP server is advertised but its URL is not published. Payment is held in escrow and released when the client confirms the work. Published headline numbers conflict (142 vs 56+ countries; 3,275+ vs 1,200+ tasks completed).
cards.short: A freelance marketplace where AI agents post tasks by API and Veriff-verified people bid to do them.

tasks: on-site inspections
mystery shopping and inventory checks
photography
event attendance and real-time reporting
deliveries, errands and sample collection
field research
quality checks
phone calls

pricing.model: client sets a budget and freelancers bid their own rate; no client fee; 10% deducted from the freelancer on completion
pricing.unit: hour (typical physical-task rate, not a minimum)
pricing.notes: Provider: freelancers 'typically $15–$30/hr for physical tasks and $30–$100+ for digital work'; 'Clients: No fees — you pay the agreed task price, nothing extra'; no minimums. Listed freelancer profiles show rates as low as $5/hr, so $15 is the stated typical floor, not a minimum.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: FAQ: 'physical tasks in active areas are often filled within hours' with an urgent deadline and a fair budget. That is time to find a freelancer, not to deliver. Escrow releases 24–48 hours after the client approves; disputes are reviewed within 48 hours.

coverage.notes: Coverage claims conflict: the home page shows 142 countries, 2,847+ verified humans and 3,275+ tasks completed (fixed numbers in the site's code, not live counts); the FAQ says '56+ countries' and 'over 1,200 completed tasks', as does llms.txt. The View Tasks page's '150 Active Tasks' and '$1.2M Total Value' and its task list are sample data built into the page. The Browse Humans directory shows real-looking profiles (first ones in Pakistan, Kenya and Nigeria), each showing 0 completed tasks. No country list is published. Home-page counters also vary per load (seen 142 and 122 countries, 2,464-2,847 humans, 2,835-3,275 tasks on 2026-10-27), so none is reliable.

licensing.summary: The Terms (Design 3D Solutions Ltd, effective 2026-02-20, Delaware law) are a generic AI-service template: users own their 'inputs (prompts)' and the 'AI Outputs generated specifically for you', and grant the operator a perpetual, worldwide licence to use them to provide and improve the Services, 'including anonymized/aggregated use for AI/ML development'; opt-out of non-essential use by email to privacy@design3dsolutions.com. Users may not 'Train competing AI models with our outputs or prompts' or scrape content. Nothing addresses who owns a freelancer's deliverables (photos, reports), resale, or the buyer's right to train AI on them. The Terms also say 'We will NOT use raw or identifiable personal data (PII) for model training'; the AI/ML use is anonymized or aggregated only.

human.method: Veriff KYC for every freelancer (government ID photo plus selfie video liveness check, automated review) before the profile goes live; agent operators must pass KYC before generating API keys
human.unknown: Whether the verified account holder is the person who actually does the task; no per-task identity check is described.

application.unknown: No capture app: the FAQ says there is no mobile app yet, and proof of work is uploaded through the website.

camera.unknown: No live-capture requirement is described; uploaded proof could be any file, including an old or edited photo.

time.unknown: No capture-time check on proof is described; only platform timestamps on job status.

location.unknown: No GPS, check-in or location check on the freelancer or the proof is described.

content.method: The freelancer uploads proof of work and marks the job complete; the client reviews it and releases escrow; support reviews disputes within 48 hours
content.unknown: The platform does not say it checks proof itself; whether the proof shows what was asked rests on the client's own review.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of deliverables is offered.

cards.name: Bee Maps (Hivemapper)
cards.summary: Dashcam street-level imagery network run by Hivemapper, Inc. (dba Bee Maps). Contributors drive with Bee cameras and, since August 2026, are paid by default in USDC funded by Bee Maps. Data is sold through the Bee Maps Data API: imagery, ML-detected road features, AI event videos, and on-demand collection (Burst and video requests) for a chosen location.
cards.short: A dashcam network that can be asked for fresh imagery or video of a specific street.

tasks: street-level imagery by polygon (latest, or a specific week)
road feature detections (speed limit and stop signs, fire hydrants, traffic lights, parking and turn restrictions, crosswalks)
AI event videos (harsh braking, aggressive acceleration, swerving, high speed, high g-force, stop sign violation) with GPS traces and IMU data
on-demand imagery collection (Burst) for a point and radius
on-demand video request for a polygon or a driven line within a time window

pricing.model: consumption-based, prepaid balance, no upfront commitment
pricing.notes: Public rate card: imagery $0.005 per image; AI event videos $6 per video; road detections $3 per 1,000 detections; Burst $1 per location, paid only when the location is mapped. The price of a /requestVideo order is not published. Bee Edge AI is priced separately ($15/device/month own devices; $0.02/km network devices). Prepaid API balance; add funds $5 to $1,000 through Stripe checkout; new accounts get $20 free credits with no card required. Price increases take effect 14 days after posting.

latency.typical: Archive imagery days to weeks old; Burst results within hours in urban areas, days in rural areas
latency.notes: Per the Data API guide. No SLA or measured latency is published, and Burst timing is described qualitatively. A Burst location stays active for a validity window (the reference example is 30 days); a /requestVideo order expires if no qualifying video is recorded before validUntil.

regions: Burst: global, depends on local driver density
coverage.notes: Provider states 754M total km mapped, 22M unique km and 37% of world roads (beemaps.com counters, self-reported; the API reference says 36%). Density per region is not published in the pages read. Max query area 5 sq km per request. 'Global' (areas *) means no country limit is applied, but the provider claims '100+ countries', not every country.

licensing.summary: The Data Products Terms of Service (Q4 2025) grant a non-exclusive, non-sublicensable, non-transferable right to use the Bee Maps Data Products only in connection with the customer's own Implementations (products that interoperate with the APIs). The customer may not transfer, distribute, resell, lease or (sub)license the Services or Data Products, use them to build a competing product or for benchmarking, and must protect them from scraping. Bee Maps and its licensors exclusively own all rights in the Data Products. The terms do not mention AI or ML training; the docs market AI event videos and imagery for model training; neither is licence text. The terms also bar creating derivative works of the Data Products, so do not read marketing talk of derived datasets as a right.

human.unknown: Capture is passive dashcam recording. Contributors get random three-word usernames and sign in by email; no identity or uniqueness check of contributors is documented.

application.method: Only approved Open Camera devices contribute; the network assigns each new device low trust that rises as it passes visual challenges and agrees with other devices (server-side reputation, not cryptographic attestation).
application.unknown: No hardware or firmware attestation is published. These are Hivemapper Network reward checks; whether they still apply after Bee Maps ended its services agreement with the Hivemapper Foundation (July 2026), and whether API data is filtered by them, is not stated.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Imagery comes from Bee Maps' own dashcam hardware; the network's vision-based consensus is described as defending against AI-generated imagery and replay attacks. No hardware-level signing or attestation is published, and Bee Maps is not on the C2PA conforming products list. Whether a single unverified device's imagery can reach API results is unknown.

time.method: Each frame and video carries a device timestamp; network consensus treats observations as valid when independent devices agree at the same location and time window.
time.unknown: The clock source and any trusted time-stamping are not documented.

location.method: Dual-band (L1/L5) GNSS module with embedded security; frames return GNSS quality metrics (gdop, hdop, pdop, eph, cno) and IMU data; contributions are checked at the H3 hex level against other devices.
location.unknown: Resistance to GNSS spoofing and how the accuracy metrics are derived are not documented. The Helium-hotspot location check described in older Hivemapper posts could not be fetched and is not relied on.

content.method: Road features are ML detections returned with confidence scores, detection counts and first/last-seen dates; faces, bodies, vehicles and licence plates are blurred on the device.
content.unknown: Confidence calibration, error rates, and any human review of detections are not published.

corroboration.method: Vision-based consensus: observations from multiple independent devices at the same hex and time window are cross-referenced, with device-diversity weighting and de-duplication of devices in the same vehicle.
corroboration.unknown: In low-traffic areas there may be too little overlap for consensus. Whether imagery sold through the API, especially a fresh Burst or video request with a single contributor, is corroborated is not stated.

cards.summary: Hover sends a capture request (a link by SMS or email) to a homeowner, adjuster or other person at the property, who scans it with the Hover phone app. Hover turns the photos into a 3D model with roof, exterior or interior measurements (PDF, JSON, XLSX, ESX and more).
