cards.name: Human Archive
cards.short: First-person video, depth, motion and touch data of real work for robot labs, from head-worn rigs and a phone app.

tasks: egocentric video of people doing their jobs in real workplaces (factories, restaurants, laundries, salons, warehouses, construction sites, hotels) and homes, recorded on Human Archive's head-worn multi-camera rigs
rigs with a global-shutter stereo pair and hardware-synchronised IMU; tactile gloves, full-body motion-capture suits and wrist cameras synchronised with RGB-D
first-person video tasks recorded by paid contributors in the Human Archive iOS app (video plus IMU and, where the phone has it, LiDAR depth; no audio)
Voice Exchange: solo and two-party voice recordings (audio only), licensed as separate datasets
post-processing into 3D hand pose, world-frame SLAM camera poses and dense step-level action labels, with bystander faces blurred
off-the-shelf (OTS) catalogue datasets and robot deployments (not new captures)

pricing.notes: No prices are published. Buyers use a contact form ('we'll send over our researcher dashboard and samples'), book a call, or email team@humanarchive.ai.

latency.typical: Not published
latency.notes: No turnaround is stated for new collection. In the app, contributors pick posted tasks and payouts follow approval.

freshness.typical_age: Ongoing collection; catalogue data is existing footage
freshness.notes: Human Archive sells from an 'OTS catalog' (its HARD-2 benchmark used 100 hours from it) and says it works 'alongside leading AI labs to scale human video/sensor data'. It publishes no order flow for collection to a buyer's spec, so how much of a buyer's data is captured after the order is not stated.

coverage.notes: Press reports put most collection in India, through 120+ partner businesses (hotels, restaurants, home services, quick commerce), with expansion to Southeast Asia and early US pilots (TechCrunch, Inc42, May 2026). Wing VC describes a network across homes, factories and warehouses in 'the U.S., India, and beyond'. The contributor app is on the US App Store; its terms exclude residents of Illinois, Texas, Washington and Oregon. Human Archive's own site lists no countries.

licensing.summary: App contributors keep ownership of their clips and grant Human Archive a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, non-exclusive, sublicensable licence to use them 'to develop, train, evaluate, and improve machine-learning and robotics models' and to include them 'in datasets Human Archive licenses to its customers for those purposes'. Customers receive data 'under a written agreement' that restricts use to the agreed purposes, prohibits re-identifying contributors and requires confidentiality (privacy policy). The buyer licence is not public; resale, buyer ownership and Human Archive's reuse of a buyer's data are not stated. Terms for footage collected through partner businesses' workers are not published. The Ego500 release is described as open-source, but no licence is shown on its page. No buyer licence is public, so whether a customer may train AI is not stated by the provider; training is the evident purpose but is set by each contract.

human.method: App contributors hold accounts, confirm they are 18 or over, and pass identity checks run by the payout providers (Stripe, Circle) where required; Human Archive receives only the verification status. Workplace footage comes from workers at partner businesses.
human.unknown: No identity method is published for partner-business workers, and no per-recording identity record is public.

application.unknown: Workplace capture uses Human Archive's own head-worn rig and app tasks are recorded in its app (nothing uploads until Submit), but no device or app attestation is documented. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Global-shutter stereo cameras with a hardware-synchronised IMU on the rig; phone camera, IMU and LiDAR in the app. Contributors confirm each recording is genuine and not altered with generative-AI or post-production tools. No signed capture; Human Archive is not on the C2PA conforming products list. Screen or generated footage is excluded only by contributor confirmation and review.

time.method: Session metadata records when a recording was collected; rig video and IMU share a hardware clock.
time.unknown: The hardware clock aligns streams to each other; no signed or independently time-stamped capture time is documented.

location.method: Collection metadata includes the environment and location; the app uses device location only if the contributor grants permission.
location.unknown: No location proof is documented, and app location is optional.

content.method: App clips: on-device hand-visibility check, about one frame a minute sent to Google's Gemini API to confirm the assigned task, human review of flagged clips and random audits. Workplace footage: a QA model cuts and filters sessions, then annotators verify clips and labels and an independent reviewer approves them (100+ annotators; 0.763 inter-annotator agreement on boundaries).
content.unknown: Acceptance rates and per-dataset QA results are not published beyond Ego500's agreement figure. Frames sent to Gemini may be reused by Google to improve its own products (privacy policy §4.3).

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual captures. HARD-1 and HARD-2 are Human Archive's own robot benchmarks of data usefulness, not checks of provenance.

delivery.basis: Human Archive says it is 'working alongside leading AI labs to scale human video/sensor data' and offers an 'OTS catalog'; it publishes no turnaround for new collection.

auth.how_to_get: Fill in the contact form at humanarchive.ai/contact.html (name, email, notes), book a call through the cal.com link on the home page, or email team@humanarchive.ai.

mcp.notes: No Human Archive server in the official MCP Registry (searched 'human-archive' and 'humanarchive', 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No public API or API docs. Buyers are offered a 'researcher dashboard and samples' after contact. humanarchive.ai returns 404 for /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.

payment.notes: No buyer payment method is published; terms are set in a written customer agreement.

consent.method: Published for the contributor app only: contributors accept a consent confirmation before each recording session, which is logged with the task and session metadata; Voice Exchange adds a one-time voice consent and a per-call consent from both parties. Video tasks must show only the contributor's own hands and task, never other people or children; recording at work needs the employer's written permission and must not capture customers. Contributors can delete their account, but approved clips are de-identified and kept in datasets.
consent.unknown: Human Archive publishes nothing on how workers at partner businesses, who wear its head-mounted rigs at work, are told about or consent to recording. Its co-founder told Inc42 that partner contracts require partners to obtain informed consent and that it is 'the partner companies' responsibility to educate their employees'; TechCrunch wrote that 'it is not clear what information Human Archive gives workers about how their footage is used'. For home-service visits, press reports say customers choose a discounted recorded visit or a full-price unrecorded one; that flow is not published by Human Archive.

worker_pay.model: App: a payout per approved submission, shown on each task. Partner workers: an hourly rate, per press reports.
worker_pay.notes: App payouts are shown in the app only, and unapproved or later-revoked submissions earn nothing. TechCrunch reports a $1/hour base rate, against ₹250–400 (about $2.63–4.20) an hour reported for other firms; the co-founder told Inc42 the average is '$1-10 per hour', which Inc42 could not verify. cards.summary: Human Archive (Human Archive, Inc., San Francisco; $8.2M seed, May 2026) collects first-person data of real work for robot learning. cards.name: Human For AI
cards.short: One pseudonymous human operator who takes agent tasks by API or MCP, free during a pilot. Signed text receipts.
cards.summary: A one-person human-in-the-loop service ("Operator 001", pseudonymous) that AI agents call over a keyless REST API or a remote MCP server. Tasks include real-world verification with photo or text evidence and local physical-world errands (visit, photograph, check, measure, observe) in the operator's undisclosed local service area, plus remote testing, review and judgment work. Every task is reviewed by the operator before acceptance; everything is free during a proof-of-concept pilot. Each delivered task carries an Ed25519-signed JWS receipt over the sha256 of the delivered text and the task's lifecycle timestamps, checkable offline against a published key set.

tasks: real-world verification with photo or text evidence (place, product, price, business, claim)
local physical-world tasks in the operator's service area: visit, photograph, deliver, check, measure, observe
on-site photos and observation of a location at a specific time
counts and documentation on site (dimensions, quantities, queue lengths, foot traffic, posted notices)
manual data collection, labeling and research
remote work: product/app testing, AI output review, human judgment, decision escalation

pricing.notes: Every service is $0 per task during the pilot (the only tier); budget_usd is accepted and ignored. No payment step exists, and tasks accepted during the pilot are never billed retroactively. Paid tiers may come later and would be announced on /pricing and in /agent.json first.

latency.typical: First response within 12 hours; typical response about 4 hours
latency.notes: Response targets are 'honest targets, not a contractual SLA'. Working hours every day 19:00-00:00 operator local time; urgent tasks by prior arrangement only. Physical errands are scheduled after acceptance, so delivery time is not stated. human.json also lists working_days Sunday-Thursday, which conflicts with 'any day of the week' elsewhere.

delivery.basis: Provider: 'First response comes within 12 hours, any day of the week; the errand itself is scheduled after acceptance.' No delivery time is stated.

freshness.typical_age: Captured after the operator accepts the task
freshness.notes: No archive. Deliverables state what was observed, what was inferred and the operator's confidence.

coverage.notes: One person. The exact service area is not published ('confirmed at task review to protect operator privacy'); wider coverage 'by arrangement'. Out-of-reach locations are declined or counter-proposed at review. English only. Remote tasks (testing, review, research) have no stated place limit but are not physical capture.

licensing.summary: Terms (effective 2026-07-19): once delivered, the deliverable is the requester's, who 'receives all rights to use, modify, and republish it, for any lawful purpose'. The operator keeps internal records but does not publish task content. Resale and AI training are not named. Privacy policy (effective 2026-07-06): task data is 'never sold, shared with advertisers, or used to train AI models'.

human.method: The service is one human operator, known only as Operator 001, who reviews and performs every task; the trust page marks 'Real, single human operator' and 'Contactable identity' as true
human.unknown: The operator is deliberately pseudonymous. Third-party identity verification (government ID through an independent provider) is listed as pending, so 'verified human' is the service's own word.

application.unknown: No capture app or device attestation is described.

camera.unknown: No live-capture rule, camera attestation or C2PA signing is described. Signed receipts cover the delivered text only, not photos or files (media hashing is an open roadmap item).

time.method: Physical-task reports come with 'timestamped photos'; each delivered task's receipt signs the task's lifecycle timestamps (submitted, accepted, delivered), verifiable against https://humanforai.dev/.well-known/jwks.json
time.unknown: The provider states the receipt timestamps are 'our own assertion, signed. Nobody outside this service witnessed them'; external anchoring is not built. How photo timestamps are produced is not stated, and the lifecycle times are not the capture time.

location.unknown: No GPS stamp, check-in or location check is described; where a photo was taken rests on the operator's report.

content.method: The operator who does the work writes the deliverable with a confidence block separating what was observed from what was inferred; the signed receipt binds the sha256 of the delivered text so later alteration is detectable
content.unknown: The receipt proves the text is unaltered and came from humanforai.dev, not that it is true; the terms call deliverables 'assistance, not guaranteed truth'. Photos and files are not covered by the receipt.

corroboration.unknown: One operator; no independent second capture or cross-check is offered.

receipt.method: Each delivered task carries a compact JWS signed with Ed25519 over the sha256 of the deliverable text and the task's lifecycle timestamps; the public key is at /.well-known/jwks.json.
receipt.unknown: The provider's own assertion ('Nobody outside this service witnessed them'); it covers the text only (photo hashing is not built), is not bound to your request or a nonce, and is not anchored externally.

sources.claim: Ed25519 JWS receipts over the deliverable hash and lifecycle timestamps; key at /.well-known/jwks.json; text only; anchoring not built

auth.how_to_get: No keys, OAuth or accounts. The protected-resource metadata states authentication_not_required: true and no authorization server exists. A task needs a real return channel: a contact_email whose domain is MX-checked, or delivery: 'status_poll' (deliverable returned as text in operator_notes; 1 such task per client per day).

endpoints.notes: Service catalog (11 task types; the catalog is examples, not limits).

endpoints.params: task_type, description (10-5000 chars) required; location_required, location_detail, deadline (ISO 8601), output_format, contact_email (required unless delivery is status_poll), delivery (email|status_poll), requester; optional Idempotency-Key header
endpoints.notes: Returns 202 with task_id and status_url. Submission is not acceptance: the operator accepts or rejects each task. Duplicates within 24 h return 409.
submitted -> accepted -> delivered, or rejected with a reason; status_history, seen_by_operator_at and an operator-set eta. Anyone holding the task_id can read its public status.

Once delivered: operator_notes (the deliverable text for status_poll tasks), receipt (compact JWS, EdDSA), deliverable_sha256 and receipt_issued_at. Email-delivery deliverables also go to contact_email.

api.sdk: npm humanforai 0.1.4 (stdio MCP proxy); PyPI humanforai 0.1.0 (client and CLI with verify-receipt); Go module github.com/humanforai/humanforai-go
api.rate_limits: Per-client hourly and daily submission caps plus a global daily pilot capacity (429 with Retry-After, resets 00:00 UTC); RateLimit headers on responses; repeat abusers blocked (403). One small test task is welcome; bulk synthetic submissions get the client blocked.

mcp.notes: Streamable HTTP, stateless, no auth. Tools: get_human_services, submit_human_task, check_task_status, message_human_operator. Registry latest is v0.1.4 with the remote URL and the npm stdio package.

api.notes: Messages to the operator: POST /api/v1/messages (reply_to email or an https webhook URL; replies signed with HMAC-SHA256) and a pollable thread with a one-time access token. Receipts are issued only for tasks delivered from 2026-07-20, and are re-issued if the operator edits a deliverable. The receipt is a compact JWS over deliverable_sha256 and lifecycle timestamps, not the detached RFC 8785 receipt of the irlpls standard.

payment.notes: Nothing to pay during the pilot: no payment step, invoice or card. The service says it never asks for payment, credentials or accounts, and that any such request is not from it.

requester.checks: No account or identity check. Each task needs a working return channel (MX-checked email, or the status-poll path capped at one task per client per day). The operator reviews every task before acceptance and rejects illegal, deceptive, unsafe and privacy-invasive work, explicitly including surveillance of individuals, stalking and doxxing. Rate limits, duplicate detection and a blocklist (on a salted hash of the caller's network address) handle abuse. The terms bind an agent's principal to what the agent submits.
requester.unknown: Who the requester is is not checked beyond the return channel; screening rests on one person's review of the task description.

Homepage: '1 verified human', first response < 12 hours, free for now, task flow, report/photos/structured JSON delivery

Pricing: pilot is the only tier at $0 per task; budget_usd ignored; never billed retroactively; paid tiers would be announced first
No authentication of any kind; anonymous access is the only method; error codes 400/403/404/409/429, never 401
RFC 9728 metadata: authentication_not_required true, no authorization servers, no scopes
Receipt signing key: Ed25519, kid receipts-2026-07, alg EdDSA

cards.name: ICEYE
cards.summary: ICEYE runs a large synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through cloud and at night. Its Tasking API v2 is for customers with a contract. They can get a price, check feasibility and task a new capture centred on a point. The capture window is at least 24 hours wide and ends within 14 days. The customer picks the imaging mode (Strip, Scan, Spot, Dwell and their variants), the priority, and how soon products are available after acquisition: 8, 3 or 1 hour.

tasks: task a new SAR capture centred on a point (or anywhere covering an AOI circle, with aoiRadiusMeters) in an acquisition window at least 24 h wide, ending within 14 days
imaging modes: STRIPMAP, SCAN, SCAN_WIDE, SPOTLIGHT, SPOTLIGHT_EXTENDED_AREA, SPOTLIGHT_FINE, SPOTLIGHT_EXTENDED_DWELL (and _FINE, _PRECISE), as allowed by contract
price a task before ordering (amount and currency, minor units), on contracts with a pricing plan
feasibility check for a list of candidate tasks (FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE, and budget fit where priced)
priority BACKGROUND or COMMERCIAL (stated >90% statistical reliability)
product availability SLA: 8 h (default), 3 h, or 1 h in certain regions after acquisition
product types GRD, GRD-COG, SLC, SLC-COG, QLK, SICD, SIDD, CSI, VID as the contract and mode allow
Object Detection and Identification derivative ODI (formerly Detect & Classify; replaces DC-ATR, which is removed 2026-11-15) on Dwell modes and SPOTLIGHT_FINE, where enabled
planned and actual imaging time and footprint via the task scene endpoint
delivery to SFTP or S3 locations, and webhook notifications on task changes

pricing.model: per task, set by contract (region, priority, imaging mode, SLA, exclusivity, EULA)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published, not free. Each contract has a fixed pricing model, and the same task can cost different amounts under different contracts. GET /tasking/v2/price returns the price in minor currency units, but only on contracts with a pricing plan (hasPricingPlan). The docs' example of 529199 USD minor units (about $5,292) is only an example. Cancelling is free within 1 hour of submission or more than 72 h before the window. After that it costs 10% of the order value at 72-48 h, 20% at 48-24 h and 100% under 24 h, and a task cannot be cancelled once the window has started.

latency.typical: Products available 8 h after acquisition by default, 3 h or 1 h with a faster SLA; acquisition happens somewhere in a window of at least 24 h that cannot start immediately
latency.notes: The minimum lead time before collection is 12 h for COMMERCIAL priority and 24 h for BACKGROUND (Product Specification, Table 3-2). The scheduler decides ACTIVE or REJECTED within 20 minutes of submission. The SLA counts from the end of acquisition and leaves out download or delivery time. Non-SLA products usually follow within about an hour, with no guarantee. The 1 h SLA is Commercial priority only, needs a feasibility pass, is not available for Dwell modes, and is 'guaranteed' for over 80% of feasible tasks.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes, contract and scheduling)
coverage.notes: SAR works through cloud and at night. Prices vary by region with demand. The contract decides which regions, imaging modes, priorities and exclusivity you may use, and the 1-hour SLA applies only in certain regions.

licensing.summary: Each task picks a STANDARD or GOVERNMENT EULA, and the full terms are in the customer's contract. ICEYE US publishes its EULA (updated 2 December 2025). It grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable licence for the End User's internal use only. It forbids distributing, sublicensing, selling, publishing or making products public, and forbids commercial use. ICEYE keeps all title to products and to the parts of them inside the customer's derivatives. 'Data Derivatives' are outputs that keep no SAR pixels or sensor or ephemeris data and cannot be reversed back to them. The customer owns these outright and may use them for any purpose, credited 'Powered by ICEYE'. AI or ML training is not mentioned. Exclusivity: PUBLIC images go into ICEYE's public catalog 14 days after acquisition, where other customers can buy them. PRIVATE images are withheld from that catalog. The Product Specification says permanently, and the API docs say for the contract's agreed period.

freshness.typical_age: Captured in your window, available hours after acquisition
freshness.notes: ICEYE also sells past images from its archive catalog, where new images appear at least 14 days after acquisition. irlpls lists ICEYE only for new tasked captures.

auth.how_to_get: ICEYE issues a TOKEN_URL, CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET during onboarding on a contract. To start onboarding, fill in the SAR data contact form at https://www.iceye.com/contact/sar-data. POST grant_type=client_credentials to the TOKEN_URL with HTTP Basic auth (client id and secret) to get a bearer token that lasts 3600 s. v2 does not support the older username and password flow.

endpoints.notes: Your contracts: allowed imaging modes, priorities, SLAs, exclusivity, delivery locations, start/end dates, and hasPricingPlan.
Budget: consolidatedSpent, onHold, optional spendLimit (minor units). Only for contracts with a pricing plan; available funds = spendLimit - consolidatedSpent - onHold.

endpoints.params: contractID, pointOfInterest[lat], pointOfInterest[lon], imagingMode; optional acquisitionWindow, exclusivity, priority, sla, eula, incidenceAngle, lookSide, passDirection, reference
endpoints.notes: Returns {amount, currency}, amount in minor units; 403 if the parameters are not allowed by the contract or the contract has no pricing plan.

endpoints.params: array of tasks with the createTask fields (all with the same priority)
endpoints.notes: Returns FEASIBLE / INFEASIBLE per task; also checks budget when the contract has a pricing plan.

endpoints.params: contractID, pointOfInterest {lat, lon}, acquisitionWindow {start, end}, imagingMode; optional reference, priority, sla, exclusivity, eula, incidenceAngle, lookSide, passDirection, aoiRadiusMeters, productTypes, derivativeProductTypes, deliveries, notifications
endpoints.notes: Returns 201 with status RECEIVED; the scheduler sets ACTIVE or REJECTED within 20 minutes. 400 ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS if the contract budget is too low. No idempotency key is documented; the free-text reference field can tag tasks.
Status RECEIVED, ACTIVE, FULFILLED (SLA products ready), DONE (all products), or terminal REJECTED, CANCELED, FAILED.
Planned (ACTIVE) or actual (FULFILLED/DONE) imaging time, incidence angle, look side, pass direction and footprint.

endpoints.params: limit, cursor, contractID, createdAfter, createdBefore and filters
endpoints.notes: Your tasks.
STAC-like items with signed download URLs that expire after 1 hour; available once the task is FULFILLED or DONE. /products/{productType} returns one type.
STAC items; use only to fetch metadata for your own tasked captures (collections incl. private/tasking), not as an archive route.

api.rate_limits: Not published in the pages read.
api.notes: To cancel, PATCH /tasking/v2/tasks/{taskID} with {"status": "CANCELED"} while the task is RECEIVED or ACTIVE (charges in pricing.notes). Webhooks are registered with the Notifications API. Delivery to SFTP or S3 uses config IDs set up by ICEYE. Every tasking request needs a contractID. The API docs show paths without the /api prefix, which is part of base_url. ICEYE publishes an open-source demo app on GitHub (github.com/iceye-ltd), but no official SDK was found.

mcp.notes: No ICEYE MCP server is in the official MCP Registry (search 'iceye' returned 0 servers, 2026-10-26).

human.unknown: ICEYE satellites capture the images, not people. Whether a person reviews a capture before delivery is not stated.

application.unknown: No public signing or checksum scheme for delivered products was found. Download URLs are signed for access only, not to prove where the content came from.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Products come from ICEYE's own SAR satellites in a stated imaging mode, with sensor and orbit metadata. Which satellite and sensor took the image is ICEYE's word. No cryptographic provenance is published.

time.method: The task scene reports the actual imaging start and end, and product items carry start_datetime and end_datetime inside the requested window
time.unknown: No independent or signed timestamp. How acquisition times are validated is not documented.

location.method: Tasks target a WGS 84 point. Products are geolocated using refined orbits and calibrated against ground-surveyed corner-reflector sites. ICEYE gives a fleet worst-case RMSE of 6 m, and its June-November 2025 campaign at Rosamond (521 images) found mean errors under 0.4 m.

delivery.basis: From the Create Task and Product Specification docs: products are available SLA_8H (default), SLA_3H or SLA_1H after acquisition. payment.notes: The contract has a spend limit, and a task fails with ERR_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS if it would go over. Under the ICEYE US direct-sales terms (v1.0, April 2021), fees are invoiced every two weeks and due within 30 days, in euros unless the order says otherwise. ICEYE has a separate invoicing process, and no card or agent payment rail was found.

requester.checks: Customers are onboarded by ICEYE's COSP team and contract with ICEYE, and contracts set what each customer may task. Under the US direct-sales terms, ICEYE may accept or reject any order at its sole discretion. Orders may be subject to government regulatory review, and ICEYE can modify or terminate an order to comply. Customers must follow export controls and must not distribute products to sanctioned parties. The EULA choice (STANDARD or GOVERNMENT) depends on the type of end user.
requester.unknown: What due diligence ICEYE runs on new customers during onboarding (KYC, end-use or target screening) is not published.

cards.name: LXT (clickworker)
cards.summary: AI data company LXT, which agreed to buy the German crowd platform clickworker in December 2024 and now issues clickworker's North American terms. Its crowd photographs and films to a brief: custom image and video datasets (people, pets, products, scenes, documents) shot at home, at a nearby location with the clickworker smartphone app, or in a studio; and store checks, where workers visit listed shops, photograph shelves and displays with geo data and fill in checklists. Projects are run by LXT's managed service. The clickworker Marketplace API v2 (HTTP Basic auth, access through support) can create tasks, track them, fetch results and accept or reject them; its standard products are surveys, sentiment and iFrame tasks, and photo work is set up as a custom product.

tasks: custom image collection: people and poses, pets and animals, products and objects, scenes and environments, documents and screens
custom video collection: human activity, pets, object interaction, indoor and outdoor scenes, facial and body movement
three settings: remote (at home by PC or phone app), mobile on-site (a nearby location, by smartphone app), in-person (studio, client premises or LXT data collection centre, with a moderator)
store checks and display audits: workers visit listed stores and photograph shelves, displays and promotions with the clickworker app, uploading with geo position, store name and address
on-site mystery checks with photo, video or written documentation
API: create tasks from templates (Survey, Sentiment, ExternalForm/iFrame; custom products set up by clickworker Operations), track status, fetch results, accept or reject, count workers near a point

pricing.model: Custom quote (managed); per-task worker payment you set (API/self-service)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means unknown, not free. LXT quotes image collection by number and type of images, contributor requirements, regions and metadata, and video by scope and turnaround. clickworker's FAQ says managed costs depend on time and quality requirements, with an individual offer per project. Through the API you set the worker payment per task in cents (e.g. external_form_payment); clickworker adds a basic payment surcharge (rate not published) and typically a 40% surcharge on bonuses. Self-service fees are shown on the platform when the order is submitted.

latency.typical: Store checks: 'often within hours'. Datasets: not published.
latency.notes: clickworker's store-check page says 'Results often within hours, not days'. LXT's dataset projects run briefing, setup, pilot, then full-scale capture, and LXT only says 'high throughput rates with managed service and direct app upload'. The API docs say completion 'will take some time, depending on the complexity of the work and availability of workers'.

coverage.notes: LXT cites image and video collection in 150+ countries and 1,000+ locales with 10M+ contributors; clickworker's homepage says its workforce is in 136 countries. A published store-check case study ran in DE, FR, UK, IT, ES, TR and RU with 300 to 800 stores per country. The API targets tasks by ISO country code and can count workers within a radius (minimum 10 km) or bounding box, so density near an address can be checked before ordering, with an account.

licensing.summary: clickworker's North American self-service terms (LXT AI Inc., effective 30 March 2026, §8) give the client, upon full payment, 'a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use task results for its internal business purposes'; the same §8 bars reselling or sublicensing the Platform itself; the terms do not mention AI training, resale of results, or LXT using client data for its own models. The rest-of-world client terms (clickworker Germany GmbH, 2012) say nothing about rights in results; managed projects run under an individual contract. Workers grant clickworker unlimited rights of use in what they produce (worker GTC §7). LXT offers mutual NDAs and markets its collected images as 'fully consented'.

human.method: Workers must be 18+, give truthful personal data and hold one account each (no alter egos); clickworker may require evidence that the data is correct before activating an account. LXT says contributors are 'vetted' and selected to the project's requirements.
human.unknown: Whether an identity document is checked for every worker is not stated; the terms only reserve the right to ask for evidence.

application.method: On-site work uses the clickworker app for Android and iOS.
application.unknown: No check that the app or device is genuine or unmodified is documented.

camera.unknown: Camera type can be included as metadata, but no check against imported, screen-captured or generated media is described.

time.unknown: A timestamp 'can be included' as metadata; how it is set and whether it can be trusted is not documented.

location.method: In the store-check case study, workers photograph the store front 'with geo data' and upload shelf pictures 'with geo position, the business address and the store name'.
location.unknown: How the geo position is captured and whether it is checked against the store is not described; geolocation is not mentioned for dataset collection.

content.method: LXT: multi-layer QA with programmatic checks, gold tasks, peer review, human review and compliance validation. Store checks: optional clickworker internal verification of the pictures. API: optional review jobs, then the customer accepts or rejects each result (buyoff).
content.unknown: Review criteria and error rates are not published.

corroboration.method: Peer review of submissions by other contributors; on the API, a separate content-review job can precede the customer's buyoff.
corroboration.unknown: Whether peer review applies to every capture project and what it checks is not described. Reviewers share the platform and operator, so this is not independent confirmation.

auth.how_to_get: HTTP Basic auth with your clickworker customer email and password. Ask clickworker support for API access (https://www.clickworker.com/contact-for-customers/, helpdesk@clickworker.com). Sandbox: https://api-sandbox.clickworker.com. The irlpls adapter reads CLICKWORKER_CREDENTIALS as 'email:password'.
The OpenAPI file declares an access_token query parameter for Asset Library endpoints only; how to obtain one is not documented.

endpoints.notes: Products available to your account (standard: Survey, Sentiment, ExternalForm/iFrame).
Counts workers in an area before launching location-based tasks.
Creates a task from a task template (POST /customer/task_templates first). Optional notification callback URL for TASK_COMPLETED, TASK_TIMEDOUT and CUSTOMER_INPUT_REQUIRED.
States: created, queued, running, finished, timedout, cancelled, feedback (awaiting buyoff).
Results inline. Accept or reject with PUT /customer/tasks/{taskId}/accept or /reject.
Orders group tasks for billing.

api.sdk: None. OpenAPI 3.0.3 file at https://www.clickworker.com/mpapi/cw-mp-api-v2.yaml with curl, JavaScript, PHP and Ruby samples. Customer portal: marketplace.clickworker.com.
api.rate_limits: Not published. The North American terms forbid exceeding 'documented rate limits'; pages hold at most 50 results.

mcp.notes: No clickworker or LXT server in the official MCP Registry. www.lxt.ai exposes an undocumented WordPress MCP endpoint (wp-json/mcp/mcp-oauth-server, OAuth with PKCE S256, scope 'mcp'); it appears to belong to the website and is not documented as a way to order data.

api.notes: Version 2.0.42. Content-Type and Accept must be application/json. The sandbox has no active workers. Photo collection and store checks are not standard API products; clickworker Operations can configure custom products, and store-check results can be delivered by API. Account balance via GET /customer (balance, reserved amount, credit limit).

freshness.typical_age: Captured for your order
freshness.notes: LXT also sells off-the-shelf datasets; only custom collection is described here.

delivery.basis: clickworker store-check page: 'Fast turnaround – Results often within hours, not days.' No turnaround is published for LXT image or video datasets, which start with a briefing and a pilot.

payment.notes: Self-service: top up a prepaid account before sending an order; North American terms say fees are payable in advance and may need pre-funding or wallet balances. Managed service: invoices at the end of each month. The API reads the balance but has no top-up endpoint.

requester.checks: North American terms: business accounts only (consumers not permitted), accurate and complete information, no impersonating another business; LXT accepts each order and may refuse or modify tasks for compliance reasons. Rest-of-world terms: clients may use the platform only once clickworker connects and authorizes them, and each project needs clickworker's binding acceptance.
requester.unknown: Whether LXT verifies the business's identity, or screens store-check or mystery-check targets, is not documented.

cards.name: Mapilio
cards.short: Contributor street-level imagery licensed by road-km; price by quote.
cards.summary: Street-level imagery platform. Contributors upload geotagged photos from phones, action cameras and 360 cameras; the site reports about 20.3M image records in 72 countries and territories (snapshot 28 September 2026, not a live count). Mapilio sells annual licences priced by the road-network length of an area (packages from 1,000 to 100,000 km, price not published) and separately licenses automatically extracted Object Detections and Map Features. Paid capture jobs are a planned marketplace, not available yet. Imagery is existing contributor capture, not made to order.

tasks: license street-level imagery for an area by road-km on an annual plan
license object detections (items visible in images) for an area
license map features (estimated object positions or geometry derived from imagery, e.g. traffic signs)
host private imagery on the Mapilio platform (monthly plans by number of images)

delivery.basis: Pricing page: contact Mapilio with the area, data type, output format and integration needed; this leads to a quote covering availability, licensing and pricing. No turnaround is published.

pricing.model: annual subscription by road-network length; quote
pricing.unit: per year, by road-km package (1,000 to 100,000 km)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 is a schema placeholder, not a price: no amount is published. The pricing page shows no numeric price (price field blank, '1,000 km road coverage' label). 'If your shooting is under 1000km, you can contact us to get a free trial.' Private hosting is on monthly plans by number of images, and 'automatically extracted data needs to be licensed separately'. Vendor figure: '1000km corresponds to approximately 200,000 pictures' at a five-metre distance calculation.

payment.notes: No payment methods are published on the pricing page; terms are agreed through the quote.

latency.typical: Not published; quote-based
latency.notes: No delivery or turnaround time is stated; 'We will confirm what is available for your area before promising a delivery date.'

freshness.typical_age: Depends on when a contributor last captured the place
freshness.notes: Existing contributor imagery. No way to order new capture today; the paid capture marketplace is 'a planned product, not a currently available earnings program'.

regions: Contributor-driven; 72 countries and territories in the stored country summary, density uneven
coverage.notes: About page (snapshot 28 September 2026): 20,328,577 image records, 72 countries and territories, 281 uploading accounts. The page says this is not a live coverage count and gives no kilometre figure. The pricing page lists no coverage and says the team confirms availability for your area before promising delivery. No country list is published, so no areas are set.

licensing.summary: Public imagery is published under CC BY-SA, which licences pages say permits commercial use subject to attribution and ShareAlike. The licences page says the imagery policy 'does not specify a blanket license for all AI-generated detections' and to contact Mapilio before redistribution; the pricing page warns 'do not assume the imagery license grants access to every extracted dataset or service', and that dataset-specific terms are confirmed in the quote. Terms: users 'do NOT retain all rights' in User Content and grant Mapilio a nonexclusive, royalty-free, irrevocable, worldwide licence; reselling the Mapilio Services is prohibited unless permitted in separate writing; data mining, robots and scraping not approved by Mapilio are barred. Terms expressly allow extracting information from Mapilio images for OpenStreetMap. Neither the terms nor the licences page mention AI or machine-learning training, so ai_training and resale are not set.

human.unknown: Nothing documented about whether contributors are identified or distinct real people; the site reports 281 uploading accounts.

application.unknown: No app or device attestation is documented. Uploads come from the Mapilio app, the Mapilio Kit CLI and a desktop uploader.

camera.unknown: No signed capture is documented. Mapilio was not checked against the C2PA conforming products list.

time.unknown: Not documented whether or how capture time is verified; the terms and pricing pages say nothing on this.

location.unknown: Not documented whether positions are authenticated. The pricing page says detections may not be at the image's location and map-feature positions are estimated.

content.method: Automated face and licence-plate blurring with a report control for missed cases (home page)
content.unknown: Blurring is privacy, not authenticity. The pricing page says detections show what is in an image, not necessarily where, and that classes and accuracy depend on model, imagery and GPS quality.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-checking of individual images is documented.

auth.how_to_get: Not documented publicly. The pricing page says Mapilio confirms 'the available API or delivery method and the dataset-specific terms' after you describe your needs; the developer page lists APIs for images, sequences, changesets, map objects, image detections and users but gives no base URL or auth method.

api.notes: docs.mapilio.com returned HTTP 502 on every attempt on 2026-11-04, so endpoints, base URL, auth and rate limits could not be read. No first-party MCP server found in the MCP Registry.

access.notes: Order is by contacting Mapilio for a quote. Terms bar 'data mining, robots or similar data gathering or extraction methods not approved by Mapilio', so automated bulk access is not open. automation_allowed is left unset.

sources.claim: Annual plans by road-km (1,000 to 100,000 km), price not shown, free trial under 1,000 km, optional private hosting, detections vs map features, dataset-specific terms and API confirmed in quote, marketplace planned not available
Terms: broad user-content licence, reselling Services prohibited, scraping/data mining barred, OSM extraction allowed, no AI/ML training mention
CC BY-SA public imagery incl. commercial use; no blanket licence for AI-generated detections; no statement on AI training or resale
About 20.3M image records, 72 countries and territories, 281 uploading accounts (snapshot 28 September 2026); capture tools; blurring; planned marketplace
Developer page lists APIs for images, sequences, changesets, map objects, image detections and users; no base URL or auth stated
No MCP server listed in the official registry

cards.name: Mapillary
cards.short: An archive of crowdsourced street-level photos.
cards.summary: Meta-owned archive of crowdsourced, geotagged street-level photos and panoramas (more than 3 billion images, contributors in 190 countries), searchable through the Mapillary Graph API by small bounding box, by point and radius (up to 50 m), or by capture date, plus machine-detected map features (traffic signs and points) and per-image detections. It returns existing imagery only: you cannot commission a new capture.

tasks: search existing street-level images by bbox (< 0.01 deg square) and capture date
find the best image near a point (lat/lng, radius up to 50 m, ranked by proximity, recency and 360°)

fetch image thumbnails (256/512/1024/2048 px and original) and metadata (captured_at, geometry, computed_geometry, compass angle, panorama flag, camera make/model, creator, organization, quality_score, on_foot)
search machine-detected map features (traffic signs, points) by bbox, type and first/last seen date, with the images each was derived from
per-image object detections (segmentation polygons with class values)
coverage and map-feature vector tiles

delivery.basis: Archive only: no new capture can be ordered.

pricing.notes: Mapillary's platform page says imagery is accessible in the cloud 'for free'. No pricing page exists (www.mapillary.com/pricing returns 'We couldn't find the page'). Access needs a client token from an app registered in the developer dashboard. Commercial use is limited to the purposes in Terms Section 12 (see licensing).

payment.notes: No payment is published or required: the API is free with a client token. No payment methods are listed.

latency.typical: Seconds per API call (search returns existing imagery); no turnaround for new capture because none can be ordered
latency.notes: No official API latency figure found. How long after upload an image becomes searchable (processing, blurring) was not confirmed.

freshness.typical_age: Varies widely by place: from recent to many years old; depends on when a contributor last drove or walked there
freshness.notes: Every image carries captured_at, and search can filter with start_captured_at / end_captured_at, so an agent can reject stale results. There is no way to request fresh capture of a location.

regions: Global (wherever contributors have uploaded imagery; density uneven)
coverage.notes: Coverage is whatever contributors have captured. Mapillary's about page says contributors in 190 countries and more than two billion images; its home page says more than 3,000,000,000 images. Coverage vector tiles (mly1_public, mly1_computed_public) show where imagery exists. Terms Section 22 bars use from US-embargoed jurisdictions. No per-region density figures were found.

licensing.summary: Terms (effective 15 February 2024) Section 3: other users' content is under CC BY-SA 4.0 unless Mapillary indicates otherwise; some data sets may carry other terms such as CC BY-NC-SA, and those licence terms win where they conflict with the Terms. Section 12: commercial use is allowed only for (i) 'improvement, training, and development of products, services, maps, studies, platforms, websites, applications, software, algorithms, datasets, solutions, or technologies' and (ii) providing services to clients, and requires safeguards against re-identification or unblurring and a process to report incidents to vendor-incident@meta.com. Section 5 bans selling or reselling the Mapillary Services without a separate written agreement, unapproved data mining or scraping, re-identification or unblurring, and use for real-time navigation or autonomous vehicle control. Section 11: apps must materially supplement Mapillary, not merely redistribute content; downloaded images and API-derived data must show the Mapillary logo and link back. Section 13 allows use for OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps contributions. Content is owned by Mapillary or its licensors (contributors keep their rights), so a user gets a licence, not ownership. Resale is left unset: the Terms ban reselling the Services, but the CC BY-SA licence on user content allows commercial redistribution under share-alike, and the Terms say the licence wins in a conflict. The Terms never say 'AI' or 'machine learning', so AI training is not stated; §12's 'training ... algorithms, datasets' wording suggests commercial training use is permitted, and CC BY-SA share-alike applies to derivatives.

human.method: Each image exposes creator (username and id) and, where affiliated, an organization
human.unknown: Nothing documents whether a contributor is a distinct, real or identified person; uploads also come from organizations and professional rigs

application.unknown: No public attestation of which app or uploader produced an image; Mapillary accepts uploads from any camera and from desktop and command-line uploaders

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Image metadata includes camera make, model and camera_type, filterable by make and model with a bbox. Make, model and altitude come from contributed metadata (the docs cite Exif for altitude and orientation) with no documented hardware attestation; they can be wrong or edited. Mapillary is not on the C2PA conforming products list

time.method: Each image has a captured_at timestamp, filterable in search
time.unknown: Where the timestamp comes from (device clock, Exif or GPS) and whether Mapillary checks it are not documented

location.method: Each image has its original geometry and compass_angle, plus computed_geometry and computed_compass_angle from Mapillary's structure-from-motion processing
location.unknown: Original GPS can be noisy or edited; how computed positions are derived and how far they can be trusted is not specified beyond pointers to OpenSfM

content.method: Faces and licence plates are automatically blurred (privacy, not authenticity); each image has a predicted visual quality_score
content.unknown: No documented checks for staged, edited or synthetic images. Blurring changes the content and can miss faces and plates (a 2018 company blog reports 99.9% detection)

corroboration.method: Map features are derived from multiple detections in multiple images (first_seen_at / last_seen_at, with the contributing images listed)
corroboration.unknown: Nothing cross-checks an individual image. Dense places may have many overlapping images an agent can compare itself; sparse places may have one

auth.how_to_get: Register an app at https://www.mapillary.com/dashboard/developers to get a client access token (needs a Mapillary account). The header form works for Entity API calls.
Same client token sent as ?access_token=XXX. Preferred for vector tiles; strongly discouraged for user access tokens.

Authorization code flow for user tokens: send the user to https://www.mapillary.com/connect?client_id=...&response_type=code, then POST the code to https://graph.mapillary.com/token with Authorization: OAuth <client secret>. Tokens expire (example expires_in 9000 s) and are refreshed at the same endpoint. Needs a pre-registered app; no self-registration, PKCE or RFC 9728 metadata is documented.

endpoints.params: bbox=left,bottom,right,top (< 0.01 deg square), start_captured_at, end_captured_at (ISO 8601), limit (max/default 2000), creator_username, is_pano (needs bbox or creator_username), make, model (bbox only), organization_id, sequence_ids, fields=id,captured_at,geometry,computed_geometry,compass_angle,is_pano,thumb_256_url,thumb_1024_url,thumb_2048_url,thumb_original_url,creator,quality_score,on_foot,...
endpoints.notes: Core call: existing images of a place and time window. Paging (after cursor) works only with creator_username. Thumbnails are URLs in the response.

endpoints.params: lat, lng, radius (metres, default and max 50), limit (default 1, max 100), fields=...
endpoints.notes: Image radius search (added 2 April 2026): returns the 'best' images near a point by proximity, recency and 360° preference. Cannot be combined with bbox, tile, s2, image_ids or sequence_ids.
Single image metadata and thumbnail URLs. Several entities of one type at once: GET /?ids=ID1,ID2

endpoints.params: bbox (< 0.01 deg square), object_values (wildcards, comma-separated), start_first_seen_at, end_first_seen_at, start_last_seen_at, end_last_seen_at, limit (max 2000), fields=id,object_value,object_type,geometry,aligned_direction,first_seen_at,last_seen_at,images
endpoints.notes: Machine-detected map objects such as traffic signs; GET /:map_feature_id fetches one, and fields=images lists the images it was derived from
Object detections in an image; geometry is a base64-encoded vector-tile polygon (extent 4096). Also /:map_feature_id/detections
Image ids in a capture sequence; fields param not honored
Coverage vector tiles (Mapbox Vector Tile spec; layers overview, sequence, image). Also mly1_computed_public, mly_map_feature_point and mly_map_feature_traffic_sign

api.rate_limits: Entity APIs 60,000/min per app; Search APIs 10,000/min per app; tiles 50,000/day. Over the limit the Graph API returns 'Application request limit reached' (code 4); tiles return 4xx. Terms Section 11 lets Mapillary throttle or revoke client_ids.
api.sdk: mapillary-python-sdk (https://github.com/mapillary/mapillary-python-sdk; the docs recommend it for areas larger than the bbox limit); MapillaryJS viewer; embed iframe at https://www.mapillary.com/embed?image_key=IMAGE_ID

mcp.community: Third-party wrapper in the official MCP Registry, not run by Mapillary: io.github.pipeworx-io/mapillary (v0.1.3, remote https://gateway.pipeworx.io/mapillary/mcp).
mcp.notes: No first-party Mapillary MCP server found.

api.notes: All requests to graph.mapillary.com and tiles.mapillary.com need a token; a keyless call returns 'Invalid OAuth 2.0 Access Token' (code 190) and tiles return 403. Entity endpoints have only limited bbox search; the docs expect vector tiles for spatial filtering at scale.

access.notes: Terms §5 allow access only through published interfaces; documented limits per app are 60,000 per minute (Entity API), 10,000 per minute (Search) and 50,000 per day (tiles).

rate_limit.notes: Search APIs, per app; entity APIs 60,000 per minute; tiles 50,000 per day. Over the limit: 'Application request limit reached' (code 4).

sources.claim: Base URLs graph.mapillary.com and tiles.mapillary.com; auth via Authorization: OAuth header or access_token query param; client token from developer dashboard; OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with read/write/upload scopes, token exchange and refresh

/images search params, bbox < 0.01 deg square (since 16 January 2026), image fields (thumbnails 256/512/1024/2048/original, captured_at, geometry, computed_geometry, make, model, creator, organization, quality_score, on_foot), paging only with creator_username
Image radius search (lat, lng, radius max 50 m, limit max 100), added 2 April 2026

mapillary-python-sdk recommended for large areas

cards.name: Mecka
cards.short: Robot-learning data to order: paid people record first-person video, motion and touch with Mecka's own sensor kit.

tasks: commission task-specific collection of human demonstrations in homes and commercial environments
egocentric (first-person) video of everyday tasks such as cooking, cleaning, making coffee or fixing cars
capture with Mecka-made multi-sensor kit: camera caps, a sensor hub and tactile gloves that record grip force
capture at recruited businesses (e.g. bakeries, a PCB manufacturing line)
post-processing into motion tracking, hand pose, 3D reconstruction and aligned sensor streams
dataset access, model evaluations and on-site robot deployments (not captures)

cards.name: Amazon Mechanical Turk
cards.summary: CLOSED. Amazon's crowdsourcing marketplace for small paid online tasks (HITs), with an AWS API (CreateHIT, ListAssignmentsForHIT, and others via boto3). mturk.com states the service permanently closed on September 30, 2026; HIT creation and task completion ended that day. Before closure it was built for remote, browser-based work. Workers could be filtered by country or ISO 3166-2 subdivision through the Worker_Locale qualification, but no public source describes sending workers to a specific physical place or verifying where or when a photo was taken. Listed for the record only. An agent cannot use it.

tasks: online microtasks (HITs) built with QuestionForm, HTMLQuestion or ExternalQuestion

The 40 percent rate for 10+ assignments took effect on 2015-07-22 (SPSP). Wikipedia gives one cent as the minimum task payment. The pricing is moot since the closure.

latency.notes: Requesters set HIT lifetime (LifetimeInSeconds) and per-assignment time limit (AssignmentDurationInSeconds). No typical fill time was published. HIT submission ended on 2026-09-30, and unsubmitted HITs expired automatically.

The Worker_Locale qualification could restrict a HIT to ISO 3166 countries or ISO 3166-2 subdivisions such as US-WA. That was a worker-profile attribute, not proof of physical presence. No city-level targeting was documented, and Amazon published no list of covered countries.

licensing.summary: Under the Participation Agreement (last updated 2020-03-25, still shown on mturk.com), work product from Tasks is a work made for hire for the Requester, ownership vests in the Requester, and Workers waive moral rights (s. 3.3). Section 3.7 says task content Requesters upload and work product they receive may be retained and used to improve the Site and other machine learning related products and services of Amazon or its affiliates. The agreement does not mention resale of work product or AI training by requesters, so those keys are omitted. The Acceptable Use Policy prohibited collecting or deriving workers' personally identifiable information, posting third parties' personal information, and HITs requiring registration elsewhere. It does not address physical-location or photo tasks.

cards.name: Mundane
cards.summary: Agent-to-human marketplace ("v0.1 prototype", terms v0.2, early access) run by Mundane, Inc. An AI agent searches for nearby workers who passed a Stripe Identity ID and selfie check, posts a task that is screened against an Acceptable Use Policy, offers it to one worker, and holds the pay plus fee in escrow from a prepaid USD wallet until it accepts the proof. Each capability has typed proof requirements (photo, geo check-in, confirmation code, signature). Callable through a REST API, a hosted MCP server with 38 tools (bearer key) or the mundane-mcp stdio package; an agent gets a key by self-serve API signup. Interactive tasks let the agent see still frames from the worker's phone camera and guide them live.
cards.short: Agent-to-human marketplace: ID-verified people do photo checks, errands and queues; escrow.

tasks: photo documentation: visit a location and take photos meeting stated criteria (photo, geo check-in by default)
in-person errand: pickup, drop-off, brief in-person interaction (photo, confirmation code, geo check-in)
delivery pickup: pick up an item and deliver it to a named recipient (photo, geo check-in, signature)
wait in line and obtain a stamped or signed token (photo, confirmation code)
check something in person: is it open, is it in stock, what does the notice say
interactive task: still frames from the worker's phone camera while the agent guides them live
chained jobs: 2-5 workers in turn with an item handed on at each step

pricing.notes: from_usd 0 because there is no published price: each worker sets a per-task ask rate and an offer must be at or above it (interactive tasks: at least the worker's interactive rate). The platform fee is added on top and disclosed in the offer response. A cancellation after a worker accepts can owe the worker a fee, disclosed on cancelling. Searching for workers is free (needs a key, no funded wallet). In disputes Mundane keeps the platform fee. USD only.

latency.typical: Not stated; set by the task deadline and whether a nearby worker accepts the offer
latency.notes: The provider says of offers to workers: "Not yet, in most places. Mundane is new", and the Terms guarantee no minimum number of offers. Offers expire after 24 hours by default (minimum 5 minutes). The only published run is a founder demo (Austin, 9 August 2026) in which the founder was both requester and worker: posted to completed in about 55 minutes. After submission the agent reviews proof; a rejection goes to Mundane's human review queue. Proof photo images are deleted 30 days after upload once the task is settled, so fetch them before then.

coverage.notes: Workers can sign up in the US, UK, Canada, Switzerland and the EEA ("the places where Stripe can both verify ID and pay out"). No worker counts are published, and the provider says offers are rare "in most places"; an empty search is a normal result. The EEA is expanded in areas to its 30 member countries.

licensing.summary: Terms (v0.2; the page header says last updated 20 October 2026 but its footer says 10 July 2026): users keep any ownership they have in submitted content, including worker proof, and grant Mundane a nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to host, copy, process and display it "only as reasonably needed to provide, secure, support, and improve the service and comply with law". The Terms do not say whether the requester gets ownership, resale or AI-training rights in a worker's proof photos, and do not mention AI or ML training. On a task posted as shareable, the worker licenses Mundane and the requester to publish up to six proof photos in a public Conclave page, without the worker's name or exact location. For interactive tasks the agent and principal "may keep copies" of frames but must not use them to identify, track or profile anyone. The AUP limits photography to public or permission-granted spaces with no specific identifiable individuals as subjects.

human.method: Every worker passes Stripe Identity (government-ID document check plus liveness-matched selfie) and an 18+ age check before accepting a paid task; a keyed one-way value from verified name and date of birth flags duplicate or ban-evasion accounts for human review
human.unknown: The check binds an account to a verified person, not a task: nothing documented shows the verified person is the one who did the work. The provider says verification "is not a guarantee of a person's qualifications, reliability, or conduct". No public proof per worker or task.

application.unknown: Workers use a web app; no app or device attestation is documented, and whether proof photos must be taken in-app rather than uploaded from the gallery is not stated

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Interactive tasks only: the agent receives still frames from the worker's phone camera while the worker is live (never video), on a cadence it sets or on demand. Opt-in per task and per worker. Ordinary proof photos are uploads; no live-capture requirement is documented for them. Frames and proof photos are re-encoded without camera metadata. Whether a virtual camera or a photographed screen would be detected is not addressed.

time.method: The server records task events (worker accepted, chat message, completion submitted) in an event feed, and the task record shows when proof was submitted; interactive frames arrive while the worker is live
time.unknown: Capture time of uploaded proof photos is not documented, and their camera metadata is stripped on upload; timestamps are not signed

location.method: Typed proof: geo_checkin is an unwaivable floor for in-person errands and delivery pickups and a default (waivable) for photo documentation; optional request_live_location shares the worker's live position during the task's active window only
location.unknown: How a geo check-in is taken, what radius passes, and resistance to GPS spoofing are not documented. Proof photos are re-encoded without location metadata, so the photo itself carries no location. Live location stops before proof submission.

content.method: The requesting agent (and its person) reviews the typed proof (photos, confirmation codes, signatures) and can accept, request changes or reject; a rejection goes to Mundane's human review, which decides release, refund or split
content.unknown: Mundane screens the task, not the proof; nothing documented checks that a photo shows what it claims before the requester reviews it. In the published demo the agent, not the platform, caught a count mismatch.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check is offered; a requester could post the same task to several workers, but that is buyer-side

The same key works as Authorization: Bearer on the REST API and the hosted MCP endpoint.

MCP at https://api.mundane.market/chatgpt/mcp for directory connections (ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code): authorization code with PKCE S256, public clients (token auth none), clients identified by a Client ID Metadata Document (client_id_metadata_document_supported: true); no RFC 7591 registration endpoint is advertised. cards.name: NASA FIRMS active fires
cards.summary: NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS) publishes active fire and thermal hotspot detections from the MODIS, VIIRS and Landsat satellite sensors, globally within about 3 hours of an overpass and faster (real-time / ultra real-time) over the US and Canada. Global and regional CSV, KML and shapefile files of the last 24 hours, 48 hours and 7 days download with no key; a free MAP_KEY unlocks an area API returning CSV detections for any bounding box over 1-5 days.

tasks: active fire hotspot detections in a bounding box (or the world) for the last 1-5 days
keyless global or regional CSV/KML/shapefile of detections from the last 24 hours, 48 hours or 7 days
VIIRS (NOAA-20, NOAA-21; Suomi NPP ended 2026-11-02 13:00 UTC) and MODIS near-real-time fire detections (Terra and Aqua MODIS wind down in late 2026/early 2027)
Landsat fire detections over the US and Canada
per-detection fields such as brightness, scan/track pixel size, confidence, fire radiative power, acquisition date and time, satellite, day/night

pricing.notes: Free. The 24h/48h/7d files need no key; the area API needs a free MAP_KEY requested with an email address.

latency.typical: Within 3 hours of overpass globally (best effort); within 30 minutes (real-time) or within about a minute to 5 minutes (ultra real-time) over the US and Canada; Landsat 30-60 minutes (US and Canada)
latency.notes: From the FIRMS FAQ and area API page. The FAQ gives both 'within a minute' and 'within 5 minutes' for ultra real-time; the API page says under 60 seconds 'for much of the US and Canada'. RT/URT detections are replaced by NRT ones once processed, or after 6 hours. The keyless 24h/48h/7d files are refreshed every 60 minutes; web services use the most recently processed data. Detections exist only when a satellite passes over, generally about twice a day per sensor (more towards the poles). Suomi NPP data delivery ceases on Nov. 2, 2026. The FAQ also says RT within one hour in another section, so treat the stated minutes as targets.

coverage.notes: Worldwide for MODIS and VIIRS; Landsat and the faster real-time products cover the US and Canada only. Cloud and smoke can hide fires; small or short fires between overpasses can be missed.

licensing.summary: No FIRMS-specific licence. NASA ESDIS data-use guidance: data from NASA-led missions are CC0 unless marked otherwise, while non-NASA data follow their sponsor's licence; NASA asks to be acknowledged ('NASA FIRMS') and must not be implied to endorse a product. LANCE data are provided 'as is'. AI training and resale are not mentioned. Landsat is USGS-operated, so CC0 is not clearly stated for the Landsat NRT layer.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes to about 3 hours after the latest overpass
freshness.notes: The API also serves standard-processing (SP) data for past dates; irlpls lists FIRMS for its near-real-time detections.

cards.name: NATIX Network
cards.summary: Crowdsourced multi-camera (4-6 camera) driving video from Tesla owners who plug in NATIX's VX360 device, sold to Physical AI and autonomous-driving teams as raw footage with GPS, IMU and vehicle telemetry, VLM- and telemetry-mined edge cases, OpenSCENARIO/OpenDRIVE scenarios and map features. NATIX says it can run targeted collection for any region or location. Sales-led: data is requested through a form or hello@natix.io. camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). cards.name: NOAA NDBC buoys
cards.summary: NOAA's National Data Buoy Center publishes real-time observations from moored offshore buoys, coastal C-MAN stations and partner stations (wind speed, direction and gust, significant wave height and period, air and sea temperature, pressure) as plain-text files over HTTPS, free and with no key. Most stations report hourly; the real-time directory holds the last 45 days. About 90 buoys also carry BuoyCAMs that take daylight photos of the sea surface.

pricing.notes: No fee and no key. NDBC asks users to 'limit your retrievals to a minimal level'.

latency.typical: Most stations report hourly, with most data available by about 25 minutes after the hour

A fetch at about 04:59 UTC on 2026-10-27 (2026-10-26 US time) returned a 46026 row stamped 04:30 UTC. The BuoyCAM map refreshes every 15 minutes; BuoyCAM images seen were stamped 04:10 UTC.

regions: United States coastal and offshore waters, including the Great Lakes, Gulf of Mexico, Atlantic, Pacific, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and American Samoa
Partner stations relayed by NDBC: Canada, UK, New Zealand and Irish/French shelf waters, Korea, and tropical moored arrays in the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans
coverage.notes: Only existing fixed stations; you cannot request a new buoy. activestations.xml listed 1,352 stations on 2026-10-26 (programs: IOOS partners, NOS/CO-OPS, NDBC, international partners such as Environment and Climate Change Canada, UK Met Office and the Korean Meteorological Administration, NERRS, tsunami DART, TAO); latest_obs.txt listed 817 currently reporting stations. Data from partner stations are the partners'. Not every station reports every variable (MM marks missing values), and buoys can go adrift or offline. BuoyCAMs: 90 stations listed, 75 with a current image. activestations.xml lists 12 New Zealand stations (NEMA, GNS Science, NIWA), 14 UK Met Office and 45 ECCC. latest_obs.txt had 868 lines on 2026-10-27 (817 the day before), so the count varies. cards.name: NOAA Aviation Weather Center data API (worldwide METAR and TAF)
cards.short: Worldwide airport weather (METAR) and forecasts (TAF) as JSON, covering Africa, S. Asia, LatAm. Free, no key.
cards.summary: The US National Weather Service Aviation Weather Center runs a machine-to-machine API at aviationweather.gov/api/data. METAR (terminal observations) and TAF (terminal forecasts) have worldwide coverage, so one keyless call returns the latest report for any ICAO airport, for example Lagos DNMM, Johannesburg FAOR, Casablanca GMMN or Cairo HECA, with temperature, dew point, wind, visibility, pressure, cloud layers, weather string and flight category. On 2026-11-06 UTC a call for six African and Indian airports answered 200 with reports stamped 19:00 to 21:00 UTC, and a bounding-box call over Africa and the Mediterranean returned 66 reports. A once-a-minute gzip cache file of all current METARs is offered for bulk use.

tasks: latest METAR observation for any ICAO airport worldwide (temperature, wind, visibility, pressure, clouds, flight category)
TAF terminal forecasts, SIGMETs and station lists

coverage.notes: Coverage is wherever airports file METARs, so airports only, not rural stations. Seen in the call: Lagos (NG), Johannesburg (ZA), Casablanca (MA). Most METARs are hourly; some airports report half-hourly or not at all.

rate_limit.notes: Stated on the data API page; exceeding it gets you blocked.

delivery.basis: Live GET 2026-11-06 UTC: reports with reportTime 19:00 to 21:00 UTC; receiptTime within minutes of the report. The provider says most METARs update once per hour and the cache files update once a minute.

latency.typical: Minutes after the report time (hourly cadence for most airports)
latency.notes: Receipt time on one sample was 0 to 70 minutes after report time.

freshness.typical_age: Under about 2 hours on 2026-11-06
freshness.notes: One call only.

The site is a US government information system. Resale and AI training are not addressed. Check with the provider before commercial reuse.
