endpoints.params: GeoJSON Feature: geometry (Point or Polygon) and properties order_name, sku (e.g. TSKPOI-M, TSKRRD-M.NN.NN) and parameters (start, end, revisit_period, processing levels as the contract allows); header x-satellogic-contract-id
endpoints.notes: Creates tasking or archive orders. Cancellation: DELETE /orders/{order_id}.
Order, capture and deliverable events; also GET /orders/{order_id}/captures and /orders/{order_id}/deliverables.
Orders as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection, paginated.
Deliverable with status, footprint and assets (href to GeoTIFF on api.satellogic.com/assets).
STAC API search of the existing archive (not new captures).

api.notes: OpenAPI 3 spec (Aleph API v2, 2.0.0-beta.3) at https://developers.satellogic.com/aleph-v2/api/satellogic_api_v2.yml, server https://api.satellogic.com with paths under /v2. No RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata (api.satellogic.com/.well-known/* returns 403). The Auth0 authorization server publishes RFC 8414 metadata at https://auth.platform.satellogic.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, with no registration endpoint. Signed-package public key: https://api.satellogic.com/.well-known/publickey.pem. Sample packages for every processing level are in the public S3 bucket satellogic-sample-data (eu-west-1).

payment.notes: Paid under a contract or order form; the licence refers to invoiced amounts, payment terms and 1.5% monthly late interest. No card or self-serve checkout. Through UP42 instead, tasking is paid from prepaid UP42 credits.

requester.checks: Customers sign a contract set up by an account manager. They must comply with export controls and sanctions, must not deal with denied or sanctioned parties, and must give Satellogic compliance documents on request. Orders for listed conflicted or restricted areas get 'enhanced due diligence on the requesting customer'. Use must be peaceful and lawful and must not violate privacy or identify natural persons. Each order is accepted only after Satellogic confirms it can capture it.
requester.unknown: What identity or KYC checks are done when the contract is set up is not published.

human.unknown: Captured by Satellogic satellites, not people.

application.unknown: No device or ground-segment attestation is documented. The signed delivery manifest is a statement over delivered files, recorded under provenance.receipt.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Captures come from Satellogic's own NewSat satellites; package names carry the satellite (e.g. SN43). Sensor identity is operator-asserted.

time.method: Capture time is in the package's STAC metadata and the capture events (CaptureCollectionStarted, CaptureAcquired); the signed delivery manifest (provenance.receipt) covers the metadata files.
time.unknown: How capture times are validated is not documented, and the signature only dates from processing.

location.method: Orthorectified products; geoaccuracy measured against an ESRI basemap (CE90 and RMSE, at least 30 match points). Vendor deck: 30 m CE90 for L1 Basic and Ortho-Ready, 10 m CE90 for Ortho (with ground control points).
location.unknown: Satellogic says the ESRI reference basemap's accuracy is 'variable and unknown'; per-image accuracy reports were not found in public docs.

content.unknown: Capture and deliverable quality-control steps exist (QC events), but there is no documented method for detecting manipulated imagery.

corroboration.unknown: No documented cross-check against other sensors for delivered scenes (radiometric cross-calibration with Sentinel-2 is a calibration step, not corroboration).

receipt.method: Since 8 September 2025 every delivery package includes a SHA-256 manifest of all files, signed with Satellogic's RSA-4096 key (PKCS#1 v1.5) when the package is generated; the public key is at https://api.satellogic.com/.well-known/publickey.pem.
receipt.unknown: Not evidenced: on 2026-10-26 none of 102 signed public sample packages verified against the published key, though their file hashes matched their manifests; re-tested 2026-10-28 on an SN43 Baotou L0 package, verification failed with an RSA padding error (a different key). Signed at processing, not capture: it shows files are unchanged since Satellogic generated the package, not what the sensor recorded, and it is not bound to your request or a nonce.

cards.name: SatVu
cards.short: Thermal infrared satellite images of heat, day or night, tasked by API under a SatVu contract.
cards.summary: SatVu (Global Satellite Vu Ltd, London) operates the HotSat mid-wave infrared satellites, which image heat at up to 3.5 m resolution, day and night. Contract holders use its web app, REST API or Python SDK to run a free feasibility check, get a price and place Standard tasking orders (a date window of at least 7 days) or Assured orders (a chosen pass in the next 8 days), including recurring series. SatVu states delivery within 72 hours of capture, 95% of the time. HotSat-2 has been in commercial operation since June 2026. HotSat-3 launched in October 2026 and is being commissioned. SatVu tasking is also sold through SkyFi.

tasks: Standard tasking of a new thermal infrared capture of a point target within a date window of at least 7 days, placed at least 24 hours ahead, with off-nadir (0-45 degrees), cloud cover (25-100%) and day/night/both settings
Assured tasking of a specific satellite pass in the next 8 days, at the highest priority, delivered regardless of cloud cover
recurring order series over the same location on a repeating cadence
free feasibility check before ordering (usually under a minute)
price check before placing an order, including licence-level and catalog-withhold add-ons
track, modify or cancel orders; order-status webhooks
Primary (all frames, radiometrically corrected) and Surface Brightness Temperature (orthorectified, in kelvin) products
heat signatures of industrial sites, buildings and activity, day or night

pricing.model: per tasked scene, at prices set in each contract (GBP or EUR), plus percentage uplifts for licence level and catalog withhold
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published, not free. Each contract has its own product prices and a credit limit. The price endpoint returns base, add-on and total amounts in minor currency units before you order. SatVu's documented example contract shows licence uplifts of 0% (Evaluation), 50% (single entity) and 100% (2-5 entities), and a 30% uplift for a 7-day catalog withhold. Contracts can carry a minimum purchase per term. SatVu says SkyFi also sells its imagery with published pricing and no long-term contract.

latency.typical: Capture within your window (Standard, at least 7 days) or chosen pass (Assured, next 8 days), then delivery within 72 hours of capture, 95% of the time
latency.notes: Feasibility usually returns in under a minute and is not a capture guarantee. Standard orders are delivered only when their parameters are met; SatVu retries at later opportunities and guarantees no minimum capture rate. The capture-to-delivery target comes from SatVu's preliminary Tasking Terms of Service v1.0 (May 2026).

regions: Global (any point on Earth, subject to satellite passes and your contract's geographical access)
coverage.notes: Point targets only. A scene is about 3.5 x 4.5 km at nadir, and an order is fulfilled only if a 1 km radius around the point is fully in the scene. Each contract sets its geographical access, either global or a region. Cloud blocks thermal infrared; Standard orders set a cloud-cover limit, Assured orders do not. One satellite is operational today: HotSat-2 has been in commercial operation since June 2026. HotSat-3 launched in October 2026 and is being commissioned; SatVu says two satellites will give a 1-2 day revisit anywhere, and up to 12 a day at northern latitudes. SkyFi's announcement on SatVu's site says HotSat-3 tasking is expected in early 2027. HotSat-1 suffered an anomaly in December 2023.

licensing.summary: SatVu's EULA (22 July 2026) grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence. Products are 'licenced, not sold' and SatVu keeps the IP. You choose a licence level per order. Commercial levels are single organisation, 2-5 entities, more than 5 entities, or public release. They allow internal non-commercial use, plus small web extracts with no georeferencing, at most 2048 x 2048 px and attributed '(c) [YEAR] SatVu'. Clause 3.1.3 bans selling or supplying imagery or derivatives to third parties beyond your licence level; reselling needs a separate reseller contract. Data Derivatives (contain no imagery and are irreversible) and algorithms you develop with the products stay yours (clause 10.3), but commercial use must be disclosed to SatVu first. The EULA does not mention AI or machine-learning training by buyers.

freshness.typical_age: New capture after ordering; delivered within 72 hours of capture (95%)
freshness.notes: SatVu also sells a catalog of past captures, including other customers' tasking orders after any withhold period. irlpls lists SatVu for new tasked captures.

auth.how_to_get: OAuth2 client credentials: copy the Client ID and Client Secret from your user profile in the SatVu web app, then POST grant_type=client_credentials with audience https://api.satellitevu.com/ to https://auth.satellitevu.com/oauth/token. Send the result as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'; tokens last 60 minutes. You only get an account after SatVu sets up a contract with your organisation.

endpoints.notes: Feasibility request: free and places no order. Statuses: pending, processing, failed, feasible, not feasible. For Assured orders, GET /{contract_id}/tasking/feasibilities/{id}/response returns the available passes, each with the signature used to order it.
Price for the order parameters plus licence_level and addon:withhold. Returns base, add-on and total amounts in minor units. Standard orders use the same payload as feasibility and order.

Places a Standard or Assured tasking order; the price is deducted from the contract credit limit. No idempotency key is documented. Recurring series: POST /{contract_id}/tasking/series/. Cancel while staged: POST /{contract_id}/tasking/orders/{order_id}/cancel.
Order statuses: staged, in progress, fulfilled, failed, cancelled, expired, with status_history. Task attempts: GET .../tasks. Webhook topic tasking:order_status (Standard Webhooks, signed).
Searches your own orders and feasibility requests, e.g. by intersecting geometry. Archive search is a separate STAC Catalog API.
Returns a link to a .zip of the delivered data once the order is fulfilled: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, STAC JSON metadata, UDM and PNG previews.

api.sdk: satvu (PyPI, Python 3.10+), version 0.12.0
api.rate_limits: Not published.

mcp.notes: SatVu has no entry in the official MCP Registry. SatVu tasking can also be ordered through SkyFi's MCP server (see the skyfi card).

api.notes: Public OpenAPI file: https://api.satellitevu.com/otm/v2/openapi.json. The authorization server is https://auth.satellitevu.com, which publishes metadata at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server and /.well-known/openid-configuration. It has no registration endpoint, and the API publishes no protected-resource metadata. A separate integration contract returns simulated 'NotSat' data free of charge for testing. Other APIs: Policy (/policy/v1, list contracts), Wallet (credit balance), ID (webhooks), Catalog (STAC), Orders (catalog orders), Reseller.

payment.notes: An API order is charged to the contract's credit limit with no checkout step, so an agent holding the credentials can buy within that limit. SatVu invoices a tasking order only after it delivers data that meets the order's parameters. Invoices are due in 30 days unless the contract says otherwise, paid by ACH, wire or similar; no cheques. Cancelling a staged order is free.

requester.checks: Organisations sign an agreement and pass KYC before they get platform access. Resellers must register each end-user organisation (name, company, country) for KYC before ordering for it; most approvals take about 5 minutes, some 1-3 business days. The EULA forbids giving access to people or organisations from, or controlled from, China, Russia, Syria, Belarus, North Korea or Iran.
requester.unknown: What the direct-customer KYC checks is not published, and no screening of individual targets or purposes is documented.

human.unknown: Captured by SatVu satellites, not people.

application.unknown: Delivered files carry STAC metadata but no published signature or checksum, so tampering after delivery cannot be detected. Only webhook notifications are signed. The order 'signature' field is an HS256 feasibility token, not a data signature.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Captured by a HotSat mid-wave infrared (MCT) frame camera, as 'snap videos' of up to 25 frames in one second. The Primary product delivers every frame with its calibration parameters. Sensor origin is SatVu's own statement; it is not signed or C2PA-attested.

time.method: Each frame carries an acquisition-start timestamp in the frame index file and STAC metadata. The order API gives acquisition details and a timestamped status history.
time.unknown: Timestamps are set by SatVu and not signed or independently time-stamped.

location.method: Georeferencing starts from onboard attitude and orbit (AOCS) telemetry and is refined with tie points against Sentinel-2 mosaics, then orthorectified on the Copernicus GLO-30 DEM. Stated accuracy is 15 m CE90 or better for Surface Brightness Temperature (0-30 degrees off-nadir), or 200 m CE90 when refinement fails. An order is fulfilled only if a 1 km circle around the target is inside the scene.
location.unknown: SatVu says its georeferencing accuracy was independently validated, but the Product Quality Assurance Report has not been published yet.

content.method: At delivery SatVu checks that the capture meets the order: the target circle is in the scene and cloud cover is within the limit (every image is cloud-assessed, with a per-pixel quality mask).
content.unknown: Nothing is published for detecting altered imagery. Cloud classification is less accurate by day.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual captures. SatVu says its temperature calibration was checked against NOAA's VIIRS sensor, with results still to be published.

delivery.basis: "Capture-to-Delivery: ≤ 72 hours, measured monthly at 95% performance." Standard orders "require a minimum 7-day imaging window" and must be placed "≥ 24 hours prior to TOI"; Assured passes can be chosen "only... for the next 8 days". (source: SatVu Tasking Terms of Service PDF; the 72 h figure is not on the product pages)

cards.name: Sensor.Community
cards.summary: Sensor.Community (formerly Luftdaten.info) is a contributor-driven global network of DIY, low-cost sensors that publishes open environmental data: particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5), temperature, humidity, air pressure and, from some stations, noise. About 17,000 sensors in 72 countries reported in the last 5 minutes on 2026-10-26, most of them in Europe. A keyless API returns every measurement of the last 5 minutes, filterable by radius, box, country or sensor type, plus 1-hour and 24-hour averages. It reports what volunteers' sensors already measure; it cannot place new sensors.
cards.short: Citizen PM2.5/PM10, temperature, humidity and noise sensors in 70+ countries, last 5 minutes, no key.

tasks: particulate (PM10, PM2.5) readings near a point, in a box or by country
temperature, humidity and air pressure near a point
noise level (LAeq, min, max) where a DNMS noise sensor reports
latest readings from one sensor by its API ID
5-minute, 1-hour and 24-hour averages for every sensor
filter by sensor type (e.g. SDS011, BME280)

pricing.notes: Free: the API serves data by GET request with no credentials. No paid tier is offered; the project asks for donations.

latency.typical: Last 5 minutes
latency.notes: The filter and per-sensor endpoints return measurements from the last 5 minutes. The docs say data are not immediately available: an endpoint covering the last minute is updated every minute, and one covering the last 24 hours every 5 minutes. A probe returned readings 1 to 6 minutes old.

freshness.typical_age: Under 5 minutes
freshness.notes: Continuously reported by volunteers' sensors. A daily CSV archive also exists (archive.sensor.community), but it is history, not in scope.

coverage.notes: Wherever volunteers have installed sensors. The all-sensors feed on 2026-10-26 held 17,291 sensors in 72 countries; Germany (6,792), the Netherlands (2,636), Poland, Bulgaria and Belgium had the most, and the US had 80. Outside Europe coverage is sparse.

licensing.summary: The site footer licenses the database contents under the Open Data Commons Database Contents License (DbCL) 1.0, the firmware under GPL-3.0 and photos under CC0 1.0. DbCL grants a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual copyright licence that 'explicitly include[s] commercial use' and sublicensing, on condition that you comply with the ODbL, which covers the database itself; the footer does not link the ODbL separately. Contents come 'as is' without warranty. No terms of use beyond these licences and a privacy notice were found, and nothing mentions AI training, resale or ownership.

time.method: The server sets the timestamp when it receives the data; the docs tell senders not to send a timestamp.
time.unknown: The timestamp is the server's receive time, not the sensor's measurement time, and nothing is signed. The feed gives no time zone; the probe values matched UTC.

location.method: Each sensor's owner sets its location in the devices.sensor.community configuration site.
location.unknown: Self-reported by the volunteer and not checked. Records carry an exact_location flag: in a probe, flagged stations gave full-precision coordinates and the rest 3 decimals (about 100 m), but the flag's meaning is not documented. An indoor flag is also self-reported.

content.method: Readings come from named low-cost sensor models (e.g. Nova Fitness SDS011, BME280, DHT22), reported as raw values.
content.unknown: Low-cost sensors with no calibration or quality control documented for the API, and no correction (e.g. for humidity) is stated.

human.unknown: Volunteers register sensors with an account; no identity check is documented, and owners are not named in the data.

application.unknown: The firmware is open source (GPL-3.0), but nothing attests that a device runs unmodified firmware, and data are pushed with only a sensor ID header.

camera.unknown: Not a camera source.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms individual readings; neighbouring sensors can be compared by the user, but the provider documents no cross-check.

delivery.basis: API docs: '/airrohr/v1/filter/{query} - all measurements of the last 5 minutes filtered by query'; 'An endpoint covering data in the last minute is updated every minute.'

requester.checks: None. The data endpoints need no account or key; the docs ask only for a User-Agent header that lets the operators contact the source of excessive requests.
requester.unknown: Nothing is commissioned; nobody is sent to a place.

auth.how_to_get: No credentials. Send a User-Agent header that identifies you and lets the operators contact you (required since 2022-11-04).

endpoints.notes: All measurements of the last 5 minutes within a radius in km.
All measurements of the last 5 minutes inside a bounding box.
Comma-separated country codes. Filters can also be type={SDS011,BME280,...}.
Last 5 minutes for one sensor. Use the API ID shown on maps.sensor.community, not the chip ID.
All measurements of the last 5 minutes for all sensors (about 18 MB).
Per-sensor averages over the last hour. Also data.json (5 min), data.24h.json, data.dust.min.json and data.temp.min.json.

api.rate_limits: No numeric limit published. The User-Agent is required so operators can contact the source of excessive requests.
api.notes: Use data.sensor.community for reading; api.sensor.community is optimised for receiving data and the docs say not to request data from it. The root of data.sensor.community returns 403, but the documented paths work.

mcp.notes: No server in the official MCP Registry for sensor.community, luftdaten or airrohr (searched 2026-10-26).

payment.notes: Free; no payment.

A free key from the portal is needed for full use. The portal's shared 'sample' key returned HTTP 200 with data but is limited to 5 rows per call. Field names are Korean-style codes; the grade text is in Korean.

ozone, NO2, CO and SO2 readings
air quality index and grade by district

cards.name: Shaip
cards.summary: Managed AI training-data vendor whose contributors and in-house workforce capture custom image, video and speech datasets to a spec (subject, volume, locales, demographics, consent), using the Shaip Work app in the field or head-mounted rigs for first-person video. Every project is scoped and quoted by sales under a contract, starts with a pilot, and passes multi-stage QA before delivery.

tasks: custom image collection to a spec (objects, people, faces, documents, food, landmarks, hand gestures), with documented participant releases
custom egocentric (first-person) video with head-mounted or wearable rigs and full-body and hand motion tracking, in homes, kitchens, factories, warehouses, offices or outdoors
custom speech and audio collection (scripted, spontaneous, dialogue, wake words) in 150+ languages and dialects
on-site and field collection at a location you name, and capture on specific mobile devices or custom cameras
multi-sensor and teleoperation capture for physical AI (depth, LiDAR, IMU, hand and eye tracking, GPS), time-synchronized
field capture by taskers in the Shaip Work mobile app
pilot batch before full collection; annotation of the collected data on request

pricing.model: Custom quote after a scoping call
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means not published. Shaip says there is no flat rate and it does not publish fixed rates. Image cost depends on volume, type, regions, metadata and consent; egocentric video on hours or clips, task complexity, environments, participant diversity and annotation depth; larger milestone-based programs are priced per batch. Quotes usually arrive within two business days.

latency.typical: Weeks (pilot: weeks from signed brief to first batch)
latency.notes: Shaip says typical physical-AI pilot timelines run in weeks from signed brief to first-batch delivery; studio and egocentric captures are faster, multi-sensor rigs slower. Quotes usually within two business days. One case study reports 10,000 valid hours of egocentric VR motion data from about 4,000 participants delivered in a single month.

regions: Global contributor network, 100+ countries (list not published)
coverage.notes: Company figures: 500,000+ crowd-scale contributors, 10,000+ in-house workforce, 100+ countries, 150+ languages and dialects; 30K+ vetted egocentric collectors and 50 cities of egocentric coverage; one landmark project covered 40+ countries. Shaip names no countries, so availability in a specific city is not published.

licensing.summary: Marketing pages say images are 'fully-consented' with 'documented participant releases', every egocentric clip is captured under signed commercial-use participant releases with a 'commercial-use license', de-identification is available, and datasets ship with an auditable provenance record. The public Terms of Service cover the website, plus a payments clause that refers to the platform; customer purchases are governed by a Master Services Agreement or Statement of Work that is not public. Buyer ownership, AI-training rights, resale and whether Shaip reuses delivered data are not stated publicly.

human.method: Contributors are described as a 'vetted' and 'credentialed' network plus a 10,000+ in-house workforce; participants sign releases.
human.unknown: How vetting works, whether identity is checked, and duplicate-account controls are not documented. The Shaip Work App Store listing tells contributors 'No special skill or experience required'.

application.unknown: Field capture uses the Shaip Work app (web, iOS; the Android link on Shaip's site returns 404 on Google Play), but no app or device integrity checks are documented.

camera.unknown: Automated checks for blurry images, faces and duplicate images are described, but nothing checks for gallery imports, re-captured screens or generated media. The platform page says taskers collect 'real-world or synthetic data'.

time.unknown: Delivered with metadata and, for multi-sensor rigs, time-synchronized streams, but no trusted capture time is documented.

location.unknown: The Shaip Work App Store privacy label says the app may collect precise location (developer's statement, not verified by Apple), but no geolocation check on delivered images or video is documented.

content.method: Six Sigma stage-gate QA with multi-stage validation, gold tasks and compliance checks on every batch; AI-assisted checks (duplicate, blurry image, face, landmark, content moderation, diversity) before human review; accuracy, visibility and consistency checks with retakes for egocentric video.
content.unknown: Error rates and acceptance criteria are not published. Shaip says each dataset ships with an 'auditable provenance record'; its contents (consent records vs. per-file custody) are not published.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of submissions is described.

auth.how_to_get: No API. Contact sales through the form on shaip.com ('Contact Us', 'Request a sample dataset'); work is placed under a Master Services Agreement or Statement of Work.

cards.name: SkyFi
cards.summary: Self-serve marketplace that resells archive and newly tasked satellite and aerial imagery from many operators (Vantor, Planet, Umbra, ICEYE US, Satellogic, Sentinel open data and others) through one web app, a REST Platform API and a first-party remote MCP server (OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration), with per-km² or per-scene pricing, validate-before-order price checks, webhooks and delivery to S3/GCS/Azure.

tasks: search the existing imagery archive by AOI polygon, date, resolution, product type, provider, cloud cover and off-nadir angle
order archive scenes (cropped to an AOI)
task a new satellite capture over an AOI within a time window (DAY, NIGHT, VIDEO, MULTISPECTRAL, HYPERSPECTRAL, SAR, STEREO, THERMAL product types)
feasibility / pass checks before tasking (Planet, Umbra, SatVu)
free Sentinel-1/Sentinel-2 open data orders
archive notifications to a webhook when new imagery matches a filter
basemaps and tile streaming tokens
run paid analytics (NDVI, NDWI, building, vessel and vehicle detection) on delivered imagery (MCP)

pricing.model: pay per order, per km² or per scene; no subscription or minimum spend
pricing.unit: per km² (optical archive, High resolution; smallest per-km² imagery price stated besides $1/km² basemaps)
pricing.notes: From skyfi.com/pricing: optical archive from $5/km² and new optical tasking from $8/km² (Vantor, Planet, Satellogic; 15 cm to 1 m); optical archive tops out at $100/km² for Ultra High 7.5 cm aerial; SAR from $450/scene archive and $675/scene tasking (e.g. Umbra); 3D products (DSM/DTM/point clouds) from $7.50/km²; basemap mosaics from $1/km²; open data free; no subscriptions, contracts or minimum spend. The same page's summary cards say single archive image from $15, single tasking image from $200, aerial from $35, analytics from $5. Minimums: SkyFi's FAQ says minimum tasking area is 25 km² and a 25 km² tasking request starts at $200; Planet Select orders need a 25 km² minimum AOI (from $6/km² archive >30 days, $12/km² flexible tasking). Archive minimums are per scene: each search result carries minSqKm/maxSqKm, priceForOneSquareKm and priceFullScene/fullSceneOnly. Exact prices come from the API (POST /pricing, /tasking/products, the */validate endpoints; MCP validate tools return estimatedCostCents). A 'full pricing sheet' download exists but was not read. Free accounts can place 1 open-data order per day and paid orders with a card on file; Pro accounts 5 open-data orders per day plus advanced billing (Pro price not found). The MCP connector itself is free. Check: the static pricing page shows only the per-image starting prices ($15 archive, $200 tasking, SAR $450, aerial $35); the per-km2 rates, the $675 SAR tasking figure and the 25 km2 minimum were not visible on it in a later check, so confirm them in the app or the pricing sheet.

latency.typical: Archive: usually within 24 hours. Tasking: within 48 hours of capture, capture timing set by your tasking window
latency.notes: Per the Platform API docs: 'Archival imagery order delivery is usually within 24 hours' and 'Tasking orders will deliver within 48 hours of image capture.' Archive results include a deliveryTimeHours field. The pricing page FAQ mentions a guaranteed 'Next Available Capture' tasking mode that 'delivers imagery within 24 hours regardless of weather' (which providers and terms apply was not found). Order status changes can be pushed to a webhook (2 s timeout, up to 3 retries).

regions: Global (subject to each operator's archive and orbit coverage)
coverage.notes: SkyFi says it aggregates 50+ provider partners and 300+ satellite and aerial sources (llms.txt; the pricing and API pages say 300+ sources) and serves users in 179 countries. In-app providers named on the pricing page: Vantor, Planet, ICEYE, Umbra, Satellogic, Vexcel, Pixxel, GEOSAT, IMPRO and SIIS. The API's provider enum also lists Sentinel-1/2 (Creodias), Urban Sky, NSL, BlackSky, SatVu and Constellr. AOIs must be simple convex WKT polygons, max 500 vertices; archive searches max 500,000 km². Tasking offerings can be excluded with reason AOI_RESTRICTED (criteria unpublished). Actual availability per location and date depends on the underlying operator; Vantor imagery needs a separate EULA acceptance (else 403). The EULA bars making products available to embargoed or sanctioned countries, regions or parties under US export rules.

licensing.summary: SkyFi EULA: limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, revocable licence for the end user's own internal purposes; you may create value-added products (VAP) and derivative works, share with contractors under written terms, and post or print extracts for promotion only; products may not be resold, redistributed or shared, and only derivative works that contain no imagery data and are irreversible may be distributed. Imagery remains the satellite provider's property (EULA 4.1); markings must not be removed. The EULA does not address AI/ML training. The MCP Terms say imagery is 'licensed, not sold' and bar reselling or redistributing it except as the provider licence permits; some operators (e.g. Vantor) have their own EULA. On SkyFi's own use of your data: the main privacy notice says data submitted through its AI-based tools may be logged and, once anonymised, used in training models; the MCP privacy policy says it does not use personal information to train AI models.

human.unknown: Not applicable in the usual sense: captures are made by satellite/aircraft operators, not individual people; SkyFi documents no operator-level attestation.

application.unknown: No public description of how SkyFi checks that delivered files are unmodified operator products; no signing or checksum scheme is documented in the API spec.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). Sensor identity is metadata asserted by the operator and passed through by SkyFi; no independent check documented. SkyFi was not found on the C2PA conforming products page.

Dynamic client registration is deprecated by the MCP specification of 2026-07-28 in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD); whether SkyFi accepts CIMD is not stated.

cards.summary: The Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI) publishes hydrological observations through the Hydroobs open data service. Parameter 2 is discharge at 15-minute resolution (m3/s), with 721 stations listed, 299 flagged active on 2026-11-07. A keyless GET for station 2357 (Abisko, Torneälven catchment) with period latest-hour answered 200 on 2026-11-07 UTC with values 58.0 and 58.2 m3/s, the newest stamped 18:00 UTC, quality flag O. Other parameters include daily and monthly discharge, water temperature, and ice and snow items. The service nests parameter, station and period (latest-hour, latest-day, latest-months, corrected-archive) and returns JSON, XML, CSV or Atom.

cards.name: Toloka
cards.summary: Self-serve data platform: a requester describes a collection task, an AI assistant builds the pipeline (instructions, contributor audience by country and language, price, quality criteria), and contributors it describes as ID-verified record and upload the data, checked by an LLM reviewer and optionally by human reviewers. The documented collection template is egocentric (first-person, head-mounted) household-activity video; other collection (images, audio, in-the-field capture) is built from a description. Funded from a prepaid balance topped up by card; projects, runs and exports can also be driven through a beta REST API, a TypeScript SDK and a CLI. Toloka's older mobile field-task app (geotagged photos of places) is no longer documented and is not described here.
cards.short: A self-serve platform where vetted contributors record first-person task video to your brief.

tasks: custom egocentric (first-person, head-mounted) video filmed to a written brief, uploaded by contributors (Egocentric Activity Video Collection template: 50 to 1,000 videos, 13 default household activity categories)
household and manual task video for robotics and physical AI training
other new data collection (images, audio, in-the-field capture) set up by the platform assistant from a description; no template for these is documented
custom data collection or workflows outside self-service, on request

pricing.model: Per run: a cost forecast (Expected and Maximum) is approved before deploy, then charged pay-as-you-go against a prepaid team balance
pricing.unit: run (one pipeline run of up to 10,000 items)
pricing.notes: from_usd 0 means no unit price is published. You set the per-task price paid to each contributor; Toloka adds a fixed 33% commission, plus LLM QA per review call, human QA per sampled review (payout scaled to review time plus 10%), and a video-review charge (base rate plus per-minute rate) where the LLM reviewer watches video. The real per-task and per-call prices appear only in the in-app cost breakdown. Deploying freezes the run's prices. No minimums or contracts. HomER (63 head-mounted household videos, 17 categories) cost about $50 in total; that is one example, not a rate. New accounts get $50 credit after the first $50 of qualifying spend.

latency.typical: First batch in about 3 hours; results in 24 hours (provider marketing)
latency.notes: The egocentric video page lists '3 hrs' to first batch and 'production-ready results in 24 hours'; HomER took 3 hours to collect. A template deploy usually takes 5 to 15 minutes before tasks are live. No SLA; real time depends on brief, volume, price and contributor availability.

coverage.notes: Toloka cites 200,000+ contributors in 100+ countries and 40 languages, but publishes no country list, only exclusions: contributors cannot be resident in sanctioned jurisdictions (e.g. Russia, China, Iran, Belarus, Cuba, North Korea, Syria) or in places its ID-verification or payment providers do not cover (including Switzerland, Taiwan and Kenya). The requester can limit the contributor audience by country and language. Recording happens wherever contributors live (mostly their homes), not at a place the requester picks.

licensing.summary: Self-Service Agreement (22 Apr 2026). §7.1: the buyer owns Output created specifically for it once Fees are fully paid (§7.2 excludes the seller's Background IP); §7.3: contributors must assign those rights to the buyer. The terms assume buyers train AI models on Output (§2.6, §8.4.1) but contain no express training grant but forbid using it to build or train products that compete with Toloka (§6.2(vii)). §6.2(iv) forbids reselling Output, and §6.2(iii) forbids making it available for the benefit of unaffiliated third parties. §7.4/§7.9: Toloka may train its internal models on your Data and Output unless you opt out in writing; the opt-out is prospective only and does not cover derived de-identified 'Toloka Data'. §5: Data and Output from a free trial are licensed to Toloka irrevocably and perpetually for any purpose, including model training, and the opt-out does not apply.

human.method: Contributors must pass Toloka's identity, residency and eligibility verification (an identity document showing country of residence); labeling tasks default to experts who have passed ID verification.
human.unknown: Whether the verified account holder is the person who filmed each clip, how multi-account use is detected, and whether collection templates (not only labeling nodes) require ID-verified contributors. No public evidence. The eligibility terms name no identity-verification vendor ('our identity verification provider') and document no liveness check or re-verification; an account can be shared after enrolment.

application.unknown: Contributors record with their own smartphones or cameras and upload files; no capture-app or device attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: No check that a video came from a real camera rather than a screen, edit or generator is described; HomER rejected re-used clips by rule, not by a documented detector.

time.unknown: No trusted capture time is documented.

location.unknown: No location capture or check is documented. The audience filter restricts contributors by country of residence, not where a clip was recorded.

content.method: An LLM reviewer checks every submission against the requester's written quality criteria (e.g. head-mounted, both hands visible 95%+ of the time, no third-person footage), with a verdict and reason per criterion, and watches video fields; rejected work goes back for correction or reassignment. Optional human review checks a 10 to 100% sample. Toloka cites 89.1% accuracy at catching failures.
content.unknown: How the 89.1% figure was measured, the false-accept rate, and whether people review anything the model passes when human review is not switched on.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check of a collected recording is described. Multi-contributor agreement (Quorum nodes) is documented for labeling, not for confirming a capture.

auth.how_to_get: Sign up at platform.toloka.ai, then in the Business Console open your company, go to API keys and click Generate API key. Send it as 'Authorization: ApiKey <key>'. The key acts as its user and does not expire until deleted.
A project-scoped token issued with POST /api/v2-beta/projects/{projectId}/tokens by an API-key holder; revocable.

Interactive use: 'toloka login --browser' signs the CLI in through the browser (Google or Microsoft); the session renews for up to 14 days. Toloka's agent skill says never to ask a person to paste a key into chat.

endpoints.notes: Lists projects across your teams; read-only connection check.
Cost forecast for a pipeline before a run.

Starts a paid run. A pipeline must first be imported or copied (no endpoint assembles nodes), with a dataset bound via POST /pipelines/{pipelineId}/dataset. Blocked for teams that have not completed identity or business verification.
Poll until succeeded or failed; a cancelled run reports failed with 'Run canceled'. GET /runs/{runId}/cost gives the run's cost.
Run items. Full results: POST /datasets/{datasetId}/exports, then poll GET /exports/{exportId} for a download link (expires after 30 minutes).

api.sdk: @toloka-platform/sdk (TypeScript, 0.x) and the toloka CLI; Toloka publishes agent runbooks at platform.toloka.ai/agents/SKILL.md. The older Python toloka-kit targeted the legacy API.
api.rate_limits: 60 requests per minute per endpoint; RateLimit-* headers; 429 when exceeded. A run processes at most 10,000 items; a dataset holds at most 150,000.

mcp.auth: OAuth 2 (protected-resource metadata at https://mcp.tendem.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp; Keycloak at auth.tendem.ai publishes a dynamic client registration endpoint and PKCE S256) or 'Authorization: ApiKey' for headless use
mcp.notes: This is Tendem, Toloka's expert-task product ('research, writing, analysis, and data work'), not the Toloka Platform data-collection crowd. No MCP server for the data-collection platform was found.

api.notes: The Pipeline API is beta: request and response shapes may change without notice. OpenAPI 3.1 document at https://platform.toloka.ai/api/v2-beta/doc. State-changing requests need Content-Type: application/json. Payments and top-ups are not in the API.

freshness.typical_age: Recorded after you launch the run
freshness.notes: Toloka also sells existing datasets; only the commissioned collection is described here.

delivery.basis: Egocentric video page: '3 hrs' to first batch, 'production-ready results in 24 hours'.

rate_limit.notes: Per endpoint; RateLimit-* headers; 429 when exceeded. A run processes at most 10,000 items.

payment.notes: A team keeps a prepaid USD balance, topped up by card (Stripe) in the Business Console; bank transfer on request. A run reserves its cost from the balance and pauses if it runs out. The API can spend an existing balance but cannot top it up. All purchases are final and non-refundable.

requester.checks: Before adding funds or placing paid orders, a requester must give a valid payment method and pass KYB and sanctions/export screening; a team that has not completed identity or business verification cannot start a run. Some jurisdictions get enhanced due diligence (ID and proof of address for owners and directors). Toloka may review and moderate any project before or after publication, and the terms forbid using the service for unlawful surveillance, biometric identification or doxxing.

cards.name: Truelabel
cards.short: Introduces robotics labs to firms that capture physical-AI data to their spec, then checks and processes the delivery.
cards.summary: A Brazilian company (Ensoft Informática LTDA, trading as TrueLabel) that connects organizations needing physical-AI training data with organizations that capture it, and runs the processing pipeline between them. A buyer describes the task, setting, data type (head-worn video, teleoperation, motion capture, fixed cameras) and hours; Truelabel looks for suppliers who can capture it and checks each recording against the buyer's spec (camera sync, hands in view, faces and screens blurred) before delivery, splitting takes into episodes, syncing streams and labelling actions. Truelabel is not a party to the buyer-supplier deal unless a signed agreement says so; that deal sets price, ownership and licence. Its revenue is processing fees under a signed agreement per engagement. Its own collector marketplace closed on 8 October 2026; no prices, timelines or API are published.

tasks: introduction to suppliers who capture to a buyer's spec: head-worn (first-person) video, teleoperation, motion capture, fixed cameras
capture with Truelabel's capture app or phones it supplies: first-person video, device-motion data and capture metadata; sound only when a project needs it
checking each recording against the buyer's spec line by line, with incomplete or ambiguous items flagged for review
processing into training examples: episode splitting with idle time trimmed, streams synced to one clock, actions, hands and outcomes labelled to the buyer's guide, faces and screens blurred
per-example provenance (device, session, labelling guide) in a dataset bundle with a manifest

pricing.notes: Not published. Truelabel's revenue comes from processing fees set in a signed agreement for each engagement. The price of the capture itself is agreed between buyer and supplier, outside Truelabel's terms.

licensing.summary: Truelabel takes no ownership of or licence to recordings: the arrangements between the organizations involved, and with the people who record, decide who owns recordings and how they may be used. The service customer (whoever hires Truelabel) must hold every right and consent, including image and voice. The terms name model training, derivative works, exclusivity, redistribution and resale as separate terms for the operator's spec, not defaults. Unless the service customer opts out in its agreement, Truelabel may use recordings in de-identified or aggregated form to improve its processing pipeline (quality checks and processing steps); it does not sell or relicense them. A check result is not acceptance, legal clearance or a warranty that data is lawful or consented.

cards.name: Truepic Vision
cards.short: Texts or emails a person at the place a capture link; photos are checked for time, GPS spoofing and device integrity.
cards.summary: Truepic Vision sends the person at a property, vehicle or piece of equipment a capture link by text or email. They take photos and videos in the Truepic Vision app or a mobile browser. Each photo comes back with pass/warn/fail results: device time against server time, GPS spoofing, distance from the address, signed capture details, upload integrity, rooted or jailbroken phones (app only), and photos of a screen. Results arrive by API or webhook, with an optional PDF report and AI analysis. Access is sold to businesses with a $1,000/month minimum, and API credentials come only after Truepic sets up the organisation. The service has US and UK/Europe regions.

pricing.notes: Flex: month-to-month. The $1,000/mo minimum is one invoice that includes a use-case allotment (e.g. 200 recall inspections at $5); inspections above it bill at the plan rate. Per-inspection rate by use case: product recall $5, insurance underwriting $16–$48, home lending $29, auto warranty $36, construction lending $39, insurance claims $48, equipment financing and business credentialing $51. Standard (annual): headline $1,450/mo at $58/inspection for 300/yr; use-case tiers run down to $2/inspection for product recall at 50,000+/yr; overage $28–$65 by tier. Enterprise above 10,000/yr is custom. One Virtual Inspection covers up to 100 images from one person for one event; every further 100 images counts as another. AI Analysis is billed separately per subject.

licensing.summary: Terms of Service §3.2: "As between Truepic and Customer, Customer owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Customer Content" (photos, data and other content from Customer or its End Users). Truepic gets a licence during the term to use the content "to provide and improve the Services and to create the Aggregated Anonymous Data", which it may use "for any lawful purpose". Reports ("analytics, data, and output generated from an inspection", including AI Output) are part of the Services, which Truepic owns. §4.4 bars selling, sublicensing or providing the Services to third parties and bars modifying any Report. Content from AI Analysis is 'not used to train or improve generalized AI models' (Additional Product Terms). The terms do not mention resale of the captured photos, or AI training by the buyer.

application.method: Truepic Lens capture in the Vision app or web app. capture_integrity_result checks the signed details, data_result checks the upload. jailbreak_result and device attestation (AppAttest/SafetyNet) run in the native apps only.
application.unknown: These are Truepic's own results. Its signing certificates chain to Truepic's own CA, which is not on the C2PA Trust List, and Truepic is not on the C2PA Conforming Products List. The web app signs on the server and has no root detection or attestation. SafetyNet is deprecated by Google in favour of Play Integrity.

camera.method: Lens signs each capture with content credentials (C2PA manifest): on-device with a device key in the native Vision apps, server-side in the web app, Lens Web SDK and Embedded Vision. capture_integrity_result checks the signed details ('Securely signed; tamper-proof').
camera.unknown: Truepic is not on the C2PA Conforming Products List and its CA is not on the C2PA Trust List (checked 2026-10-28), so a validator will not report the manifest as Trusted. Web captures are signed on Truepic's server, not on the device. No revocation policy for signing keys is documented. Signing does not detect a re-photographed screen; pop_result (under content) is a model's verdict.

time.method: time_result: device time within 5 minutes of server time and not modified. The time is signed into the capture's content credentials.
time.unknown: The signature chains to Truepic's own CA, not the C2PA Trust List, and no RFC 3161 time-stamp is documented. The buyer has to trust Truepic's check.

location.unknown: Location comes from the phone and can still be spoofed. Truepic's spoof detection is its own, and the web app has no sensor data.

content.method: Integrity: content credentials and capture_integrity_result (signed details verified; the upload checked by data_result). Depiction: pop_result flags photos of a screen or a print; optional object_detection_result and content_analysis_result (odometer, VIN, text); optional AI Analysis.
content.unknown: Truepic calls AI Output probabilistic and "not a definitive determination". The default checks cover tampering, not whether the photo shows the right thing. Integrity rests on Truepic's own CA; depiction checks (pop_result, object and content analysis) are detector verdicts and cannot raise content above claimed.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms the capture. The Risk Network flags devices that other customers have flagged, which is a fraud signal, not confirmation.

cards.name: Environment Agency real-time flood-monitoring API
cards.short: England's river, groundwater and rain gauges, UK tide gauges and live flood warnings. Free, no key.
cards.summary: The Environment Agency's beta real-time API serves water level and flow from about 5,500 monitoring stations in England, about 1,000 rain gauges, the UK National Tide Gauge Network, and current flood alerts and warnings for England, all keyless under the Open Government Licence. Levels and flows are measured usually every 15 minutes, but the Agency says stations typically send data once or twice a day, more often when flood risk is high; on 2026-10-26 most latest readings were under an hour old.

tasks: find gauges within N km of a point, by river, town, catchment, type or status
latest river, groundwater and tidal water level
latest river flow (some stations)
15-minute rainfall totals from tipping-bucket rain gauges
tide gauge levels (15-minute mean) around the UK coast
wind and air temperature at a few stations
current flood alerts and warnings with severity and situation message
flood alert and warning area polygons
readings for the last four weeks; older readings as daily CSV archives

coverage.notes: The station list returned 5,539 stations on 2026-10-26 (5,318 level, 1,055 rainfall and 394 flow measures, plus a few wind and temperature). River, rain and groundwater stations are in England; queries around Cardiff, Aberystwyth and Glasgow found none except Newport tide gauges. The tide gauge network (the Agency says 44 locations) also covers Wales, Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Isle of Man; Lerwick, Portrush and Port Erin returned 04:15 UTC readings, while Jersey is listed but returned no readings. coverage.areas lists England only, since the coastal sites are a thin network. Flood warnings are the Agency's, for England. Rain gauge locations are rounded to a 100 m grid and the stations are unnamed.

pricing.notes: Free open data under the Open Government Licence, with no requirement for registration.

rate_limit.notes: No request rate published. Readings: 500 items by default, at most 10,000 via _limit; readings?latest returns every station in one call. Responses carry Cache-Control max-age=300.

delivery.basis: Environment Agency: water levels and flows are monitored usually every 15 minutes, but data is transferred typically once or twice per day, more often during heightened flood risk; the readings set is updated every 15 minutes. Tide gauge data typically lags 15 to 30 minutes.

latency.typical: Usually under an hour for most stations; some only once or twice a day
latency.notes: The Agency says levels and flows are measured usually every 15 minutes but transferred typically once or twice per day, more often when flood risk is high; rainfall is also typically transferred once or twice a day; tide gauges lag 15 to 30 minutes. Live check at 05:00 UTC on 27 Oct 2026 (26 Oct US time) of /data/readings?latest: 5,376 latest values, newest 17 minutes old, median 31 minutes, 84% under 60 minutes, 98% under 24 hours, 117 older than a day. Responses are cached (Cache-Control max-age=300). Beta service with no guarantee of service level.

freshness.typical_age: Median about 30 minutes on 2026-10-26; up to a day for stations that send once or twice daily
freshness.notes: The API holds readings for up to the last four weeks; a reading's URI stops resolving after 28 days. Readings are sometimes updated in batches, so use the since filter on a measure or station to keep a full history. Daily CSV archives are at /flood-monitoring/archive. A flood warning stays at severity 4 ('Warning no longer in force') for about 24 hours, then disappears.

licensing.summary: Open Government Licence v3.0, no registration. The OGL grants a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to copy, publish, distribute, adapt and exploit the information commercially and non-commercially, on condition of attribution. The API asks for the statement 'this uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta)' (rainfall and tide gauge data have their own wording). The site terms say logos and trademarks are exempt from the OGL. Neither the OGL nor the site terms mention AI or machine-learning training, or resale by name.

time.method: Each reading carries a dateTime in UTC (Z suffix) for when the reading applies.
time.unknown: Timestamps come from the Agency's own telemetry system and are not signed; how logger clocks are set or checked is not documented. Readings may arrive in late batches.

location.method: Fixed stations with published WGS84 lat/long, British National Grid easting/northing and grid reference.
location.unknown: Coordinates are the Agency's own records, not independently checked. Rain gauge locations are deliberately rounded to a 100 m grid.

content.method: Each measure states parameter, qualifier, unit and datum (mAOD, mASD or m) and value type (instantaneous, mean, total, maximum, minimum); stations publish typical range and records.
content.unknown: Beta service with no guarantee of service level; the Agency says it should not be relied on for safety-critical uses. No quality flags are published per reading, and NaN values are simply omitted from JSON.

human.unknown: Not applicable: readings come from automated Environment Agency gauges, not from people.

application.unknown: No signing or attestation of readings from gauge to API; integrity rests on the Agency operating the network.

camera.unknown: Not a camera source.

corroboration.unknown: Nothing documented independently confirms individual readings.

auth.how_to_get: No key and no registration.

endpoints.params: lat, long, dist (km; may be approximated by a bounding box); parameter (level, flow, rainfall...); qualifier; type (SingleLevel, MultiTraceLevel, Coastal, Groundwater, Meteorological; TideGauge for tide gauges); status (Active, Closed, Suspended); riverName; town; catchmentName; search; _view=full; _limit; _offset

endpoints.notes: The Agency recommends one call to /data/readings?latest every 15 minutes rather than crawling stations.
All readings for one station; /id/measures/{id}/readings does the same for one measure.

endpoints.notes: Current flood alerts and warnings, updated every 15 minutes.
Flood alert and warning areas with a link to each GeoJSON polygon.

Readings return 500 items by default (no default limit for latest, today or date queries unless _sorted is set), up to a hard limit of 10,000 via _limit; flood areas default to 500 with no hard limit. cards.name: Umbra
cards.summary: Operator of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite constellation that images through clouds and at night. Its Canopy web app and REST API let you check feasibility, task a new Spotlight (5x5 km, 0.25-1 m priced) or Scan capture in a time window you set, track it, and download the delivered collect via STAC. Collects generally arrive 1-4 hours after the window closes. List prices start at $675 per 5x5 km scene at 1 m. Every Canopy registration goes through Umbra's regulatory review. Umbra also runs a public CC BY 4.0 open-data archive, but that is context only: here it is listed for new captures.

tasks: task a new SAR Spotlight capture centred on a point (default 5x5 km scene; 4x4 km, 10x10 km and Natural Footprint scene sizes if enabled for your organization; range resolution 0.25, 0.35, 0.5, 1 or 2 m; multilook 1/2/4/8 via the API)
task a new SAR Scan strip between two points 25-100 km apart (8 km swath; 2 m up to 100 km, 1 m up to 75 km, 0.5 m up to 50 km)
Extended Dwell collects (list-priced on umbra.space; not an imaging mode in the Canopy API, which offers SPOTLIGHT and SCAN)
feasibility check: get imaging opportunities for a location and time window before ordering
track task and collect status; cancel tasks that are still SCHEDULED, SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED or ACTIVE
deliver products: GEC (always), SICD, SIDD, CPHD, CRSD, DI_GIF, DI_TIF, plus STAC metadata; CSI products for 5x5 km Spotlight
push deliveries to a configured cloud destination (AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage delivery configs)

pricing.model: per tasked collect, list price by imaging mode, scene size, resolution and number of looks
pricing.unit: per 5x5 km Spotlight scene (1 m, 1 look)
pricing.notes: From umbra.space/pricing and the Umbra Product Guide. Spotlight 5x5 km, 1 look: 1.0 m $675, 0.5 m $950, 0.35 m $1,750, 0.25 m $3,250; more looks raise it (e.g. 1.0 m 10-look $2,200; 0.25 m 3-look $4,900). Natural Footprint, 1 look: $1,500 (1 m) to $3,750 (0.25 m); processed to 10x10 km at no extra charge on request if the scene is large enough. Extended Dwell 5x5 km $4,750; CSI and SAR video +40% on list price. Scan by strip length: 2 m $1,250-$2,250, 1 m $2,500-$3,500, 0.5 m $4,000 (25-50 km). GEC, SICD, SIDD and JSON metadata are included; CPHD or CRSD add $250 each and switch a 5x5 km Spotlight to Natural Footprint pricing. Bistatic/multistatic: +100%. A 30-day Archive Withhold (keeps the new collect out of Umbra's archive) costs 200% of list price. Pricing is per collect; no minimum order was stated. The Canopy API has no price-quote endpoint. Fees are non-refundable under the Tasking Terms.

latency.typical: Delivered 1-4 hours after the end of your tasking window
latency.notes: Task Lifecycle Tutorial: the scheduler processes the task queue every 10 minutes, and collect delivery 'will generally happen 1-4 hours after the associated Task's windowEndAt has passed.' Capture happens inside the window you set (windowStartAt/windowEndAt); the scheduler biases to the earliest feasible time in the window. In the UI the window end is limited to 7 days ahead, and scheduling reaches about 7-8 days ahead (state vectors). Umbra says it is 'generally safe to submit Tasks up to three hours before the desired collection time'. Product Guide mean revisit: 4.71 h at the equator, 3.75 h at ±30°, 2.32 h at ±50°, 0.88 h at ±67°. If feasibility returns no opportunities, the docs say to resubmit with a longer window.

regions: Global (subject to orbit passes and restricted access areas)
coverage.notes: SAR sees through cloud and works at night. Any point or line can be requested; actual availability comes from the feasibility endpoint. Polar orbit (97.4°), ground range 170-1,100 km either side of the flight path. Restricted Access Areas (an API endpoint and a published GeoJSON list) block tasking: some areas need screening beyond standard KYC (ongoing conflict), some conflict with Umbra priorities, and some are limited by US regulation (e.g. resolution limits over Israel). Spotlight is 5x5 km by default; Natural Footprint is larger (commonly 7.5x11 to 16x10 km) if enabled. Scan swath is 8 km wide.

licensing.summary: The Satellite Tasking Services Terms and Conditions license all delivered Content under CC BY 4.0: content is 'licensed, not sold', and Umbra keeps all right, title and interest. Attribution is required, with the notice 'SAR-derived data © [YEAR] Umbra Lab, Inc.' on adapted material. Umbra's Licensing & Attribution page says customers may publish, resell at a profit without royalty, and sell derivative works. The Terms override CC BY where they conflict, e.g. US export controls and sanctions (no resale to embargoed countries). The Terms do not mention AI or machine-learning training. Per the Product Guide, new tasked collects enter Umbra's Archive Catalog (which Umbra sells) unless you buy a 30-day Archive Withhold at 200% of list price. Delivered content can be downloaded for 90 days after notice. The separate open-data archive on AWS is also CC BY 4.0.

human.unknown: Not applicable in the usual sense: captures are made by Umbra's own satellites, not individual people

application.unknown: No public description of signing or checksums that would prove delivered files are unmodified Umbra products; the STAC metadata documented has no checksum fields. Downloads come from pre-signed URLs on Umbra's STAC endpoint.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Collects carry SAR metadata (platform/satelliteId, range resolution, looks, polarization, grazing, azimuth and squint angles); Umbra publishes satellite IDs with NORAD numbers. SICD/CPHD are standard NGA sensor-model formats. Sensor identity and parameters are operator-asserted metadata; no independent check documented. Not on the C2PA Conforming Products List.

time.method: STAC datetime is the centre of aperture; start_datetime and end_datetime are the first and last radar pulse, in UTC, inside the tasked window
time.unknown: How pulse times are measured and checked is not publicly documented, and nothing timestamps them independently

location.method: Collects carry footprint geometry (WGS 84); GEC is geocoded and ellipsoid-corrected; SICD includes sensor geometry. Umbra states 8 m CE90 absolute geolocation accuracy, and its automated QA includes a geolocation calibration check when calibration sites are collected.
location.unknown: The 8 m CE90 figure is a system specification, not a per-collect measurement; no public per-collect geolocation report

content.method: Limited warranty in the Tasking Terms that delivered Content will 'reasonably be of the area of interest as requested' and meet the Product Guide specs (replace or credit, claims within 30 days). Automated QA before delivery rejects blank, eclipsed or mispointed collects (status CORRUPT, task ANOMALY).
content.unknown: No public method for detecting manipulated or synthetic SAR imagery; QA checks image quality, not authenticity. Raw CPHD/CRSD lets an expert reprocess, but that is not an integrity guarantee.

corroboration.unknown: No documented cross-check against other sensors; a buyer could compare against other SAR or optical providers themselves

freshness.typical_age: Captured inside the window you set after ordering, delivered 1-4 hours after the window ends
freshness.notes: IRLpls lists Umbra for new tasked captures. For context only: Canopy also has a STAC archive catalog and archive-task ordering (priced at the equivalent list price), and Umbra publishes a CC BY 4.0 open-data archive on AWS (s3 umbra-open-data-catalog, us-west-2). Those are not the offering listed here.

auth.how_to_get: OAuth2 client credentials for scripts and services: an organization admin creates one shared client_id/client_secret on the Canopy Organization page (Authentication tab), then POSTs them to https://auth.canopy.umbra.space/oauth/token with audience https://api.canopy.umbra.space and grant_type client_credentials. Tokens last 86,400 s; token requests are limited to 50 per 24 h per client, so cache them. Use audience https://api.canopy.prod.umbra-sandbox.space for the sandbox. Needs an approved Canopy account.

Copy an access token from https://canopy.umbra.space/account (expires after 24 hours). For a sandbox token, switch on 'Test Mode' in the app header and call api.canopy.prod.umbra-sandbox.space; sandbox collects are not billable. No public account sign-up flow was found: the docs point to umbra.space/contact, and every registration is subject to Umbra's regulatory review.

endpoints.params: constraints (required; SPOTLIGHT with GeoJSON Point geometry, or SCAN with a 2-point LineString), windowStartAt, windowEndAt (required); contractId
endpoints.notes: Feasibility rather than price: returns id and status (RECEIVED/COMPLETED/ERROR). Poll until COMPLETED to read opportunities. Rate limit 2/s, 120/min, 3600/h.
Poll feasibility; results are kept only about five minutes after creation. Null opportunities means resubmit with a longer window.

endpoints.notes: Creates a new capture (billable). New tasks should move to SUBMITTED or REJECTED within minutes. No idempotency key is documented (userOrderId is a free label, searchable on collects). Rate limit 2/s, 120/min, 300/h. Check organization settings (GET /admin/organizations/settings) for the resolutions and products your organization may use.

Task status (RECEIVED, SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED, ACTIVE, SCHEDULED, TASKED, TRANSMITTED, INCOMPLETE, PROCESSING, PROCESSED, DELIVERING; terminal DELIVERED, REJECTED, CANCELED, ERROR, ANOMALY) and collectIds
Cancel a task; works only while SCHEDULED, SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED or ACTIVE. Returns 204, or 422 on failure. Rate limit 2/s, 120/min, 300/h.
Collect status and history (e.g. SCHEDULED ... DELIVERED; CORRUPT if automated QA fails)

endpoints.notes: Your organization's collects
GeoJSON FeatureCollection of places where tasking is disallowed for your organization

STAC API v2 Item for a delivered collect (property umbra:collect_id); assets carry pre-signed, expiring download URLs. The v1 path /stac/collections/{organization_id}/items/{collect_id} is deprecated.
STAC API v2, collection umbra-sar, CQL2; filter on umbra:collect_id. Signed asset URLs are included only when few items are returned (default threshold 5).

api.rate_limits: Per organization, rolling window: 25 reads/s and 5 writes/s on standard endpoints. Create Task and Cancel Task 2/s, 120/min, 300/h. Create Feasibility 2/s, 120/min, 3600/h. Client-credentials token requests 50 per 24 h per client. Limits may change.
api.notes: No RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata: api.canopy.umbra.space returns 401 on /.well-known paths. auth.canopy.umbra.space publishes RFC 8414 metadata with no registration endpoint.

delivery.basis: Canopy Task Lifecycle Tutorial: collect delivery 'will generally happen 1-4 hours after the associated Task's windowEndAt has passed'. Total time also depends on the tasking window you set and on feasibility; Umbra says tasks can generally be submitted up to three hours before the desired collection time.

payment.notes: Billing Terms: self-service Snapshot orders put a hold on a credit card or ACH account at checkout and charge it on delivery; Subscriptions are billed monthly for collects delivered. Enterprise accounts pre-commit to a volume, draw down a shared credit and are invoiced monthly, net 30. The Tasking Terms also allow check or wire transfer, in USD. Fees are non-refundable. No agent payment rail is documented.

requester.checks: Tasking Terms: every Canopy registration is subject to regulatory review by Umbra or a third party, and Umbra may refuse anyone. Customers must represent they are not on US sanctions or export-control lists and must provide compliance documents on request. Restricted Access Areas need screening beyond standard KYC.
requester.unknown: What the regulatory review and KYC check in practice, and how long approval takes, is not published

cards.name: USGS earthquake feed
cards.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey's real-time earthquake feeds list new seismic events worldwide (magnitude, location, depth, time, automatic or reviewed status, tsunami flag, PAGER alert) as GeoJSON updated every minute, free and with no key. Events come from the ANSS Comprehensive Earthquake Catalog (ComCat), which merges solutions from seismic networks around the world. The FDSN event web service filters by time, place, radius, magnitude, alert level and review status.

tasks: earthquakes in the past hour, day, week or 30 days, by magnitude threshold (significant, 4.5+, 2.5+, 1.0+, all)
query earthquake events near a point (latitude, longitude, maxradiuskm) or in a box since a given time, above a magnitude
filter by PAGER alert level (green, yellow, orange, red), review status (automatic or reviewed), significance, felt reports or depth
event detail: magnitude, depth, place, time, status automatic/reviewed, felt reports, tsunami flag, PAGER alert level, and associated products such as ShakeMap, DYFI and moment tensors
watch for new or revised earthquakes by polling a feed, or the query service with updatedafter

pricing.notes: No fee and no key.

latency.typical: USGS FAQ: about 2.5 minutes on average after an earthquake in California, typically within 8 minutes elsewhere in the US, about 20 minutes on average outside the US
latency.notes: The GeoJSON summary feeds are labelled 'Updated every minute'. Per the same FAQ, GeoJSON feeds of 7 days or less are cached for 1 minute, other 7-day-or-less feeds for 5 minutes, and 30-day feeds and searches for 15 minutes, which adds to the delay. A query response on 2026-10-26 carried Cache-Control: public, max-age=60.

coverage.notes: Worldwide. ComCat merges solutions from seismic networks around the world (contributors include US regional networks and agencies in many other countries). USGS says the network is densest in California and sparse in some areas outside the US, so small events abroad are less complete and slower to post.

licensing.summary: USGS says USGS-authored or produced data and information are in the U.S. Public Domain and asks for credit (e.g. 'Credit: U.S. Geological Survey'); not everything on USGS sites is public domain, and copyrighted third-party material needs the holder's permission. USGS gives no warranty of accuracy, completeness or usefulness. Events and products contributed to ComCat by non-USGS networks were not checked separately. The terms do not mention AI training or resale.

freshness.typical_age: Minutes after an event for the real-time feeds; the query service also reaches back through the catalog
freshness.notes: Early values are automatic and are revised as networks and analysts refine them; the 'updated' field changes when they do. Events can also be deleted (the query service returns HTTP 409 for a deleted event unless includedeleted is set).

auth.how_to_get: No key needed.

endpoints.params: level: significant, 4.5, 2.5, 1.0, all; period: hour, day, week, month
endpoints.notes: GeoJSON FeatureCollection, 'Updated every minute'; properties include mag, place, time, updated, status, tsunami, alert, felt, sig, net, ids, sources, nst, dmin, rms, gap, magType, url, detail. USGS recommends these feeds for automated applications.

endpoints.params: eventid, e.g. aka2026vgpxtq (the 'detail' URL in each summary feature)
endpoints.notes: One event with its associated products (origin, phase-data, and where available shakemap, losspager, dyfi, moment-tensor).

endpoints.params: format=geojson (default quakeml; also csv, kml, text, xml); starttime (default now - 30 days), endtime, updatedafter; minlatitude/maxlatitude/minlongitude/maxlongitude or latitude, longitude, maxradiuskm; minmagnitude, maxmagnitude; mindepth, maxdepth; alertlevel, minalertlevel; reviewstatus (automatic, reviewed); eventtype; orderby (time, time-asc, magnitude, magnitude-asc); limit (1-20000); offset; eventid
endpoints.notes: FDSN Event Web Service. Queries over 20,000 events return HTTP 400. Keyless radius query near Ridgecrest, CA returned automatic 'ci' events on 2026-10-26.

endpoints.params: same parameters as query; format=geojson or text or xml
endpoints.notes: Counts matching events; returned {"count":459,"maxAllowed":20000} for starttime=2026-10-25 on 2026-10-26.
Contributing networks; /fdsnws/event/1/catalogs lists catalogs, /fdsnws/event/1/application.json lists enumerated parameter values.

api.rate_limits: None published. The query service caps a request at 20,000 events. USGS asks automated applications to use the real-time GeoJSON feeds rather than the query service whenever possible.
api.sdk: USGS lists libcomcat (Python), matcomcat (Matlab) and an R comcat package on its ANSS Developer's Corner.

mcp.community: No USGS-run MCP server in the official MCP Registry. Third-party earthquake servers are listed, e.g. io.github.cyanheads/earthquake-mcp-server, io.github.mrfentmen/usgs-earthquakes-mcp, com.olyport/earthquake, com.daedalmap/earthquakes.

human.unknown: Events are located automatically from seismic networks; analyst review shows only as status 'reviewed', with no named reviewer

application.unknown: No signing of feed contents; integrity rests on USGS and contributing-network operations

camera.unknown: No imagery

time.method: Each event has an origin time and an 'updated' time in milliseconds
time.unknown: Origin time is an estimate that can be revised; per-event timing uncertainty is not in the summary feed

location.method: Each event carries an estimated epicentre and depth, with solution-quality fields (nst stations used, gap azimuthal gap, dmin distance to nearest station, rms residual)
location.unknown: Location uncertainty varies by region and network density, and is largest where networks are sparse

content.method: Each event has a status field (automatic or reviewed), filterable with reviewstatus, so you can tell which values an analyst has checked
content.unknown: Automatic magnitudes and locations can change substantially after review, and events can be deleted

corroboration.method: The 'ids' and 'sources' fields list every contributing network whose solution was associated with the event. Where networks disagree, ComCat picks a preferred product by weight, favouring the network authoritative for the region; the other solutions stay available in the detail feed.
corroboration.unknown: Many small events have a single contributing network, so nothing independent confirms them

delivery.basis: USGS: feeds 'Updated every minute'; an earthquake is posted in about 2.5 minutes in California, within about 8 minutes elsewhere in the US and about 20 minutes outside the US.
