cards.name: USGS stream gauges
cards.summary: U.S. Geological Survey network of automated stream gauges reporting gage height, discharge and other water parameters, served free through the modernized Water Data OGC API (api.waterdata.usgs.gov). It supersedes the legacy WaterServices APIs, which USGS will retire during its final decommission campaign (November 2026 to February 2027, completing in Q1 2027). About 1,400 USGS river cameras at gauge sites also publish still images every few minutes to every hour through the public NIMS API.

tasks: gage height / stage (parameter 00065)
streamflow discharge (parameter 00060)
water temperature (parameter 00010)
latest observation per time series
historical continuous and daily values
field and channel measurements used to check the sensors
find gauges near a point or in a bounding box
river camera stills (USGS NIMS / HIVIS; capture interval set per camera, from 2 to 60 minutes, some daylight only)

pricing.notes: No fee is charged. The API key is free (managed by api.data.gov, emailed on sign-up) and only raises rate limits. USGS says anyone making more than a few queries per hour needs a key. Keyless requests returned data on 2026-10-26.

latency.typical: About 15-60 minutes behind real time for typical gauges (15-minute recording, roughly hourly transmission)
latency.notes: USGS FAQ: real-time streamflow is typically recorded at 15-minute intervals, stored on site and transmitted to USGS once an hour, depending on the relay technique. Live checks on 2026-10-26 at 04:55 UTC (27 Oct): USGS-01646500 (Potomac) had its newest discharge value at 03:50 UTC, last modified 03:57 UTC, about 65 minutes old. USGS-01650800 had a value at 04:45 UTC, about 10 minutes old.

regions: United States, including Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands
coverage.notes: Only existing fixed gauges; you cannot request a new gauge. The monitoring-locations collection also includes non-USGS agency sites (e.g. a USEPA site in a Washington DC bbox query), not all of which have continuous data. Some sites are discontinued and return null values with a DISCONTINUED qualifier. Live checks on 2026-10-26 found same-day readings in Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands; American Samoa's newest continuous reading was from 2008. River cameras: 1,394 listed in the NIMS API (1,152 not hidden) across most states plus Puerto Rico and Guam. Total gauge count not verified.

licensing.summary: The API's OpenAPI description gives its licence as 'US Government work in the public domain', linking to CC0 1.0. It also links CC0 as the terms of service. USGS says USGS-authored data are U.S. Public Domain and asks for credit (e.g. 'Credit: U.S. Geological Survey'). Not every item on USGS sites is public domain: some third-party images are copyrighted and need the holder's permission. Recent data are provisional and provided on the condition that neither USGS nor the U.S. Government is liable for damages. The terms do not mention AI training or resale. Licensing of non-USGS agency data in the API was not checked.

freshness.typical_age: Typically under ~1-2 hours for active real-time gauges; history back to the period of record
freshness.notes: latest-continuous returns the most recent value per time series; continuous returns full sensor history. Each value carries approval_status: recent values are 'Provisional' and may be substantially revised after field inspections and measurements.

auth.how_to_get: No key needed for light use. USGS says you need a key for more than a few queries per hour.
Optional and free: sign up at https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/signup (an api.data.gov key, sent by email) for higher rate limits.
The same free key, passed as the api_key query parameter.

endpoints.params: bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat; site_type_code (e.g. ST = stream); state_code; limit; f=json
endpoints.notes: Find gauge sites in a box (no radius parameter seen; derive a bbox from a point). Returns GeoJSON with id like USGS-01646500, name, agency, site type, HUC, drainage area and horizontal positional accuracy/method.

endpoints.params: bbox; monitoring_location_id (e.g. USGS-01646500); parameter_code (00060 discharge, 00065 gage height); limit; f=json
endpoints.notes: Most recent observation per time series. Properties: time_series_id, monitoring_location_id, parameter_code, statistic_id, time, value (string), unit_of_measure, approval_status, qualifier, last_modified. Any response property is queryable (see /queryables). Paginate via the 'next' link.

endpoints.params: monitoring_location_id; parameter_code; datetime (instant, start/end interval, '..' open range, or ISO 8601 duration like P7D); limit
endpoints.notes: Full-resolution history from automated sensors.
Most recent daily value per time series; 'daily' collection holds full daily history.

endpoints.params: monitoring_location_id (repeat the parameter for several; a comma list matches nothing); parameter_code (repeatable); computation_type=percentile|median|arithmetic_mean|minimum|maximum; normal_type=DOY (day of year) or MOY; start_date / end_date as MM-DD; page_size (default 1000, max 10000); next_token
endpoints.notes: Replaces the legacy daily statistics (nwis/stat). GeoJSON; per site and parameter, values per time_of_year with percentiles 5/10/25/50/75/90/95 and sample_count (years), computed on approved data. Use parent_statistic_id 00003 (percentiles of the daily mean). Beta: USGS says it is subject to change. Served through the same api.data.gov gateway; the signup page's key is for 'USGS water data APIs' and no statistics-specific limit is published.
Manual discharge and gage-height measurements USGS uses to check and correct automated records; latest-field-measurements and channel-measurements also exist.

River cameras with camId, nwisId, coordinates, newestImageDT, ingest schedule (interval in minutes, 24/7 or daylight) and image directories (smallDir 720 px, thumbDir, overlayDir, tlDir) on public S3.
Newest image filenames for a camera, newest first; image URL = camera.smallDir + filename.

api.rate_limits: No numbers published for keyless use. USGS says more than a few queries per hour needs a key. Keys are optional, free api.data.gov keys (X-Api-Key header or api_key query parameter) and give more requests per hour; going over returns HTTP 429. The X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining response headers report the limit (the docs example shows 1000), but keyless responses on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-28 carried no such headers. USGS asks anyone needing custom limits to write to wdfn@usgs.gov.

mcp.community: No USGS-run MCP server in the official MCP Registry. Third-party servers are listed, e.g. io.github.cyanheads/usgs-water-mcp-server, io.github.mansurjisan/usgs-mcp, io.github.mrfentmen/usgs-water-mcp, com.olyport/water.

api.notes: 2026-10-28: USGS is retiring the legacy WaterServices (Instantaneous Values, Daily Values, Statistics, Site). Per USGS: a 2 s delay on every request from 2026-11-16, 10 s from 2027-01-11, 30 s from 2027-01-25, 60 s from 2027-02-01, redirect outages on 2027-01-27 (about 24 h) and 2027-02-15 (about 48 h), shut down on 2027-02-22. irlpls (adapter, landing page, browser 'Get it now') uses only api.waterdata.usgs.gov: latest-continuous for readings, monitoring-locations for names, statistics/v0/observationNormals for the usual range for a date, NIMS for cameras.

human.unknown: Not applicable in the usual sense: readings come from automated government-operated instruments, not from individual contributors

application.unknown: No public attestation or signing of data from gauge to API; integrity rests on USGS operating the network

camera.unknown: River camera stills come from fixed USGS-installed cameras at gauge sites; no capture signing or tamper evidence is documented, so whether a frame is unaltered rests on trust in USGS operations.

time.method: Each value carries an observation time and a last_modified timestamp, as USGS reports them.
time.unknown: How logger clocks are set or checked was not found in the docs read; nothing is signed or time-stamped by a third party.

location.method: Fixed sites with published coordinates plus horizontal positional accuracy and method fields in monitoring-locations (e.g. 'Interpolated from map', 'Mapping grade GPS unit')
location.unknown: Accuracy varies by site and many coordinates are interpolated from maps; the fields are agency-entered, not independently attested

content.method: Improbable values relayed by telemetry are automatically screened until verified. Values carry approval_status (Provisional or Approved) and qualifiers. USGS states provisional data may be inaccurate due to instrument malfunctions or site changes and may be substantially revised after field inspections and measurements.
content.unknown: Provisional values (the freshest ones) can be substantially wrong; the screening rules and review procedure were not read in detail

corroboration.method: Field measurements and channel measurements collections expose the manual readings USGS uses to check and correct automated records
corroboration.unknown: How often a given gauge is field-checked, and how far provisional values drift before correction, was not established

cards.name: Vangrid
cards.short: Pay a USDC bounty by x402 and a contributor films a place; you get a capture link and a 3D model.
cards.summary: Vangrid runs a bounty board for ground-level video captures of real places. An agent posts a bounty in one HTTP call, paying the amount in USDC on Base or Arc through x402 with no account or API key; contributors with the Vangrid capture app film it, the agent reviews watermarked previews and accepts one, and receives a capture link (processed on the device: Vangrid's docs say requesters never receive raw video) plus a textured 3D model (GLB). Every capture is fingerprinted (content sha256, coarse geohash, timestamp) and the fingerprints are committed in Merkle trees whose roots are attested on Base through EAS, so anyone can check that a capture's hash existed by the end of its window. Faces, plates and bodies are blurred on the device. Pay-per-request endpoints also return metadata for captures already anchored.

tasks: walk-around video capture of a specific place (loading dock, forecourt, junction, building, stock room)
3D reconstruction of the accepted capture as a textured GLB mesh
ground-level spatial data for robotics, mapping and world models
lookup of already-anchored captures by area and time window (metadata only)
free provenance check of a capture's sha256 against its Base anchor

delivery.basis: Agent bounty docs: 'A person has to go and film, so this takes hours or days.' Deadline 1 to 30 days (default 7); reconstruction after acceptance 'typically takes 30 minutes or more'.

latency.typical: Hours to days for a contributor to film; then 30+ minutes of reconstruction after you accept
latency.notes: The bounty is posted to the board within a minute of payment. Submissions arrive when a contributor goes and films; nothing guarantees anyone will. The deadline is 1 to 30 days (default 7); after it, or on cancel while open, the full amount is refunded on the network it was paid on. Accepting is final.

freshness.typical_age: Usually filmed after the bounty is posted, but a contributor may submit a clip captured earlier
freshness.notes: The bounties guide says a contributor can 'Record a new one, or use a clip you have already captured.' Submissions show submitted_at, not capture time; the capture time is in the anchored fingerprint, checkable with the free provenance endpoint. The pay-per-request index returns metadata (sha256, geohash, capture time, anchor) of existing captures, not media.

pricing.model: bounty (escrowed USDC, set by the buyer)
pricing.notes: The buyer sets amount_usdc in whole USDC; the server's default minimum and maximum are 50 and 5,000 (quoted in the discovery metadata). The amount is escrowed on chain and released on acceptance: Vangrid currently keeps a 10% platform fee and about $5 for reconstruction and pays the rest to the contributor (a $50 reward pays $40); the docs call these figures examples that can change. Reconstruction is included; no second payment. Full refund on cancel while open or on expiry. Pay-per-request data: $0.01 per spatial query, $0.005 per observation, provenance check free; prices are quoted per request and can change. Enterprise API pricing is by quote.

payment.notes: Agents pay through x402 v2 (exact scheme) in USDC on Base (eip155:8453) or Arc (eip155:5042); the 402 quote lists both and the transfer settles before the bounty is created. No gas needed on Base. People post on the web board by funding the escrow from a wallet. The amount is escrowed up front and refunded to the paying wallet on cancel or expiry. Enterprise pilots are priced by contract.

coverage.notes: Coverage follows contributors: densest in metro areas, sparser elsewhere. The Terms (s.15) say the service is not offered to residents of Illinois, Texas and Washington (USA), Germany, France, Italy, mainland China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba and Crimea (this applies to anyone using the service, so presumably also to bounty buyers), and uploads are blocked in some regions by capture location and network region. Contributors may not capture private property, home or vehicle interiors, schools, playgrounds, healthcare, places of worship, military or critical-infrastructure perimeters, or identifiable minors. A public explorer tree from 2026-09-24 listed captures from cities on several continents (e.g. Istanbul, Atlanta, Amsterdam, Nairobi, Sydney, Jakarta, Tokyo).

licensing.summary: The Terms say contributors keep ownership of their captures and grant Vangrid a worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sublicensable, transferable licence to process, distribute and commercialise them and their derivatives. What licence the bounty buyer receives to the capture or model is not stated anywhere. The Privacy Policy says Vangrid processes captures to train spatial models and may license filtered datasets to defense and government customers under use restrictions, robotics, world-model and AI labs, and infrastructure operators, so a commissioned capture is not exclusive.

requester.checks: None documented for buyers: there is no account and no API key; an agent pays from any wallet, gets a one-time agent_token, and Vangrid posts the title and brief to the board from its operator wallet within a minute. The rules sit with contributors: the Terms forbid capturing private spaces, identifiable minors and sensitive sites, and ban harassing or stalking any person.
requester.unknown: Whether briefs are screened before posting, and how a request to film a specific person would be refused, is not stated.

access.notes: Terms s.8 bans 'bots, automated tools, fabricated GPS data, or spoofed locations' for all users; read in context it targets faked captures, and the agent API with x402 is explicitly offered.

auth.how_to_get: x402 v2: call without payment, read the 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, sign an exact USDC authorization on Base or Arc and retry. No account or key; needs a wallet holding USDC.
The agent_token (vgb_...) returned once by POST /bounties; it is the only credential for that bounty's status, accept and cancel calls.
GET /provenance/{hash} is free and needs no payment or token.

endpoints.params: title (3-200 chars), brief (20-4000 chars), amount_usdc (integer; default range 50-5000), deadline_days (1-30, default 7)
endpoints.notes: Paid by x402: the price is exactly amount_usdc, settled before processing. Returns bounty_id, agent_token (once), poll_url.

Free. Status (paid, open, accepting, accepted, cancelling, cancelled, expired, expired_refunded, failed), onchain_id, board_url, transactions, and submissions with watermarked preview_url (15 min) and quality_status pass/fail.

After POST /bounties/{id}/accept {submission_id} (free, final, releases the escrow), the accepted submission carries full_capture_url, model_glb_url and model_zip_url as signed links valid 15 minutes. POST /bounties/{id}/cancel refunds while open.

endpoints.params: aoi (GeoJSON Point with radius_m 1-5000, or Polygon up to 100 km2), from, to, limit (1-1000)
endpoints.notes: $0.01 by x402. Returns already-anchored captures: sha256, 6-character geohash, captured_at and Base anchor. No media.
$0.005 by x402. One anchored observation. GET /provenance/{hash} answers the same check for free.

mcp.auth: x402 from a local wallet (EVM_PRIVATE_KEY), with MAX_USD_PER_CALL and MAX_USD_PER_BOUNTY caps
mcp.notes: Open-source (MIT) stdio server github.com/vangrid-labs/bounty-mcp, run with npx -y github:vangrid-labs/bounty-mcp. Tools: vangrid_post_bounty, vangrid_bounty_status, vangrid_accept_submission, vangrid_cancel_bounty, vangrid_coverage_query, vangrid_observation, vangrid_verify_provenance. Accept and cancel are free and irreversible and not covered by the spend caps. Not in the official MCP Registry.

api.notes: Discovery: an x402 manifest at https://data.vangrid.io/.well-known/x402 lists the paid resources, networks and payTo address. A separate Enterprise Spatial API (api.vangrid.io/v1, bearer API keys, spatial query, ingest, streaming) is granted per pilot by contacting sales.

human.unknown: Contributors sign in with a wallet and need an invite code to upload; no identity check is documented, and buyers see no contributor identity.

application.unknown: Captures are recorded in the Vangrid capture app (browser or Android) and checked at ingest for quality, length, camera/location consistency and duplicates (content checks, not attestation). Vangrid says hardware-backed device attestation is 'not live yet' and that the fingerprint 'says nothing about the device that produced it'. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Recorded through the app's camera; the Terms ban fabricated, manipulated, staged or AI-generated content; ingest rejects duplicates. No signed capture or C2PA; Vangrid is not on the C2PA conforming products list, so nothing proves the video came from a real sensor rather than a screen or generator.

time.method: Each capture's fingerprint (content sha256, coarse geohash, timestamp) becomes a leaf in a Merkle tree (keccak256, sorted pairs, odd nodes hashed with themselves) whose root is attested on Base through EAS when its window closes (about every 15 to 35 minutes). Vangrid's provenance endpoint maps a sha256 to its leaf, root and attestation.
time.unknown: Claimed, not evidenced: the leaf encoding is not published, so linking a capture's sha256 to its leaf requires Vangrid's provenance endpoint, and the published proofs omit the self-pair steps for odd nodes (61 of 317 leaves in tree 5776 fail an independent sorted-pair recomputation, though Vangrid's endpoint reports one of them verified). Restore evidenced when Vangrid publishes the leaf encoding and odd-node rule, or proofs a standard verifier accepts. The anchor shows a leaf existed no later than the window close; the capture time inside the fingerprint is device-reported, a bounty submission may be a clip filmed before the bounty was posted, and the attester address is not documented as Vangrid's.

location.method: Location is optional; when given it is checked for consistency with camera signals at ingest, and a 6-character geohash (about 1.2 km by 0.6 km) is anchored in the fingerprint.
location.unknown: The anchored location is device-reported and coarse; GPS/motion cross-correlation against spoofing is 'not live yet', and some bounties may receive captures with no location at all.

content.method: Automated quality check per submission (quality_status pending/pass/fail); the buyer reviews a watermarked preview against the brief before accepting one.
content.unknown: The automated check covers quality and length, not whether the clip shows the place in the brief; that judgment is the buyer's.

corroboration.unknown: A bounty delivers one contributor's capture. Independent verifiers under collateral are 'not live yet'; the multi-view ground_truth_score described for the enterprise query API is not part of bounty delivery.

custody.method: Each capture's fingerprint is registered as a leaf in a Merkle tree whose root is attested on Base through EAS; Vangrid's provenance endpoint returns a capture's leaf, root and attestation.
custody.unknown: A registration record, not per-hop custody. The leaf encoding is unpublished and 61 of 317 proofs in tree 5776 fail an independent recomputation, so the capture-to-anchor link rests on Vangrid's API; whether the delivered full_capture_url hashes to the anchored sha256 is not stated.

cards.name: Vantor Hub (WorldView tasking)
cards.short: Task WorldView optical, 3D and radar captures by API.
cards.summary: Vantor (formerly Maxar Intelligence) sells new WorldView satellite collections through the Vantor Hub APIs: a Tasking V2 API for FastView (collection guaranteed within 24 hours of a chosen start) and FlexView (cloud, angle and sun limits) 2D imagery, WorldView 3D elevation products, and limited-release WorldView Radar tasking of Umbra SAR. Requests need an end-use code, quotes reserve account credits, and by default tasked imagery joins Vantor's public catalogue unless the account has private tasking.

tasks: task a new WorldView 2D collection over a point or polygon within a collection window (FastView or FlexView)
check feasibility (High, Medium or Low probability) before tasking
quote credits before submitting (estimate endpoints)
task WorldView 3D elevation products and, in limited release, Umbra SAR spotlight scenes
stereo pairs (FlexView only), private tasking (account option)
search the archive and order imagery (Discovery and Ordering APIs), monitor areas

pricing.model: credits reserved at submission; billed per area collected
pricing.notes: Docs: 'A usage quote is calculated when a request is submitted... Account credits are reserved'; unused credits are released; tasking minimum 50 km2, maximum 1000 km2; Umbra radar priced per 5 km x 5 km scene by resolution and dwell. Vantor's Hub page says 'credits model with transparent pricing' and 'One subscription, unlimited seats'; no dollar figures were found.

latency.typical: FastView: collected within 24 h of a start time set 8 h to 14 days ahead; FlexView: any window up to 364 days, start can be 'now'
latency.notes: FastView docs: 'Within 24 hours of the requested start time, an image will be collected'; availability is a reservation and an unavailable date returns 400 with future dates. FlexView honours cloud and angle limits so may take longer. Time from capture to delivery is not stated in the pages read. Shared limit of 1000 new tasking requests per hour across all customers.

coverage.notes: Docs list 'high demand' countries where tasking is harder: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Benin, China (East), Colombia, Congo, Cyprus, Ecuador, Gabon, Gaza Strip, Georgia, Iran, Iraq, Israel, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, North Korea, Nigeria, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Korea, Syria, Taiwan, Togo, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, West Bank, Yemen. Each request carries a required end-use code (e.g. AGR, COM, DNI, USG). Vantor publishes licence documents (internal use, subscription services, display media, fedgov and others) at vantor.com/resources/, which were not read, so resale, AI training and ownership are left unstated.

time.unknown: A refresh-rate field and service-status field are supplied per camera, but no trusted capture timestamp or signature is documented.

cards.name: WeatherXM Agent API
cards.summary: WeatherXM, which runs a community network of independently operated weather stations (its own pages claim 9,500+ deployed, 5,900+ active, 85+ countries), sells weather by latitude and longitude to software agents through an x402 API: current conditions, a 7-day hourly and daily forecast, and one day of history from the last 4 days. Each call costs $0.001 in USDC on Base, paid in the request with no account or API key. /api/health is free. The OpenAPI spec says data_source 'live' means data 'from a weather provider' and 'sample' means static testnet data; it does not say that a reading comes from a named station or from the station network, and responses carry no station ID. No payment was made, so no real response was seen.
cards.short: Weather by lat/lon for $0.001 USDC per call via x402, no key.

tasks: current conditions at a latitude/longitude: temperature, feels-like, wind speed and direction, UV index, precipitation and its probability, pressure, humidity (GET /api/current)
7-day forecast, 168 hourly and 7 daily entries (GET /api/forecast)
hourly and daily weather for one date within the last 4 days (GET /api/history)

pricing.notes: $0.001 USDC per call on /api/current, /api/forecast and /api/history (402 response: amount 1000 in USDC's 6-decimal units on Base, eip155:8453). /api/health is free. Larger or key-based access is sold separately through WeatherXM Pro, whose prices were not read.

latency.typical: Not stated
latency.notes: The OpenAPI spec returns 204 when there is no current data within a plus-or-minus 1 hour window. The weatherxm.com/data page warns that an observation's timestamp, its aggregation interval and the moment it is available through the API are three different things, and gives no number.

regions: Global: any latitude/longitude is accepted; density follows the station network
coverage.notes: The API takes any lat (-90 to 90) and lon (-180 to 180). WeatherXM's own pages claim 9,500+ stations deployed in 85+ countries (weatherxm.com/network) and, as an August 2026 snapshot, 5,900+ active and 4,300+ synoptic quality (weatherxm.com/data). It lists no countries, and the spec does not say whether or how far a point may be from a station.

licensing.summary: No licence for Agent API data is stated on the pages read. weatherxm.com/terms (last updated August 2026) covers the websites, station hardware and 'integrating with WeatherXM APIs', names the 'x402 Agent API' as a way to pay for access, and says 'Redistribution of bulk raw telemetry without appropriate licensing is prohibited.' It says forecasts and observations are provided as-is and are not the sole basis for life-critical decisions. The Pro Terms of Service (PDF, for business customers on a subscription) license data by tier, require credit 'Data provided by WeatherXM Association' where attribution applies, bar selling or passing data on to third parties under the commercial tier except in products without 'Substantial Amounts of Data', and do not mention x402. The Network Association says full commercial licences of the whole dataset are auctioned, four a year. AI or ML training and resale are not mentioned in any of these, and whether a $0.001 call grants more than personal use is not stated.

freshness.typical_age: Not stated
freshness.notes: On demand per call. Forecast and 4-day history are also offered, but irlpls lists this for current conditions.

delivery.basis: The spec's /api/current says 'Get current weather conditions' and returns 204 if there is no data within a plus-or-minus 1 hour window; no delivery time is stated.

auth.how_to_get: GET /api/health needs nothing. The data endpoints need no key or login either, only payment: an unpaid request returns 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header (base64 JSON, x402 version 2, scheme exact, USDC on Base eip155:8453, amount 1000, a payTo address, 300 s timeout). Retry with an x402 payment from the agent's own wallet; the mainnet facilitator is Coinbase CDP. A testnet server at https://agent-testnet.weatherxm.com uses Base Sepolia.

endpoints.params: lat, lon (required); tz (IANA or auto), units (metric or imperial)
endpoints.notes: $0.001 USDC. 200 gives location, current{time, temperature, feels_like, wind_speed, wind_direction, uv_index, precipitation_probability, precipitation, pressure, humidity}, timezone, units and data_source (live = 'from a weather provider'; sample = static testnet data, per the spec); 204 if no data within +/-1 h.
$0.001 USDC. 168 hourly and 7 daily entries.

endpoints.params: lat, lon, date YYYY-MM-DD (required, within the last 4 days); tz, units
endpoints.notes: $0.001 USDC. 24 hourly entries and 1 daily entry.
Free, no payment. Returned status ok, version 1.0.0, network mainnet on 2026-11-04.

api.rate_limits: Not stated in the spec.
api.notes: The spec lists lat and lon as strings although they are numbers. No /.well-known/ucp, agent-card.json, irlpls or oauth-protected-resource file exists on agent.weatherxm.com (all 404). A separate keyed REST API (stations/near, stations/{id}/latest, history, cells/{h3}/forecast) is sold as WeatherXM Pro at https://pro.weatherxm.com/ and is not covered by this card.

payment.notes: Per-call USDC micropayment on Base through x402, signed by the agent's own wallet; no card, invoice or account. The OpenAPI spec describes the API as built for agent workflows and names Coinbase AgentKit as a client.

requester.checks: None beyond payment: no account, key or identity check is described for the x402 endpoints.
requester.unknown: Not stated whether any request-time check beyond payment applies.

human.unknown: Stations are run by owners (businesses, landowners and communities) but no person-level identity check is described for readings.

application.method: weatherxm.com/network says sensors sign observations 'at the source'; weatherxm.com/data says 'Supported stations sign each observation in hardware'; /network/quality says 'device identity and signing, where the hardware supports it' establish which station produced a reading.
application.unknown: Signing depends on hardware support and the method and keys are not described on the pages read. The Agent API response carries no station ID, signature or hash, so a buyer cannot check a signature, and it is not stated that API values are signed station data.

camera.unknown: No imagery.

time.method: Each reading has an ISO 8601 time with offset in the response.
time.unknown: How station clocks are checked is not described, no trusted time-stamp is documented, and the API's availability delay is not stated.

location.method: WeatherXM scores station location 0 to 1 daily from 'Location Packets' (Proof of Location); a relocated station drops to 0 for a penalty period.
location.unknown: The pages do not say how Location Packets are generated (for example GNSS), and the score is WeatherXM's own with no public proof. The Agent API returns the requested lat/lon, not the station's, and does not say which station or how far away it is.

content.method: WeatherXM describes five checks on station data: physical limits, weather dynamics, siting signature, photographic audit, and obstruction analysis; results feed a station quality assessment visible to the owner.
content.unknown: No thresholds are published, WeatherXM says a quality score 'is not a statement of sensor accuracy and it is not a certification', and the Agent API response gives no quality score. The spec says data_source 'live' is from 'a weather provider', so it is not stated that Agent API values are station readings that passed these checks.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-check between stations or sources is documented for what the Agent API returns.

sources.claim: OpenAPI 3.1 spec v1.0.0: endpoints /api/current, /api/forecast, /api/history at $0.001 USDC, parameters, responses (200 with data_source live or sample, 204 outside +/-1 h, 402, 502), x402 on Base and Base Sepolia, facilitators x402.org (testnet) and Coinbase CDP (mainnet), free /api/health, servers agent.weatherxm.com and agent-testnet.weatherxm.com; data_source live = 'from a weather provider', sample = static testnet data
Free health check returned status ok, version 1.0.0, network mainnet (2026-11-04 15:47 UTC)
Unpaid GET /api/current returned HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header decoding to x402 version 2, scheme exact, network eip155:8453, amount 1000, USDC asset, 300 s timeout (2026-11-04)
/.well-known/ucp, agent-card.json, irlpls and oauth-protected-resource returned 404 on agent.weatherxm.com (2026-11-04)
Official MCP Registry search for weatherxm returned no servers (2026-11-04)

Terms (last updated August 2026): scope includes WeatherXM APIs; section 4 names the x402 Agent API; bulk raw telemetry redistribution prohibited without licensing; as-is disclaimer; AI training and resale not mentioned

Pro Terms of Service PDF: Data licence tiers (free personal and academic, paid commercial), attribution 'Data provided by WeatherXM Association', no Distribution to third parties and no Substantial Amounts of Data in customer services, no mention of x402 or AI training

5,900+ active and 4,300+ synoptic quality stations, 85+ countries (network snapshot August 2026); 'Supported stations sign each observation in hardware'; WeatherXM AG and Network Association roles; x402 machine-to-machine option; latency caveat; Pro REST API endpoints (a deployed count of 9,500+ is not on this page)

cards.name: WeGoLook
cards.summary: On-demand field workers ('Lookers') who go to a vehicle, property or site and capture photos, video and checklist answers in the WeGoLook app. A public order portal sells fixed-price vehicle inspections (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) from $99; insurers and other enterprises buy custom workflows by contract. WeGoLook is a Crawford & Company subsidiary (Crawford bought 85 percent in January 2017) and also powers Crawford's alternative claims inspections.
cards.short: Sends a local inspector to photograph and video a vehicle or property; online vehicle inspections from $99.

tasks: vehicle inspection ordered online: auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft
VIN and damage verification
working demonstration and walk-around video
auto and fleet claims inspection
non-complex property inspection
roof and interior/exterior property inspection (Crawford AIS network)
vacant land inspection
underwriting and real estate portfolio inspection
notice delivery and product recall checks
notarized document looks
self-service looks (customer or employee collected)
custom workflow integrations

pricing.model: fixed price per online inspection; enterprise by quote
pricing.notes: The $99 base and add-on prices could not be re-checked (the portal renders client-side). The public order portal listed Instant Inspection - Auto at a base price of $99, with add-ons: working demonstration and exterior walk-around videos $35, three-day rush delivery $35, two-day rush delivery $50. The same five vehicle products (auto, heavy equipment, motorcycle, RV, watercraft) are listed. Enterprise and claims work (Standard, Self-Service and Custom Looks) has no public price. Looker pay, per the app store listings, is mostly $15-$25 per Look.

latency.typical: About 1.6 days to first inspection on average, against a two-day SLA (2022 claims brochure); rush delivery in two or three days can be bought online
latency.notes: The 2022 brochure also gives 38 minutes average time to first contact and 11.2 miles average Looker distance. The order portal sells three-day and two-day rush delivery as paid add-ons, so standard online delivery is slower than three days, but the standard window is not stated. Crawford says many of its services can be delivered 'as rapidly as same day'. App store listings say most Looks take under an hour on site.

coverage.notes: Over 45,000 Lookers claimed. Crawford describes the Looker network as recruited 'in the U.S.' and lists 'Locations Served: United States' for its WeGoLook contacts; the Looker onboarding site says 'nationwide network'. The homepage and 2022 brochure say 'global' and 'around the globe', but no non-US country is named. A Crawford brochure footer says 'Additional countries served by Crawford's global network'. No city list or density data is public.

licensing.summary: No client terms for deliverables are public: ownership, resale and AI training are not stated. The site Terms (last updated July 1, 2020) say users grant Crawford Inspection Services a license to use their Submissions, and that site content belongs to Crawford Inspection Services or its licensors. The privacy policy (April 27, 2023) says WeGoLook does not sell personal data for money but may share it 'in exchange for other value, such as data analytics'. Enterprise contracts may differ.

human.unknown: Lookers are independent contractors who apply through the app or onboarding site; notary Looks require a notary license and roof inspectors are described as experienced. No identity check, background check or vetting process is described on a provider page. Older partner announcements (2010-2011) describe background-checked Lookers; WeGoLook's current site states no check.

application.unknown: Lookers capture in the WeGoLook mobile app, and release notes describe in-app photo validation and enforced in-app capture for 'v2' Looks, but no app-integrity check, Play Integrity or App Attest use is documented. No C2PA signing; WeGoLook is not on the C2PA Conforming Products List. Capture in the provider's own app or rig is not a server-verified attestation (STANDARD §3).

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: Release notes describe the app's own camera components (front/rear switch, flash, zoom, enforced landscape capture) for photos and video on v2 Looks. Whether gallery uploads are blocked on every Look type, and whether a photo of a screen would be caught, is not stated.

time.method: Reports state an inspection date and time
time.unknown: How the inspection time is recorded (device clock, server receipt or Looker entry) is not stated, and photos carry no visible per-photo timestamp in the sample report.

location.unknown: The app collects precise location and the Terms mention Google geo-location services, but no geofencing or per-photo location check is described. The sample report shows only a city. GPS spoofing risk unknown.

content.method: 'Quality assurance' is listed as a benefit on the homepage; Looks follow a fixed shot list and checklist (see sample report)
content.unknown: No description of what the QA involves, who performs it, or whether every report is reviewed.

corroboration.unknown: No public statement on second-source checks, re-inspections or fraud-rate reporting.

delivery.basis: 2022 brochure: average time to first inspection 1.6 days, two-day SLA; the order portal sells two- and three-day rush delivery.

freshness.typical_age: captured after the order, usually within days
freshness.notes: Each Look is a new on-site capture.

mcp.notes: No entry in the official MCP Registry for 'wegolook' or 'crawford' (2026-10-26).

payment.notes: Online orders are paid at checkout by credit card or PayPal; the order portal redirects to a hosted payment page (Authorize.net or PayPal Express Checkout), per its public config and code (Stripe also appears in that config). Enterprise billing terms are not public.

cards.name: Windy Webcams
cards.short: A directory of public webcams worldwide, with current images through an API.
cards.summary: Large global directory of public webcams run by third-party operators, with a REST API (v3) to find webcams near a point or in a bounding box and get current image URLs, live/timelapse player embeds and location metadata.

tasks: current still image of a place from a fixed public webcam
find webcams within a radius (up to 250 km) or bounding box
live stream / daily, monthly, yearly timelapse player embeds
visual check of weather, snow, sea state, crowds or traffic at a camera's view

pricing.model: freemium (free tier plus annual professional subscription)
pricing.unit: free tier; Professional 9,990 EUR per year
pricing.notes: Free tier: limited image size, image URLs valid for a short time (15 minutes on the pricing page, 10 minutes in the docs), pagination offset capped at 1000; images must be linked to windy.com or shown via the embeddable timelapse player, which may carry Windy ads. Professional: 9,990 EUR per year, paid annually in advance and auto-renewing; full-size images, image URLs valid 24 hours, offset up to 10,000, no ads in the timelapse player, and an all-webcams export in one call. No USD price published. The free tier may not be offered only inside the paid part of a user's app.

latency.typical: Returned on request; the image is the camera's most recent upload, its age shown by lastUpdatedOn
latency.notes: No per-camera refresh interval is published. Windy defines an Active Webcam as one updated within the last 24 hours, so an active camera's image can still be hours old. Docs recommend calling the webcams endpoint on every page load because image URL tokens expire (10 minutes free per the docs, 15 minutes per the pricing page; 24 hours professional). Windy does not guarantee the number of active webcams, the availability of any webcam, or image quality.

regions: Global (wherever webcams are registered; dense in Europe and tourist/ski/coastal areas, uneven elsewhere)
coverage.notes: Only existing webcams with fixed views; you cannot point or add a camera on request. Windy calls it 'the largest collection of webcams worldwide'; Windy staff: '70 000+' webcams (2026-05-28). Filters by country, region, city, continent and 18 categories (airport, beach, building, city, coast, forest, indoor, lake, landscape, meteo, mountain, observatory, port, river, sportArea, square, traffic, village). Terms describe webcams as mounted outdoors to monitor the general natural environment.

licensing.summary: Specific Terms of Use of the Windy Webcams API (effective 1 Sept 2023) govern and prevail over the general terms. They forbid redistributing any part of the API or its data to third parties, further redistributing the Content, giving third parties access to the API or your key, letting third parties build services on it, publishing any graphics displaying webcam images, stretching images, using image URLs other than those the API returns, continuous scanning of many webcams or downloading significant parts of image history, intensive automated use of any endpoint, and trying to identify people in the images. Users must visibly credit 'Webcams provided by windy.com - add new webcam' with links. Copyright stays with Windy and its suppliers (the webcam operators). General Windy terms add: no selling, renting or sublicensing Content, use for your own internal purposes only, and webcam images are excluded from the general permission to reuse Windy visuals. So an agent should not hand an image to a different person or publish a graphic showing it (Art. 10.1, 11.2); show it only through the player or the API URL to the key holder. AI or ML training and caching are not mentioned.

human.unknown: Who operates each camera. Terms define webcams as owned or operated by third-party Webcam Operators; no operator identity check is documented.

application.unknown: Whether images come straight from the camera or are re-uploaded or edited; terms say images 'may be further processed' by Windy. No signing or capture attestation is documented.

camera.unknown: Whether the feed is a real camera view or a looped or replaced image; no checks documented, and Windy says it has 'absolutely no control over the images'.

time.method: API returns lastUpdatedOn (ISO 8601) per webcam
time.unknown: How the timestamp is set (camera clock or upload time) and whether stale or frozen images are detected. 'Active' only means updated within 24 hours.

location.method: API returns WGS84 latitude/longitude plus city, region and country for each webcam
location.unknown: Whether coordinates are operator-entered or checked, and where the camera actually points.

content.unknown: Whether images are staged, overlaid or heavily compressed. Windy gives no guarantee and takes no responsibility for webcam content. Status values (unapproved, rejected, duplicate) suggest listings are reviewed, but no review process is documented.

corroboration.unknown: No cross-checking between cameras or against other sources documented; each webcam has an edit URL for public feedback.

auth.how_to_get: Register a Windy account and create a Webcams API key at https://api.windy.com/keys (sign-in required); a new key may take a few minutes to become active worldwide. The key must not be published or shared with third parties.

endpoints.params: nearby={lat},{lon},{radius_km} (max 250 km); bbox={north_lat},{east_lon},{south_lat},{west_lon}; categories (max 10), categoryOperation (and|or), continents (max 2), countries, regions, cities, webcamIds (max 50, overrides other filters); include=categories,images,location,player,urls; limit (0-50, default 10); offset (max 1000 free, 10000 professional); sortKey (popularity|createdOn), sortDirection; lang
endpoints.notes: Use include=images to get current/daylight image URLs and sizes; include=player for live and timelapse embed URLs. Image URLs carry expiring tokens and return HTTP 401 once expired.
Single webcam with fresh image URLs; response has status (active, inactive, ...), lastUpdatedOn, viewCount, location, player URLs and provider URL.

endpoints.params: northLat, southLat, eastLon, westLon, zoom (4-18), include, lang
endpoints.notes: Webcams spread for map display in a bounding box; maximum box size depends on zoom level.
Also /continents, /countries, /regions, /cities return geo codes usable as filters.
Basic info for all webcams in one file; professional tier only.

api.rate_limits: No numeric rate limit published. Terms forbid intensive use of any endpoint by automated software, continuous scanning of a significant number of webcams, downloading significant portions of image history, and placing inappropriate load on the API. Tier limits: pagination offset 1000 (free) vs 10000 (professional), limit max 50 per call.

mcp.notes: No Windy or Windy webcams server in the official MCP Registry (searches 'windy', 'windyty', 'webcam' on 2026-10-26).

api.notes: No OAuth: /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and oauth-authorization-server return 404 on api.windy.com and windy.com. The all-webcams export returns 403 without a key.

freshness.typical_age: Most recent image uploaded by each camera; varies per camera (see lastUpdatedOn)
freshness.notes: Current and daylight images plus a live player for streaming cameras. Timelapse players (day/month/year/lifetime) show past imagery but irlpls uses only the current image. An Active Webcam is one updated within the last 24 hours. No on-demand capture.

delivery.basis: Docs: call /webcams/api/v3/webcams or /webcams/api/v3/webcams/{webcamId} every time the page is loaded to get current image URLs, whose tokens expire after 10 minutes (free) or 24 hours (professional).

access.notes: Light use only: the API terms (Art. 8.2.2) ban intensive automated use of any endpoint and (Art. 8.2.1) continuous scanning of many webcams.

payment.notes: Free tier needs no payment. Professional is an annual subscription paid in advance through a third party when upgrading on api.windy.com, renewing automatically until cancelled. No agent payment rail is documented; the payment processor and accepted methods are not named.

requester.checks: A Windy account is needed to create an API key; requests are identified by key and Windy may log API use.
requester.unknown: No identity or use-case check beyond account registration is documented.

sources.claim: Auth header x-windy-api-key; keys at api.windy.com/keys, may take minutes to activate; image URL tokens expire after 10 minutes (free) or 24 hours (professional) and then return HTTP 401; call /webcams or /webcams/{webcamId} on every page load

cards.summary: Washington State DOT publishes about 1,700 camera feeds (state highways, mountain passes, airports, ferry terminals, and some partner cameras such as Oregon DOT's around Portland), each a still JPEG that refreshes about every 5 minutes with the date and time printed on it. cards.name: Zeitview
cards.summary: Asset intelligence company (formerly DroneBase) whose pilots collect drone, fixed-wing and robotic-crawler data for energy, utility and property assets, then add AI analysis and expert review. It also sells fixed-price drone photo and video packages for US commercial real estate, and has a contact-gated Partners API for bulk mission orders.
cards.short: Drone inspections of energy, utility and property assets; fixed-price US real estate drone photo packages.

tasks: solar inspection (visual and thermal)
wind turbine inspection (onshore and offshore; external and internal blades, towers, nacelles; lightning protection testing)
electric utility circuit patrol, vegetation encroachment, thermal hotspot and substation inspection
aerial methane detection and quantification for oil and gas
roof, facade, pavement and landscaping property assessments with 1-100 condition scores

Each package includes up to one hour of flight time on site and image hosting. Volume and enterprise pricing by contact. Enterprise terms: fees in USD, quotes valid 90 days, fees non-cancellable and non-refundable.

Terms treat severe weather as force majeure.

delivery.basis: Commercial real estate page: "Zeitview will visit and fly the site within a few days (subject to weather). After the flight, allow two additional business days for aerial marketing packages, and three to five business days for edited marketing videos." Other services: not published.

freshness.notes: Each image in the Partners API carries a taken_at timestamp. Zeitview also analyses data that customers collect themselves (bring your own data).

coverage.notes: The About page claims coverage in 80+ countries and "the largest drone pilot network in the industry". Other pages give lower, segment-specific figures: properties 20+ countries, solar 70+, wind 40. The properties and solar pages claim 80,000 pilots; the utilities page says 11K+, described as US utility coverage. Real estate packages cover "anywhere in the continental United States". No country list is published. The Partners API rejects missions in FAA-protected airspace. Per-country density and lead times are not published.

licensing.summary: General Terms and Conditions (dated October 8, 2025): Zeitview owns its services and "related technology and deliverables", and the customer acquires no IP in them (8.1). The customer owns its Confidential Information and Customer Data, defined as data about the customer (2.3, 8.2). Services are for the customer's "own internal or personal purposes" (5.1). The customer grants Zeitview a perpetual, worldwide, sublicensable licence to Customer Data to provide services, optimise them and create anonymised data sets (8.3). Zeitview may use service data, including AI-generated annotations and anonymised data sets, to improve and develop its services, and may disclose it in aggregate or de-identified form (8.6). Separately, the Site Terms of Service (s.7) give Zeitview a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence, including the right to sell, over content submitted to the Site. The commercial real estate page instead says "All drone aerial photography is yours to own and use as you like". Neither document mentions AI or model training rights for the buyer, or resale.

human.method: "Certified pilots" capture the data. Real estate pilots are "vetted and tested", and Zeitview says it is FAA-permitted for commercial flight and insured at every job site. Partners API missions record pilot_accepted, pilot_arrived and pilot_departed timestamps.
human.unknown: How pilot identity and certification are checked, and whether the delivered files were captured by that pilot. Customers may also upload their own data.

application.unknown: No claim that capture goes through a controlled or attested app. The Partners API lets some integrations use a third-party flight app and upload tool, and nothing says imagery cannot be replaced before upload.

camera.unknown: Not a signed capture, so none (STANDARD §3). What is stated: RGB, thermal, lidar and methane sensors on drones, fixed-wing aircraft and robotic crawlers. Sensor output is not signed or tamper-evident, and there is no C2PA support. Nothing rules out edited images or photos of a screen.

time.method: Each image from the Partners API carries a taken_at timestamp, and missions carry status timestamps. Each methane detection includes a timestamp.
time.unknown: The source of taken_at (likely camera metadata) is not documented, and it is not signed or checked against an independent clock.

location.method: Data is geotagged to the asset or component. Each image from the Partners API carries GPS latitude, longitude and altitude. Methane detections include a precise GPS location.
location.unknown: Positional accuracy, where the geotag comes from, and resistance to GPS spoofing or substituted files are not documented.

content.method: AI models flag anomalies, then certified analysts or domain experts review and validate each finding before delivery
content.unknown: Review error rates are not published, and nothing says a fabricated or staged capture would be caught. The terms say Zeitview "does not review the information collected during performance" of its services (6.5).

corroboration.unknown: Nothing independent confirms a capture. Repeat surveys and the portfolio view are Zeitview's own data. The FAQ calls its methane measurement EPA-approved, but Zeitview is not named on EPA's alternative test methods page.

api.notes: The Zeitview Partners API (formerly the DroneBase API) creates missions in bulk, server to server. The docs list only https://sandbox-api.dronebase.com (labelled 'production' in the Apiary metadata), which does not resolve. api.dronebase.com redirects (308) to sake.production.zeitview.com; that host is not documented and was not called. Download URLs are signed and time-limited since May 1, 2026. The marketing pages say Asset Insights is "built as an API", but no public docs for it were found. Real estate packages can also be ordered in the web Client Dashboard (clients.zeitview.com).

payment.notes: Enterprise terms: Zeitview invoices by email, payment is due within 30 days by electronic transfer in USD, and orders are subject to credit approval. Payment methods for online real estate orders are not stated on public pages.

requester.checks: All orders are subject to approval by Zeitview, including credit approval (terms 1.7). Users must be 18 or older and not barred by US sanctions (OFAC), and must provide payment information (Terms of Service 3). Missions in FAA-protected airspace are rejected (Partners API).
requester.unknown: Whether Zeitview checks the requester's authority over the property, or the purpose of a capture, is not documented.
